Drugs for a common eye condition could one day be used to treat certain aggressive cancers, including breast cancer, melanoma and a type of blood cancer.

Scientists at The Institute for Cancer Research found these cancers rely on the same molecule to become aggressive and spread

Their study found existing drugs which block the molecule and are currently used to treat patients with glaucoma could be repurposed to help fight cancer. It also identified certain markers which could determine which patients may respond well to the drugs.

Experts said that the study “lays the foundations” for identifying suitable patients, and repurposing drugs which have already proven to be safe could mean they reach patients faster.

Lead author Victoria Sanz Moreno, professor of cancer cell and metastasis biology, said: “Some cancers are particularly aggressive, and once they spread they become very hard to treat.

“Catching these aggressive cancers and preventing their ability to move around the body is really crucial to our mission to keep more people living well with cancer.

“Our research has identified a shared weakness of aggressive cancer cells that could be targeted across many cancer types, wherever they originate in the body.

open image in gallery Scientists confirmed their findings in aggressive cancers such as breast cancer ( Getty/iStock )

“We confirmed our findings in aggressive cancers such as breast cancer, melanoma, and a type of blood cancer called acute myeloid leukaemia, but we believe this molecular fingerprint of cancer cells likely to die after treatment applies to many more cancer types.

“It’s reassuring to know that a treatment already exists – a drug currently being used safely in some patients could be adapted to treat these cancers.”

Researchers set out to find markers that could be used to identify which cancers would respond well to drugs that block a molecule called ROCK, also known as Rho kinase.

When cancer cells spread around the body, they cause advanced disease that is hard to treat, and these aggressive cells rely on ROCK.

The molecule keeps the scaffolding of cells tense, making the cells contract and become round, which generates force for the cancer cells to squeeze through tissue.

The study, published in the journal iScience, saw researchers look for markers that could be used to identify which cancers would respond well to drugs that block ROCK – which are already in use to treat glaucoma.

The team, working in the Breast Cancer Now Toby Robins Research Centre at the ICR, looked at information from a drug sensitivity database to identify which types of cancer cells responded to ROCK inhibitors.

Researchers found that breast cancer cells that responded to ROCK inhibitors had a particular gene that was not working properly, called E-Cadherin.

In melanoma, the database showed that cells that respond to ROCK inhibitors tended to have a more rounded shape and high activity of a signalling pathway called NFKB.

And acute myeloid leukaemia cells that responded well to ROCK had a specific subset of gene alterations.

The findings were then turned into lab experiments on tumour samples and studies in mice.

open image in gallery The study found that patients who may respond well to the drugs can be identified with certain markers ( Getty/iStock )

The researchers hope that in the future a biopsy of a patient’s cancer showing these markers could indicate whether ROCK inhibitors would work well for the patient.

Dr Simon Vincent, chief scientific officer at Breast Cancer Now, said: “With around 11,500 women tragically dying from breast cancer every year in the UK, research like this is vital to finding more effective treatment options.

“This study helps to lay the foundation for understanding who among those with certain cancers, including breast cancer, might benefit most from existing drugs. Finding new uses for existing treatments, which we know people can safely take, is easier and faster than developing new cancer drugs from scratch.

“It’s encouraging that these drugs may be especially effective in targeting cancer cells that are more likely to spread and resist treatment.

“While this research is still at an early stage and clinical trials are needed, it’s an important step towards more personalised breast cancer treatments in the future.”

First author of the study, Jaume Barcelo, postdoctoral research fellow at The Institute of Cancer Research, London, now based at the Barts Cancer Institute at Queen Mary University of London, added: “Our study has identified a specific pattern of features that is consistent across many cancer types, and that can be used to match the right patients to this treatment.

“The next stage for this research will be to test how these drugs that inhibit ROCK work in combination with other treatments, to maximise the benefit for patients.

“As ROCK inhibitors are already approved to treat glaucoma, I hope that our findings can be used to progress the drugs into clinical trials to treat cancer in the near future.”

Susanna Daniels, chief executive officer of the charity Melanoma Focus, said: “Despite major advances in melanoma treatment over the past decade, too many people still die from the disease each year, and not every patient responds to the treatments currently available.

“Every new discovery improves our understanding of how melanoma grows and survives, bringing us closer to treatments that are more effective, more targeted and have the potential to improve survival.

“While these findings are still at an early stage and will need to be tested in clinical trials, they offer an encouraging direction for future melanoma research and the development of more personalised treatments.”

This summer is expected to see more top A-level grades awarded than in any year outside the pandemic-affected period, a trend largely attributed to the increasing popularity of mathematics and other quantitative subjects.

An education expert has predicted a small rise in the percentage of UK A-level entries achieving an A* or A grade, with boys anticipated to edge further ahead in A* grades.

Professor Alan Smithers, director of the Centre for Education and Employment Research at the University of Buckingham, stated his belief that the increases in top grades awarded over the past two years could indicate a new trend is emerging.

In 2025, a total of 28.3% of entries were awarded either an A or A*, up from 27.8% in 2024, 27.2% in 2023 and above 25.4% in 2019.

open image in gallery An education expert has predicted a small rise in the percentage of UK A-level entries achieving an A* or A grade this year ( Liam McBurney/PA )

Last year saw the highest proportion on record outside the pandemic-affected years of 2020-22 when the figure peaked at 44.8% in 2021.

Ahead of A-level results day, Professor Smithers has highlighted a "big swing" in recent years towards A-level subjects such as maths and economics.

In a new report, he noted these are "much higher yielders" of top grades, driven by job prospects that "have become more influential".

He added that mathematics in particular will significantly affect overall results.

Provisional data for England confirms maths as the most popular A-level choice this year – its 13th consecutive year at the top.

Economics has also entered the top five for the first time since Ofqual began publishing figures in 2014.

“These subjects are among the highest awarders of A* and A*/A grades,” Prof Smithers said.

“This points to a further rise in top grades.

“We cannot be sure, but it is my best guess.”

He added: “Job prospects look to have had more influence on A-level choices.

“Not surprising considering the difficulties young people are encountering.”

Last year, boys took a lead over girls in the top grades for the first time since 2018.

The proportion of boys’ entries awarded A or A* was 28.4%, 0.2 percentage points higher than the equivalent figure for girls’ entries (28.2%).

The proportion of boys’ entries awarded A* was 9.9%, 0.8 points higher than girls (9.1%).

Boys led girls at A* from 2012 through to 2019, before girls moved in front during the pandemic-affected years of 2020-22, after which boys reclaimed a lead in 2023.

Prof Smithers said boys and girls choose different subjects, with “many more” boys than girls taking A-level maths last year.

He suggested the continued growth of quantitative subjects “points to boys increasing their lead at A*” but the increase in provisional entries for psychology, biology and history will likely see girls’ percentage of the very top grade rise alongside.

He said the “advantage could go either way” for the combined A* and A grades.

open image in gallery Provisional data for England confirms maths as the most popular A-level choice this year – its 13th consecutive year at the top ( PA )

The professor also predicted Northern Ireland will continue to have the best results compared with England and Wales.

“In short, we could see in the 2026 results the small rises in top grades in the years since exams fully resumed continuing,” he concluded.

“The gap between boys and girls at A* is also likely to widen by a tenth of a percentage point or two. This would have occurred mainly as a result of increases in the entries to maths and other quantitative subjects.

“But none of this is set in stone. Although it is what the trends and provisional entries logically suggest, the grades awarded can be raised or lowered by adjusting their thresholds.

“The government, regulators, and exam boards may have their reasons for wanting the grades to remain the same or even fall, and they have the power to make this happen.”

A Department for Education spokesperson said: “Ahead of results day, young people and parents can be confident that their exam grades will be a true reflection of their abilities. This report is entirely speculative, as relevant data has not yet been released.

“Whatever young people want to do after they get their results, they should be proud of their efforts throughout their studies, and take the time to consider the full range of options available to them.

“Through our reforms to put technical and academic education on an equal footing, this Government will make sure every young person, wherever they live, is given the opportunity to choose the path that’s right for them.”

When is A-level results day 2026?

A-level results day is on Thursday, August 13.

Last year, top A-level grades rose to reach a record high outside of the Covid years, while a record number of students were accepted onto UK degree courses.

Ucas figures showed that, for 18-year-olds in the UK, 255,130 applicants were accepted onto university or college courses – up 4.7 per cent on 2024.

Overall, 82 per cent of UK 18-year-old applicants awaiting a decision on results day secured their first choice – which was the same proportion as the year before.

President Donald Trump has reportedly nominated an author of Project 2025 to serve as a watchdog for the Interior Department.

Dennis Kirk, a former official in the White House Office of Personnel Management and one of the authors of the far-right Project 2025 document to serve as the Interior Department's inspector general, according to The Hill.

Kirk previously served as a watchdog within the intelligence community last year, according to The Washington Post.

House Natural Resources ranking member Congressman Jared Huffman criticized the appointment, calling him "fraudulent."

"Dennis Kirk is a fake and fraudulent watchdog," Huffman said in a statement. "Everyone should have their eyes wide open. Each and every thing this political puppet does will be in the service of Donald [Trump]."

President Donald Trump has reportedly nominated one of the authors of Project 2025, Dennis Kirk, to serve as a watchdog for the Interior Department ( AP )

He continued, criticizing Kirk's role in the Project 2025 document.

"This man helped write the Project 2025 playbook for seizing control of the federal workforce," he said. "Now he sits inside the office charged with rooting out corruption at Interior, the department that manages our national parks, public lands, Tribal programs, and now, under Trump, gold-slathered statues and a botched Reflecting Pool renovation.”

The Interior Department has been at odds with the Trump administration over the president's various Washington, D.C. projects like his ballroom at the White House and his decision to drain and close the Reflecting Pool near the Lincoln Memorial.

The latter has become an especially raw point of contention within the federal government, as reports have shown that the contractors used to work on the pool were hired through an unusual no-bid process.

The current head of the Interior Department Inspector General's office is Caryl Brzymialkiewicz, who replaced Mark Greenblatt in January 2025 after he was fired when Trump returned to office.

He posted a statement to his website this week warning that Kirk's placement should "concern anyone who values independent government oversight."

“Placing someone with that background inside an inspector general’s office raises serious questions about the independence of one of the federal government’s most important accountability institutions,” Greenblatt said.

The Independent has requested comment from the White House.

News.title: Gomes scores for Aston Villa in defeat by Bayern Munich in Hong Kong
News.content:
Aston Villa 1 Bayern Munich 2

Aston Villa’s tour of the Far East ended in defeat as they lost 2-1 to German champions Bayern Munich in a pre-season friendly at the Kai Tak Sports Park in Hong Kong on Friday.

Bayern took the lead inside the final 10 minutes of the first half, with defender Kim Min-jae heading in from Tom Bischof’s sublime free-kick. Villa goalkeeper Marco Bizot made a string of saves in the second half to keep Bayern’s lead at one goal until former Liverpool forward Luis Díaz smashed in Bayern’s second off the underside of the bar.

Just as the game appeared to be out of reach for Aston Villa, who had struggled to create much going forward for most of the game, Unai Emery’s side showed some life late on. Summer signing João Gomes’s goal from the edge of the box gave them hope before Tammy Abraham nearly brought them back onto level terms, only to be denied by a fine save from 40-year-old Manuel Neuer.

Aston Villa are next in action in six days’ time when they take on Paris St-Germain in the Uefa Super Cup before kicking off their Premier League campaign at Brighton. Bayern have one more friendly to come against RB Leipzig before the DFL-Supercup against Borussia Dortmund. They then kick off the defence of their Bundesliga crown against Stuttgart at home on August 28.

News.title: Suspected Ebola case on packed Congo river boat sparks testing rush
News.content:
Congolese health authorities have intercepted and detained a river boat on its way to the capital after a suspected Ebola case onboard.

Authorities have set up a mobile clinic to test more than 200 passengers after one of them disembarked and died earlier on the voyage.

The boat travelling from the northeastern commercial hub of Kisangani was stopped and held in Maluku, some 40 miles from Kinshasa.

Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) is dealing with its worst ever outbreak of the viral haemorrhagic fever, which has seen nearly 4,000 cases and killed around 1,801 people according to the latest government figures.

Samuel Roger Kamba, the health minister, said a 32-year-old man had disembarked in Pimu in Mongala province, before developing ‌suspected Ebola symptoms and dying.

“We did not say it was Ebola. We said there was a suspected case for which we are being cautious,” the health minister told a press conference, according to MediaCongo, a local news site.

He said there had been no other reports of deaths among travellers.

The virus has so far spread to five provinces, though more than 90 per cent of cases have been recorded in the north eastern Ituri region.

News.title: The best luxury hotels in the Cotswolds
News.content:
From gracious old farmsteads and magnificent manor houses to an ancient coaching inn creaking with Tudor character, the top luxury hotels in the Cotswolds combine a wonderful sense of history with contemporary style and outstanding modern British cuisine. Whether near picturesque Broadway in the north of the region or close to Bath in the south, location is a key attribute to them all: some offer serene escapes in acres of their own rolling parkland; others sit amid superb gardens; and several take over classic honey-stone villages that look as if they have been beamed in from a halcyon era of the past.

They all excel in providing creature comforts, whether crackling fires by kick-back sofas, canopy beds with soft throws, or suites with terraces and hot tubs. Facilities are top-notch too, ranging from beautiful bars and quiet terraces to blissful spas with inviting pools and even an opportunity for equine adventures. Read on to discover our pick of the best luxury hotels in the Cotswolds.

News.title: El Nino could cause explosion of rabid seals, animal health experts warn
News.content:
This year’s El Nino weather event risks propelling an outbreak of rabid seals around the world, the world’s animal health body has warned.

Countries in South America and Australasia are being urged to look for signs the deadly infectious disease has reached their waters, only two years after it was first confirmed in South Africa.

The 2024 discovery of rabies in South Africa’s Cape fur seals was the first significant outbreak ever found in marine mammals and has been described as a “significant shift in rabies ecology”.

More than 100 cases have been confirmed in South Africa and Namibia since then, raising fears that aggressive rabid seals could infect humans, pets and other wildlife.

Changing patterns in fish stocks caused by the El Nino phenomenon now potentially risk widening the spread, as uninfected seal populations migrate for food and come into contact with rabid colleagues.

Scientists believe warming sea temperatures off Antarctica could send seal populations northwards into Southern African waters, where they could be exposed to rabies.

They could then return to their home waters, taking the virus with them and infecting other seal populations.

News.title: ​Arteta’s ‘dynasty’ dream collides with Arsenal’s harsh reality
News.content:
Arsenal 1 Real Betis 3

Mikel Arteta says he wants to create a “dynasty” at Arsenal as he threw down the gauntlet to his players to retain their Premier League title and reach a “different level”.

Arsenal are on the verge of completing a £75m deal for Brazil midfielder Bruno Guimãraes from Newcastle and have not given up hope of landing Real Madrid winger Vinícius Júnior, who has been offered an improved contract by the Spanish giants.

The Premier League champions slumped to a 3-1 defeat to Real Betis in Dublin on Wednesday night, when they paid the price for individual errors and a lethargic, sloppy defensive display.

But that did little to quell Arteta’s ambitions for the new season. “I’m even more excited [about this season], and we’re going to go and attack every possible title because that’s the ambition that we have,” he said.

“We know that we have the ability. We will go from a strength to a strength as well, whether it’s with the players that we have to take them to a different level, and with the market that is still open to recruit as well, so we are very optimistic about it.

“All the work that we’ve done – that I’ve done through the summer – is to understand what we need to do to win again and to create a dynasty in this football club. That’s the aim.”

Despite Arteta’s bullishness, he conceded Arsenal would have to be a lot better than they were against Betis. When asked about the mood in the dressing room, he said: “Very upset, given a hard time. They are fuming, but this is good. That’s what we need.”

Telegraph Sport analyses some of the talking points from a disappointing evening at the Aviva Stadium.

No Saliba a concern

The importance of goalkeeper David Raya and centre-backs William Saliba and Gabriel Magalhães to Arsenal hardly needs overstating. Their title success was built on the foundations provided by that triumvirate at the back.

Raya has yet to report back from holiday after Spain’s World Cup triumph and Saliba is facing an extended spell on the sidelines with a back injury. Gabriel did appear for the second half but, watching this, Arteta is unlikely to have been dissuaded from the belief he needs another top defender to compensate for the loss of Saliba.

It may have been only Arsenal’s second game of pre-season, so a degree of legginess was understandable.

But the ease with which they were cut open and overloaded by the Spanish side, and the volume of individual errors, did not sit comfortably with Arteta with just over a fortnight until they kick off their title defence at home to newly promoted Coventry City.

Only once in 63 matches last season did Arsenal concede three goals in a single game but they were fortunate Betis did not score more. “In the first half there are two different things: to play well and to compete,” said Arteta, who saw his side trail 3-1 at the interval.

News.title: Ebola outbreak outpacing containment effort, WHO chief warns
News.content:
Caused by the rare Bundibugyo strain of Ebola, for which there are no vaccines or treatments, it has been extremely difficult to contain, according to experts on the ground.

“The outbreak is spreading faster than our scale-up of the response, with new cases doubling in some hotspots over the past week alone,” Dr Tedros said on X.

Part of the difficulty is that the virus was circulating undetected for weeks before the outbreak was formally declared in mid-May, leaving health officials even now racing to catch up with the spread.

Prof Placide Mbala, director of research, clinical trials and innovation at Africa CDC, told the Telegraph: “It’s mostly the fact we arrived a bit late. It took us some time before we detected this virus outbreak. And when we detected the outbreak, we already had a total of I can say more than 200 suspected cases. It’s been difficult to catch up. That’s where we are.”

While the DRC has a wealth of experience in tackling haemorrhagic fever outbreaks, the effects of that initial delay are still being felt.

Prof Mbala said: “We have some experience dealing with the cases, the labs, the communication, the infection prevention and control.

“We have some experience... But my observation is that we were very slow, and it’s why we’re in this situation.

“We are slow detecting the people, slow responding, we are slow deploying people, we are slow to recruit the community healthcare workers to improve contact tracing, we are slow to deploy the safe burials.”

DRC’s largest outbreak had previously been from 2018 to 2020, when 3,481 cases were recorded.

The West Africa outbreak recorded 28,616 cases and 11,310 deaths according to the WHO.

Prof Mbala said insecurity was also severely hampering attempts to curb the virus. The outbreak epicentre is in Ituri province, which has been wracked by ethnic strife for decades and is also home to militias competing to control mining.

He said: “There are many, many mining groups controlling most of the mining places. We have a big issue with those places, because they are places where the response team cannot go.”

Medics and aid workers have also been undermined by violent public distrust of their efforts.

Locals in the area have either doubted the existence of the virus, or have accused health teams of deliberately spreading the infection, or somehow benefiting from it.

More than a dozen health facilities have been set alight and several health workers have been killed.

Prof Mbala said: “The local people, they also sometimes are very upset, because they believe that it’s a kind of a business, and people who are coming here, they are getting a lot of money, [so] don’t want this disease to stop.”

He said he hoped that immunity was starting to rise in some areas and this would start to curb transmission.

However there was also a risk that people fleeing the outbreak would spread the virus further afield.

He said: “The second scenario is the fact we are seeing people moving from the affected area to new areas, to run away from the response team because they do not want to go to the treatment centre.

“And in complicity with their family members living in other areas, they are now the ones who are spreading the disease to new areas

“So we’ll see new places affected because people are moving around from the affected zone to the non-affected zone.”

Protect yourself and your family by learning more about Global Health Security

News.title: Mykhailo Mudryk returns as Chelsea slip to Juventus defeat
News.content:
Chelsea 0 Juventus 1

Mykhailo Mudryk made his first Chelsea appearance since November 2024 as Xabi Alonso’s team succumbed to their second pre-season defeat.

Mudryk replaced Nicolas Jackson in the 82nd minute against Juventus, marking his return to competitive football after a long doping ban that was resolved this week thanks to changes in Wada regulations.

There were a couple of crosses delivered from the left flank by the Ukrainian winger, who could yet leave Chelsea on loan or on a permanent basis before the close of the transfer window.

Juventus were the victors though, thanks to a sumptuous 68th-minute goal by Kosovo winger Edon Zhegrova.

Alonso had 21 players on his bench, and made 12 second-half substitutions.

Levi Colwill and Cole Palmer featured in the defeat by 10-man Spurs on Saturday, but sat this game out as they continue to build fitness. Danny Welbeck did start though, reunited with former Brighton team-mate Joao Pedro up top.

Chelsea scored just one goal against Spurs and Juventus, but the thrust provided by right-back Marco Palestra in tandem with first Geovany Quenda and then Estevao was a bright spot for Alonso.

Chelsea continue their pre-season against AC Milan on Saturday, before they host Real Sociedad at Stamford Bridge on August 15.

They begin their Premier League campaign at Fulham in the Monday night slot on the opening weekend.

News.title: The underground lab where ‘princess mosquitoes’ are treated like royalty
News.content:
Beneath the grand Art Deco headquarters of the London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine lies a vast labyrinth inhabited by weird and wonderful creatures.

In this maze of subterranean labs, store rooms and corridors live colonies of disease-bearing insects and arachnids from all over the world, from bed bugs, sand flies and microscopic dust mites to the so-called kissing bugs that spread Chagas disease – a sinister condition that can cause its victims to drop dead of heart failure without warning, albeit decades after the first (silent) infection.

Behind a series of doors, contained in stacks of mesh boxes, you can even find the flies that spread trachoma, the Dickensian eye disease that is still a leading cause of blindness around the world. But be warned: entering the room is not for the faint of heart – the flies feed on human excrement and the smell is impossible to forget.

There are also many varieties of mosquito, including several species of the Anopheles genus that spread malaria, Culex and Aedes mosquitoes that are also vectors for human and animal diseases, and even Toxorhynchites, perhaps better known as the elephant mosquito, a friendly giant which doesn’t bite people but preys on other mosquitoes.

These animals have been studied intensely since the insectaries were established in the building’s vaults in the 1960s, underpinning many breakthroughs in the control, surveillance, and understanding of vector-borne diseases in the developing world.

LSHTM researchers are now looking closer to home. They have established the UK’s first laboratory colony of Aedes vexans mosquitoes, a species native to the British isles, to study whether they could harbour diseases like West Nile virus, Rift Valley fever, Zika or Japanese encephalitis.

Sports.title: Gianni Infantino’s ‘lover paid off with six-figure sum by Uefa while he ran football body’
Sports.content:
GI WHIZ Gianni Infantino’s ‘lover paid off with six-figure sum by Uefa while he ran football body’

UEFA paid off a six-figure sum to an alleged mistress of Gianni Infantino while he was its general secretary, it has been reported.

The woman received the money after their supposed relationship with the 56-year-old – while he was a top official at European football’s governing body, according to The Telegraph.



She is also alleged to have been promoted by the under-fire Fifa boss during their relationship.

Senior figures at Uefa claim the married dad-of-four ensured the woman left with the pay-off.



And after she left, the football body is understood to have paid for her to do an MBA at a business school.

In a statement on Friday night, Uefa admitted that a payment had been made and that it was aware of the allegations the woman was in a relationship with Infantino.



It said it had since “tightened” its regulations to “reflect those found in a modern, high-profile organisation”.

Infantino joined Uefa in 2000 and spent 16 years there before leaving to become Fifa president in February 2016.



A Fifa spokesperson said: ““Fifa president Gianni Infantino strongly denies these allegations, and they are categorically untrue.

“Any insinuation of inappropriate conduct or violation of statutes or regulations is defamatory.

“No employee at Uefa and Fifa has ever raised a complaint regarding Mr Infantino’s behaviour because there never was an incident where he was involved.

“All company actions related to employees, including any departure and severance packages, have always been approved by the appropriate directors in accordance with all applicable regulations.”

The alleged use of Uefa funds happened while Infantino was its general secretary, sources claimed and the woman was allegedly promoted to a management position while the relationship was taking place.



Uefa’s then president Michel Platini is said to have challenged him over the alleged affair and it was agreed she would leave with a pay-off.

As well as the pay-off it also forked out for the woman to take an MBA course at a business school which charged around £45,000 per year in fees, as part of the deal.

Sources also claimed that when the woman left, Infantino allegedly used his connections to secure a new lucrative post for the woman in a similar field.

A spokesman for Uefa said: “We are aware of the allegations and can confirm a departure payment was made to the individual in question, coupled with the payment of fees for an MBA course at a local business school.

“The payment was in line with the regulations that existed for departing staff at the time.



“Such regulations have been tightened since 2016 and the current staff regulations – which apply to all Uefa employees at whatever level – reflect those found in a modern, high-profile organisation.”

Infantino, it is claimed, promoted his alleged lover, handing her a 30 per cent pay rise and a salary of around £147,000.

Her rapid rise is said to have raised eyebrows among colleagues and concerns he could be abusing his position to advance her.

During his time at Uefa he oversaw a footballing empire which had revenues of around £1.2billion and covered the game in 53 countries.

Infantion met his wife Leena Al Ashqar when she was working for the Lebanese Football Federatoin.



The pair married in 2001 and have four children.

It is not known if his wife was aware of the alleged relationship.

Matters are said to have come to a head when Platini learned about it, reports say.

A well-placed source told The Telegraph: “He made a huge mistake and it almost cost him his career.

“People [within Uefa] were telling Platini, ‘You have to fire him’.”



Another added: “Platini challenged Gianni, saying something like ‘she or you?’ and Gianni said, ‘She will leave’, and she left.”

Sources also claimed that Platini told Infantino that either he or the woman would have to leave.

The revelations come just a week after the collapse of Infantino’s financing scheme, which he announced nine days after the end of the World Cup.

The plan would have resulted in a group of investors controlling the commercial interests of Fifa’s top competitions for both men and women.

Uefa revolted against the plan, voting 55-0 to boycott the next World Cup, a move which helped defeat the plan.



It accused Fifa of attempting to trade away football’s soul.

The Concacaf nations in North and Central America then followed Uefa’s lead and condemned the plan.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Fifa is a non-profit organisation which means in theory money made from the competition is ploughed back into football.

Infantino is said to have told his inner circle he has no plans to quit, having met senior staff in Morocco this week and he has allegedly appealed to US President Donald Trump for support.

Sports.title: Sky Sports legend Chris Kamara reveals cancer scare and urges men to get tested as he prepares for Great North Run
Sports.content:
CHRIS KAMARA revealed he had a prostate cancer scare.

And now he is urging men to bury their pride and embarrassment and get tested.



The Sky Sports legend, 68, has been supporting Prostate Cancer UK’s work for a decade, including ten charity walks with pal Jeff Stelling.

But a health scare after a routine blood test in 2024 sparked alarm bells for the former Swindon and Brentford midfielder – before he was given good news that it was not cancer.



Kammy told the Mirror: “Any man would feel scared about the prospect of getting prostate cancer.

“I’ve been working with the charity for more than a decade, so I know that early diagnosis is absolutely key.

“A routine test I had two years ago flagged up a slightly PSA level raised level.

“That was a scary thing to hear, but thankfully it turned out I didn’t have prostate cancer. After consistent monitoring, my levels remain the same.

“As men, it’s so important we look after ourselves and keep an eye on any changes.

“I do get up in the night to pee more now. But that’s a symptom of other conditions too, so check with your GP.



What is prostate cancer? Prostate cancer affects a small, walnut shaped gland that sits underneath the bladder and surrounds the urethra – the tube carrying pee outside the body. It usually grows bigger as you get older. The prostate’s main job is to help make semen – the fluid that carries sperm. Most men with early prostate cancer don’t have any signs or symptoms – that’s why it’s important to know about your risk. Possible symptoms include: Difficulty starting to urinate or emptying your bladder

A weak flow when you urinate

A feeling that your bladder hasn’t emptied properly

Dribbling urine after you finish urinating

Needing to urinate more often than usual, especially at night

A sudden need to urinate – you may sometimes leak urine before you get to the toilet If you do notice changes in the way you urinate, this is more likely to be a sign of an enlarged prostate, which is very common and non-cancerous. But it’s still a good idea to get it checked out. In the UK, about one in eight men will be diagnosed with prostate cancer in their lifetime. Some factors may mean you’re more likely to get it. This includes: Getting older – it mainly affects men aged 50 or over

Having a family history of prostate cancer

Being Black If you have any of these risk factors or if you have any symptoms, speak to your GP. They can talk to you about your risk, and about the tests that are used to diagnose prostate cancer. Source: Prostate Cancer UK

“And I know none of us likes going to the doctor about ‘problems below the belt’ – but it’s a mountain you have to climb, so just do it.

“Doing the walks alongside my great mate Jeff and meeting so many affected by prostate cancer, or who were marching in honour of loved ones they had lost, really brought it home to me.

“Those stories are heartbreaking and inspirational at the same time, and having that knowledge of the disease certainly helped me deal with my scare.

“I want to raise as much awareness as I can, particularly for black men, who are at double the risk.



“Prostate Cancer UK have a brilliant risk checker on their website. It takes 30 seconds and may just save your life.

“The problem with prostate checking, it’s your genitals, and you feel embarrassed when you shouldn’t be.

“These doctors and nurses have seen it all before. Get over that problem and go and get yourself checked.”

Rather than climbing a mountain, as he did with Kilimanjaro in 2012, Kamara is preparing to run a half-marathon.

He is set to take on the 13.1-mile challenge at next month’s Great North Run in Newcastle to raise more money for Prostate Cancer UK.



Fittingly, Kammy is doing it alongside son Jack and fellow broadcaster Ben Shephard, who have both supported him through his other major health battle.

Kamara was diagnosed with speech apraxia due to an underactive thyroid – causing him to lose his ability to speak as usual and feeling like a “fraud”.

After various treatments and forms of recovery, Kamara has got the confidence to be back on TV – in large part thanks to Shephard, to whom Kamara went public with his condition in a Good Morning Britain interview in 2023.

Kamara – who is hoping to finish in three hours – added: “Ben has been amazing. He’s part of the reason I came back to do TV.

“He convinced me to do that GMB interview with him. I’m back partly down to his help and encouragement.



“I spent a couple of years feeling sorry for myself and thinking, ‘This is totally beyond me to ever consider getting back to walking, never mind jogging.’

“I wanted to give myself a real challenge to try and get back to somewhere near the person I was.

“I’m helping a lot of charities these days. I thought, ‘What would be the perfect challenge for me?’ To do a half marathon and make it to the finish line with all my problems.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“Going down stairs I’m not so good, so going down hills is going to be a massive challenge.

“But Ben and my son Jack will guide me through that. They will make sure I get it done.”

Sports.title: Declan Rice leads kind wishes after Arsenal starlet’s heartbreaking post as he confirms ruptured ACL in Real Betis loss
Sports.content:
ARSENAL starlet Louie Copley took to social media to confirm that he has ruptured his ACL.

And Declan Rice was among a slew of Gunners stars to leave a supportive comment under Copley’s Instagram post.



Arsenal academy graduate Copley, 19, replaced Ben White as a half-time substitute as his side took on Real Betis in Dublin on Wednesday.

He was forced off just nine minutes later, however, after horribly twisting his knee – leaving fans fearing the worst.



After the game, boss Mikel Arteta gave a gloomy update, saying: “Well, probably we’re going to have it tomorrow. It doesn’t look good, the mechanism is not too positive, the symptoms that he already has either.

“So let’s hope that tomorrow the news is better.”

Later confirming his unfortunate news, Copley wrote on Instagram, alongside a snap of himself in agony: “Words can’t describe how I’m feeling right now, to making my pre season debut for the team I’ve grown up supporting to finding out I’ve ruptured my ACL.

“The road ahead won’t be easy but I’ll give everything to come back stronger and better”.

Rice commented with a heart emoji, as did fellow Arsenal stars White, Max Dowman and Myles Lewis-Skelly – in addition to other academy players too.

Jurrien Timber left a praying emoji, while Charles Sagoe Jr, currently on loan at Swedish side Kalmar, added: “Speedy recovery Lou, get well soon!!!”



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

Full-back Copley has established himself as one of the Arsenal academy’s brightest talents in recent years.

The Essex-born starlet joined Crawley Town on loan in January, playing nine times during the second half of last term in his first taste of senior men’s football.

With Copley forced off, lacklustre Arsenal went on to lose 3-1 to Real Betis.

The Gunners will be back in action on Sunday as they host Borussia Dortmund in the Emirates Cup.

Sports.title: Ex-Man Utd ace Nicky Butt has rubbish tip ban lifted — thanks to The Sun
Sports.content:
EX-Manchester United ace Nicky Butt has had his rubbish tip ban lifted — thanks to The Sun.

We told how the “raging” former midfielder, 51, rowed with staff after being told his Range Rover was deemed a commercial vehicle as the seats were down.



But bosses contacted us to say they do not have a policy stating that car seat positions change a vehicle’s classification.

They say residents are asked at the gate what they have brought so staff can direct them to the right container.



Butt was believed to have visited the Woodhouse Lane Recycling Centre in Altrincham.

Recycle for Greater Manchester said: “We’re sorry to hear about Nicky’s experience.



“But would like to reassure him that he’s still very welcome to use any of the 19 recycling centres.”

Former England ace Butt told The Good, The Bad & The Football podcast that he dumped his “smelly bags” at the centre near his home in Cheshire despite being chased by an attendant with a walkie-talkie.

The Class of 92 hero said: “I thought, well, I’m there now, I’m gonna go for it.

“So I’ve got up the ramp, I see this bloke getting up…trying to chase me up the hill, but he’s got his walkie-talkie out.



“So I’ve literally got up the top, throw all the bags out, and I’m going back down the hill, and he’s going mad at me.

“Anyway, I’m banned from the tip.”

Sports.title: Arsenal ready to hijack Liverpool’s £130million Bradley Barcola transfer from PSG after missing out on Vinicius Jr
Sports.content:
ARSENAL could look to hijack Liverpool’s swoop for Bradley Barcola after missing out on Vinicius Jr.

The Gunners had been plotting a blockbuster move for the Real Madrid winger, only for him to pen a new six-year deal at the Bernabeu.



Arsenal chiefs were committed to completing a big-money transfer for the Brazilian, who had one year remaining on his previous contract.

But Vinicius Jr instead opted to sign a new £480,000-a-week extension to stay put, ruling the Gunners out of the race.



Mikel Arteta‘s side remain desperate to land a new left winger, particularly after letting Leandro Trossard join Besiktas.

According to the Independent, Barcola is an “attractive option” for the Gunners.

But they will have to play “catch up” to Liverpool, who have already been negotiating personal terms.

The Reds are eager to land the Paris Saint-Germain winger as they seek a new star winger following Mo Salah’s departure.

Andoni Iraola‘s side have identified Barcola as a key target and have been working on the transfer for weeks.

But PSG’s asking price remains a stumbling block for all interested suitors, with Luis Enrique‘s men said to be demanding around £130million.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

And, according to French outlet Canal Plus, the Reds have told PSG they do not have the means to match their sky-high asking price.

That could now leave the door open for the Gunners to swoop.

Barcola, 23, has played 152 times for the French giants since joining from Lyon in 2023, scoring 39 goals and contributing towards two Champions Leagues and three Ligue 1 titles.

The winger came on as an 83rd minute substitute as PSG beat Arsenal in last season’s Champions League final back in May.



Given PSG’s summer business, he may be about to fall down the pecking order at Parc des Princes.

Following permanent exits for Lee Kang-in, Goncalo Ramos and Randal Kolo Muani, PSG signed French international attacker Maghnes Akliouche on Friday.

They are also keen on Ajax attacker Mika Godts, with Barcelona‘s World Cup final hero Ferran Torres also linked.



In addition to Barcola, Arsenal admire Atletico Madrid star Julian Alvarez.

A deal will be very difficult to accomplish, however, with the former Manchester City forward more likely to stay in LaLiga.

Another option is Everton ace Iliman Ndiaye.

The impressive Toffees star’s future on Merseyside looks uncertain, with Saudi side Al-Hilal also in the mix.

Arsenal gave a lacklustre display as they were beaten 3-1 by Real Betis in Dublin earlier this week.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Quizzed about the mood in the dressing room after the match, Arteta pulled no punches.

The Spaniard said: “They are very upset, given a hard time. They are fuming, but this is good. That’s what we need.”

Sports.title: Arsenal should sign Man Utd star Marcus Rashford after both sides had transfer dreams scuppered by El Clasico giants
Sports.content:
BOTH Marcus Rashford and Arsenal have seen their transfer dreams scuppered by the Clasico giants this summer.

Rashford, 28, was first to suffer when Barcelona snubbed the chance to land him in a £26million permanent deal after last season’s loan at the Nou Camp.



Instead the Catalans decided to splash out £69m on his England team-mate Anthony Gordon from Newcastle.

Arsenal’s own blow arrived on Thursday evening when top transfer target Vinicius Jr ended his flirtation with them by signing a new deal at Real Madrid worth a staggering £480,000 a week.



So, with both the Gunners and Rashford left licking their wounds, is it time they came together to solve each others’ problems?

Rashford is set to reunite with his Manchester United team-mates on Sunday for the first time in 18 months.



The forward is due to travel to Dublin for United’s pre-season training camp after completing his mandatory three-week post-World Cup break.

Rashford has not trained with United since January 2025 after loan spells with Aston Villa and then Barca.

Rashford and Alejandro Garnacho – now on loan at Villa from Chelsea – were part of a five-man ‘bomb squad’ isolated at United’s training ground last summer.

They were ordered by then-boss Ruben Amorim to report for separate training times to the main squad.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

Although Amorim was sacked in January and head coach Michael Carrick has stabilised United, the imminent reunion is still awkward for all parties.

Rashford publicly declared his wish to join Barcelona permanently in May and doubled down on his desire to leave permanently during the World Cup.

But the England international’s £325,000-a-week salary – signed before Sir Jim Ratcliffe’s Old Trafford involvement – has effectively blocked a permanent departure.

On the eve of the World Cup, Rashford posted a brief message on his Instagram page thanking Barcelona, Villa, England and their respective coaches.



There was no mention of United, the club he has been at since the age of seven.

United are also conspicuous by their absence on the bios of Rashford’s social media accounts.

Senior United figures were surprised by Barcelona’s decision not to buy Rashford, which has left them out of options.

United sources have repeatedly stressed they will not let Rashford leave on another season-long loan.

The academy graduate is under contract until 2028.



Rashford’s first appearance back at United could be in their final pre-season friendly against AC Milan, who are now managed by Amorim.

Arsenal wanted Brazilian ace Vinicius as their marquee signing to launch their first Prem title defence in 22 years.

They were led down the garden path and ended it with the sight of the Brazilian scrawling his signature on a new six-year Real contract.

But there are alternative left wingers on the market and Rashford is one of them.

Arsenal have been here before, with Raheem Sterling two years ago.



What appeared a canny deal turned out to be anything but.

Sterling’s slide has been so steep he is currently without a club and was arrested on suspicion of drug-driving in May.

Rashford is a downgrade on Vinicius – well, who isn’t? – but he ticks a lot of boxes for Arsenal: Premier League pedigree, Champions League clout, big-club nous, winners’ medals, international experience and with a point to prove.

Rashford has incentives aplenty to show he is too young for the riches of Turkey or Saudi Arabia.



He has hopes of representing England again at the Euros in 2028 as well as the 2030 World Cup.

When Rashford first steeled himself to leave United, he was insistent on playing for a Champions League club.

That would rule out Tottenham – but don’t bet against them making their own move, with boss Roberto Di Zerbi promising a “bomba” signing.

Spurs nor Rashford’s entourage have dampened speculation.

Tottenham have spent more than £200m on signings already, blowing United out of the water to buy Mateus Fernandes.



If they wanted to, Tottenham could foot the bill for Rashford’s £325,000 weekly salary.

Spurs are also lacking dynamism in attack, with James Maddison, who missed most of last season with an ACL injury and then sustained a minor problem in pre-season and Dejan Kulusevski on his way back from a patella injury he suffered in May 2025.

It suits Rashford to be linked with two of the Premier League’s biggest clubs after Barcelona deemed Gordon a better investment.

Well-placed sources have said a move to Arsenal for Rashford, however fanciful, is not a total non-starter.



Rashford has kept a low profile during his summer break but preparations have been made for his return to Manchester.

The circumstances aren’t ideal but he at least has a club.

Jadon Sancho, another winger now off the books at United, put non-league minnows Flixton on the map by using their training facilities.

Sancho is a free agent, at least.

For Rashford, he is running out of time in a transfer window that closes in less than four weeks.



Even with his steep salary, Rashford is more appealing than Sancho.

He started matches for England at the World Cup, scored in the 4-2 group stage win against Croatia and contributed to a Barcelona title triumph last season.

When push comes to shove, something can happen out of nothing in the final days of a transfer window.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Rashford’s temporary move to Villa materialised with less than 72 hours until it closed.

For now, there will be much to ponder for him and Arsenal as the new season rapidly approaches.

Sports.title: Friends with tyrants, wants royal treatment & World Cup sale bid failed… so is Infantino now too toxic to run football?
Sports.content:
WELCOMING Fifa boss Gianni Infantino to the splendour of the Oval Office, Donald Trump anointed him the “king of soccer”.

Once the target for childhood bullies, the football bureaucrat from humble beginnings was now being feted by the world’s most powerful man.



It was likely a giant ego boost for someone not already lacking in that department — a TV contract at the 2022 World Cup stipulated that Infantino must be pictured onscreen at every game he attended.

Yet, has the floundering Fifa chief’s puffed-up self-importance now chronically clouded his judgement?



Believing he had the backing of enough of football’s power brokers across the globe, he attempted to sell off stakes in the World Cup for £15billion last month.

But he had drastically overplayed his hand. Europe’s governing body Uefa threatened a boycott of the 2030 World Cup.

And despite Infantino’s plans being hastily dropped, the Europeans remain hell-bent on forcing a vote of no confidence in the Fifa president.

Trump’s cringeworthy flattery of Infantino as footballing royalty at the White House in March 2025 was ­perhaps not so ludicrous.

For the most powerful man in the world’s most popular sport enjoys all the gilded trappings of a head of state.

Dripping in wealth — he earns around £4.5million a year in salary and bonuses — Infantino, 56, likes to travel the globe by private jet, glad-handing presidents and princes.



Before he arrived in Vancouver for a Fifa conference in April, the organisation had demanded a ­presidential-style full motorcade for the football administrator.

The level four escort — which can ignore red lights and block other vehicles — is used for visiting US presidents and surpasses security measures laid on for Canada’s Prime Minister Mark Carney.

Vancouver’s police denied the request.

So how did Infantino become football’s arch power broker? And is he now too toxic to run the ­beautiful game?

He was born to Italian immigrant parents in the pretty Swiss Alpine village of Brig in March 1970.



A base for nearby ski slopes and summer hiking trails not far from the Italian border, it is a world away from the cauldrons of international football.

As the youngest of three and known as Piccolo — meaning little one — Infantino suffered health ­complications as an infant and required a blood transfusion.

He would later tell reporters that he received blood from donors in Bristol and Serbia, adding: “I would love to meet them.



“I survived with English blood and 46 years later I am the Fifa president. It’s a personal story, but I am happy to share it.”

His father Vincenzo was from Calabria — the “toe” of Italy — while his mother Maria was originally from Lombardy in its north.

They moved to Switzerland in search of a better life.

Vincenzo worked night shifts on trains while Maria was employed at a newspaper kiosk at the station.

Infantino’s cousin Daniel Nellen, who owns a hair salon in Brig, described Vincenzo’s drive to provide for his family: “Work three days, go, stay one night and come back. When he had days off, he worked in the kiosk at the station with Gianni’s mother. Then he would go again with the train to Rome, Paris, Brussels.”



Yet, despite being grafters, Daniel says the family faced discrimination because of their Italian background.

The salon boss told The Athletic last year: “From the Swiss, we felt this racism. Gianni had red hair and his skin had freckles. This was not too much of a big problem. The problem more was being Italian.”

Infantino touched on the bullying when he made his infamous speech on the eve of the 2022 Qatar World Cup.

Reacting to the criticism of the Gulf state’s human rights record, he said: “Today I feel Qatari. Today I feel Arab. Today I feel African. Today I feel gay. Today I feel disabled. Today I feel a migrant worker.

“I feel like them because I know what it feels like to be discriminated, to be bullied as a foreigner in a country. At school I was bullied because I had red hair and freckles. I was bullied. I didn’t speak good German. What do you do then? You lock yourself in your room, you cry and then you try to make some friends.”



The comments were described as “crass” and “clumsy” by one human rights group.

His cousin Daniel said that growing up, Infantino’s intelligence was “crazy,” adding: “Learning was so easy for Gianni.

“He came home from school and the first thing he would do was open up Gazzetta dello Sport, the Italian sports newspaper — the results of the games, the matches, sport, sport, sport, football, football, football.”



Inter Milan fan Infantino was not much of a player, his career reached only as far as the third team for local amateur club FC Brig-Glis. Another cousin, Renato Vitetta, revealed: “Let’s just say he wasn’t the best player.”

Any hopes that Infantino had of a career on the pitch were over when he was still a primary school pupil. In a school assignment he wrote that he had set his heart instead on becoming a football lawyer.

Cousin Daniel added: “I don’t think that when you are 20 years old, you think about becoming Fifa president.

“But he said, ‘If I’m not good enough [to be a footballer], I want to be the lawyer of the footballer’. Always, his idea was to make ­something with football.”

Aged 18, Infantino stood in FC Brig-Glis’s election for a new ­president.



He promised new sponsors and revenue streams and that his mum Maria would wash the ­players’ kit for as long as he remained president.

Shocking club veterans, he won the vote. It showed an astute grasp of electioneering that Infantino would use in the future.

Studying law at the University of Fribourg, he then won a job as legal counsel and general secretary of the International Centre for Sports Studies in the Swiss city of Neuchatel. Then, aged 30, he landed a ­position in Uefa’s legal department.

Dan O’Toole, Uefa’s former brand manager, remembers him as an “amiable” colleague.

He said last year: “In the early years, we used to go out socially and go around to his house. He was quiet, if anything. Not shy, just sort of quiet.”



Strait-laced Infantino, who speaks seven languages, became best known to football fans as the suit who drily oversaw the Champions League draw.

Rising quickly through the ranks, he became Secretary General in 2009, overseeing the expansion of the Uefa Euro 2016 tournament to 24 teams.

In 2001 he married Leena Al ­Ashqar, who once worked for the Lebanese FA. They have four daughters.



In 2016 he defied expectations and won the Fifa presidential ­election to replace disgraced Sepp Blatter. With a typically sharp- elbowed campaign, he promised to expand the World Cup to 40 teams.

A workaholic, he began his tenure by flying from Geneva to Bristol on a no-frills easyJet flight to attend a meeting in Cardiff.

He told reporters: “It was the ­easiest and best option for me. We are normal people and we have to behave like normal people.”

Today his travel tastes are a little different.

At this summer’s World Cup it was reported he flew at least 31,144 miles by Qatari private jet, watching the likes of Lionel Messi and Jude ­Bellingham work their magic.



Reportedly somewhat aloof while at Fifa’s offices in Zurich, he was said to come alive when mixing with the rich and powerful.

An anonymous source told news site Politico: “He loves dictators and billionaires. When he sees people with money, he melts.”

Nick McGeehan, from the human rights group FairSquare, said last year:

“He clearly thinks of himself as a statesperson. If you don’t think that power can be challenged, you start to behave like an authoritarian and feel at home with others with the same power.”

In 2019 Infantino accepted an Order of Friendship medal from Vladimir Putin and moved his family to Qatar before the 2022 World Cup there.

He faced widespread criticism after he took a selfie close to Pele’s open coffin at the Brazil legend’s 2023 wake.



He claimed Pele’s teammates and family members had asked him to take the photo.

In December 2025 he personally presented Donald Trump with the much-mocked inaugural Fifa Peace Prize.

By February, the US was at war with Iran. Shortly before this summer’s World Cup final, Infantino told Trump: “The American dream, Mr. President, came to reality. We united the world.”

In the tournament, when the US’s star striker Folarin Balogun was red-carded in the Round of 32, it should have triggered an automatic one-match ban, but Trump personally called up his buddy Infantino and lobbied for a review.

In a move that caused widespread anger, Fifa suspended the ban and Balogun played in the next knockout match against Belgium.



Uefa said the decision “crossed a red line” and had undermined “the integrity of the game”. Many felt ­justice was done on the pitch when the US were thrashed 4-1.

The tournament delivered record attendances and $15billion in ­revenue, with 1.5billion fans around the world watching the final itself.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Infantino, desperate for re-election next March, made his move when he considered himself at his most powerful. Yet, his plan to sell off stakes in the World Cup was a ­cataclysmic blunder.

Now, the pompous king of soccer may soon be booted off his Fifa throne.

Sports.title: FA order major change to all English stadiums after tragic death of ex-Arsenal kid Billy Vigar
Sports.content:
'TAKE ACTION' FA order major change to all English stadiums after tragic death of ex-Arsenal kid Billy Vigar

THE FA have banned solid brick walls around pitches in the wake of Billy Vigar’s tragic death last September.

The former Arsenal academy striker died aged 21 after suffering a brain injury while in action for Chichester City against Wingate & Finchley in the seventh tier.



Vigar’s fatal injury was sustained in a collision with a pitchside wall.

The awful incident prompted a petition for all such walls to be removed from football grounds.



Government and PFA chiefs had already called for a safety inquiry in June 2023.

This followed Alex Fletcher’s November 2022 collision with a hoarding while playing for Bath, which saw him suffer a fractured skull.



A safety review by health and safety experts was launched by the Football Association following Vigar’s death.

And ahead of the new campaign, the FA have made their decision.

The ruling states that it “no longer permits solid brick, breeze block or concrete barriers around pitches across the National League System for men [Steps 1-6], and the Women’s National League [Tiers 3-4].”

The FA’s statement goes on to add: “Any existing solid brick, breeze block or concrete barriers must be removed as soon as reasonably practicable, or covered with suitable protection if they cannot be removed for structural reasons.



“We have informed the clubs at this level that will be required to take action as a result of these changes.



“Matches may continue to be played at affected grounds during this period; however, clubs should assess the safety of their pitch perimeter barriers on an ongoing basis, and where alterations to these structures have been recommended during this review, they should develop a plan to complete any such alterations within a reasonable timeframe.”

Money will be made available to help clubs make the vital changes.

The statement concludes: “To support this important work, The FA and the Premier League will provide funding to facilitate these changes, which will be administered by the Premier League Stadium Fund.

“The initial phase of the programme is already underway, and we will continue to provide full support to the clubs involved in this process.”

Sports.title: Gabriel Jesus' agent addresses Arsenal transfer exit after being spotted at rival club
Sports.content:
Gabriel Jesus' agent addresses Arsenal transfer exit after being spotted at rival club

Gabriel Jesus has been made available for a transfer by Arsenal this summer and his agent has now been spotted at the training ground of Napoli amid reported negotiations

View 2 Images Gabriel Jesus could leave Arsenal this summer (Image: Stuart MacFarlane/Arsenal FC via Getty Images)

Gabriel Jesus' agent has insisted that he was not at Napoli's training ground on Friday to discuss a potential transfer for the Arsenal striker. Jesus has entered the final year of his contract with Arsenal and, having fallen down the pecking order after injuries, could be let go this summer.

‌



The Gunners have Viktor Gyokeres and Kai Havertz as their first-choice strikers and are in the market for another attacker, with Atletico Madrid's Julian Alvarez on the wish list after Vinicius Junior decided to stay with Real Madrid.

‌



Mikel Arteta is understood to have green lighted an exit for Jesus, who only made 14 Premier League appearances last season, as well as Gabriel Martinelli. The 29-year-old has been with Arsenal for four years and the club are keen to cash in, rather than lose him for nothing next year.

‌



Napoli are interested in signing Jesus, with Romelu Lukaku and Lorenzo Lucca potentially heading for the exit. Arsenal want a permanent transfer worth €20million (£17m), while the Italian giants are keen to negotiate that fee downwards.

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Arsenal could break unwanted transfer record as Mikel Arteta green lights two deals READ MORE :

Jesus' agent Giovanni Branchini was spotted at Napoli's training ground in Castel di Sangro on Friday, heightening speculation that a deal could be close. But Branchini has insisted that he was visiting the club to see another of his clients, Napoli boss Massimiliano Allegri.

‌



“Allegri and I have been in touch, I came here today to come and visit him,” Branchini told Videoinformazioni.com. “He’s working hard and he’s happy with everything. He’s always had a good opinion of this team and is satisfied with the work that is being done.”

Quizzed on Jesus, Branchini said: “I haven’t spoken to Allegri about him.” And asked if Lukaku and Lucca would have to be sold for Jesus to join, he added: “In my line of work, the ‘ifs’ count for very little, not as much as they matter for you journalists. From my point of view, it’s better to not talk about speculation.”

View 2 Images Gabriel Martinelli and Gabriel Jesus could both be sold this summer (Image: Stuart MacFarlane/Arsenal FC via Getty Images)

‌



Allegri will build his attack around Rasmus Hojlund in the 2026/27 season after the Danish striker completed a permanent £38m move from Manchester United following a successful loan spell. But there is room for another forward, with Lukaku poised to move on and Lucca facing an uncertain future too.

Arsenal have so far only managed to move on Leandro Trossard (£17m to Besiktas), Jakub Kiwior (£14.7m to Porto), Karl Hein (£2.5m to Werder Bremen) and Christian Norgaard (£7m to Everton) this summer. Arteta knows that shifting other fringe players will be key if they are to land a world-class attacker and a centre-back to provide cover for the injured William Saliba.

Jesus has struggled for consistency at Arsenal, with injuries hampering the Brazilian. He has failed to live up to his £45m fee from Manchester City in 2022 and has seen his chances of game time dramatically reduced by the arrival of Gyokeres last summer.

Sports.title: Stevenage down Wycombe with stoppage-time winner to book place in Carabao Cup second round
Sports.content:
Stevenage down Wycombe with stoppage-time winner to book place in Carabao Cup second round

Stevenage scored in the dying embers of Friday's Carabo Cup first round draw with fellow League One side Wycombe to claim a 2-1 victory.

View 3 Images Stevenage manager Alex Revell saw his side claim a stoppage-time victory over Wycombe in the Carabao Cup on Friday

Stevenage debutant Josh Magennis scored an injury-time winner to secure a 2-1 victory over Wycombe and book Alex Revell's side's place in the Carabao Cup second round.

‌



The Northern Irish international, 35, who signed from Exeter City this summer, headed it home in the fifth minute of injury time to break Wycombe hearts at Adams Park on Friday, ensuring it would be a winning start to the competitive season for The Boro.

‌



On the same night, Wolves comfortably saw off League Two side Port Vale 3-0 at Molineux while Middlesbrough defeated Wrexham 1-0 in an all-Championship affair in the other two Carabao Cup games.

‌



Carabao Cup first round TV guide: How to watch every match live this weekend READ MORE :

Both Wycombe and Stevenage welcomed fresh faces into their starting XI's following relatively busy summers, with the hosts giving competitive debuts to goalkeeper Conor Hazard, winger Silko Thomas, right back Sam Parker, and veteran defender Steve Cook, while the visitors started former Burton defender Terence Vancooten from the off.

It took a while for the game to get going, with nothing much to shout about inside the opening 25 minutes as both sides failed to convert several crosses into the box.

However, it was the experienced Dan Kemp in midfield for Stevenage who finally broke the deadlock just before the half-hour mark, pouncing on a poor touch from Wycombe defender Connor Taylor before taking the ball round his man and burying it into the near bottom corner.

‌



View 3 Images Wycombe Wanderers manager Michael Duff saw his side fall to a 2-1 defeat on home soil

The visitors could've doubled their lead within a minute as they countered at pace and caught Wycombe sleeping, though winger Phoenix Patterson could only fire low and hard into Hazard's arms.

Much to the relief of the home fans, however, Wycombe finally dragged themselves back into the game and leveled the scores in the 39th minute, with Scottish midfielder Ewan Henderson playing a neat one-two with Thomas before finding the bottom left corner.

‌



Wycombe ended the first half the better of the two sides, though Kemp came so close to doubling his and Stevenage's tally with a piledriver from the edge of the penalty area that smacked the underside of the crossbar before bouncing back out.

The Chairboys continued their positive play into the second half as the lively Fred Onyedinma caused plenty of problems down the right, while several penalty shouts for the hosts were also waived away by referee Jamie O'Connor.

View 3 Images Stevenage midfielder Dan Kemp opened the scoring in the first half

Article continues below

On the opposite flank, debutant Thomas was also causing problems for Stevenage's defense, but Wycombe just couldn't carve out an opening that would give them the lead in the tie.

Both teams pushed for a winner in the final embers of the game, but neither could find the winner they so desperately craved, until Magennis, fresh off the substitutes bench, popped up with a header in the dying seconds to win the game for Stevenage and book their spot in Monday's second round draw.

Both sides are next in action on the opening day of the League One season next weekend, when Wycombe travel to face Blackpool and Stevenage face Burton, both on Saturday, Aug. 15 (3 p.m.).

Sports.title: Man Utd contacted by Newcastle after launching Lewis Hall transfer enquiry
Sports.content:
Man Utd contacted by Newcastle after launching Lewis Hall transfer enquiry

Newcastle have sold Anthony Gordon and Sandro Tonali this summer, with Bruno Guimaraes also set to leave, and attention has now turned to Manchester United target Lewis Hall

View 2 Images Newcastle don't want to sell Lewis Hall (Image: Serena Taylor/Newcastle United via Getty Images)

Newcastle have made it clear to Manchester United that Lewis Hall is not for sale this summer at any price. United are keen to sign a left-back in this window and have kept an eye on Hall for some time, but it seems Michael Carrick won't get his man this summer.

‌



United prioritised central midfield in the early stages of the window, with Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos arriving from Aston Villa and Chelsea respectively for a combined £87million.

‌



Left-back is now a position on the agenda, with Carrick wanting competition for Luke Shaw, who impressed last season but has a chequered injury history. Academy graduate Harry Amass would be allowed to leave for the right price, while last summer's signing Diego Leon has failed to kick on so far and Tyrell Malacia left on a free transfer.

‌



Diogo Dalot and Noussair Mazraoui can both play left-back if needed, but Patrick Dorgu has shone further forward, convincing United to go back into the market.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

United thought they could take advantage of the turmoil at Newcastle this summer, with Eddie Howe being replaced by Matthias Jaissle. But the departures of Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and the pending exit of Bruno Guimaraes to Arsenal has worked against them.

‌



Sky Sports reports that Newcastle have told United in no uncertain terms to look elsewhere. The Magpies first communicated their stance two weeks ago and consider the matter to be settled.

Newcastle's hierarchy are under pressure to steady the ship following the exits of Howe, Gordon, Tonali and Guimaraes. Sporting director Ross Wilson has taken the approach of publicly explaining the £75m sale of Guimaraes to Arsenal.

"What we had to weigh up was, very respectfully from Bruno with his behaviour towards us, very emotionally as well, he effectively told us he wanted to leave and move on," he said.

‌



View 2 Images Bruno Guimaraes' exit has strengthened Newcastle's stance on Lewis Hall (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

"That doesn't mean he can go, but it certainly plays a part in what our thinking is when we hit a certain range of number. There's no part in saying it was part of our strategy and was in our thinking this summer - it wasn't. But we have got to be flexible and react to things that happen."

Unlike Guimaraes, Hall is not agitating for a move. The 21-year-old joined Newcastle for £35m from Chelsea three summers ago and has been a regular fixture on the left side of defence.

Article continues below

With Hall appearing to be a dead end, United could turn their attention to Racing Santander's Jorge Salinas, who is considered to be a viable alternative. The 19-year-old is highly rated and has a €16m (£13.7m) release clause, although United could face competition from Barcelona. Bologna's Jhon Lucumi, who is valued at €25m (£21.7m) is another option.

Sports.title: FA announce changes after tragic death of ex-Arsenal footballer aged 21
Sports.content:
FA announce changes after tragic death of ex-Arsenal footballer aged 21

Former Arsenal youngster Billy Vigar suffered a significant brain injury back in September last year, with changes now being put in place by the Football Association

View 2 Images Billy Vigar passed away in September (Image: David Price/Arsenal FC via Getty Images)

The Football Association (FA) have announced that solid walls around the perimeter of pitches have been banned following the tragic death of Billy Vigar. The former Arsenal youth player died from a head injury after colliding with a wall last season.

The incident occurred with Vigar playing for Chichester City against Wingate & Finchley FC back in September. The 21-year-old collided with a concrete wall surrounding the pitch, resulting in a significant brain injury.

Vigar was part of Arsenal’s youth sides before moving to Hastings United in 2024. He signed with Chichester City last summer, a few months before his death.

The wall at Wingate & Finchley FC has now been removed, with the FA confirming a review of pitch surroundings for non-league grounds . The findings of the review have now been released.

It has been confirmed that the FA: "no longer permits solid brick, breeze block or concrete barriers around pitches across the National League system for men [steps 1-6], and the Women's National League [tiers 3-4]".

UEFA could boycott 5 tournaments in next 11 months after new Gianni Infantino statement READ MORE :

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Article continues below

In a statement, the FA added: "Any existing solid brick, breeze block or concrete barriers must be removed as soon as reasonably practicable, or covered with suitable protection if they cannot be removed for structural reasons. We have informed the clubs at this level that will be required to take action as a result of these changes.

"Matches may continue to be played at affected grounds during this period; however, clubs should assess the safety of their pitch perimeter barriers on an ongoing basis, and where alterations to these structures have been recommended during this review, they should develop a plan to complete any such alterations within a reasonable timeframe."

Non-league clubs will be helped with funding the changes with the money coming from both the FA and the Premier League. The Press Association reports that 160 of the 900 clubs who play at the levels have been contacted over changes that will have to be made to their stadiums.

View 2 Images The FA have announced changes following the youngster's tragic death (Image: Getty Images)

The FA added: "The initial phase of the programme is already underway, and we will continue to provide full support to the clubs involved in this process.”

Following the announcement, a PFA spokesperson said: “Following the tragic death of Billy Vigar last year, we again highlighted these concerns and made clear our view that the lack of progress and leadership on this issue had been unacceptable.

"As part of working groups set up by the FA following Billy's death, we pushed for the FA's Stadium Accreditation criteria to be amended to ban these types of walls so that there is a clear and centralised policy for clubs to follow.

"Given that, it's a welcome step that the FA's regulations have now been changed to reflect that position.

"However, it will now be important for progress on the removal of such walls - and effective mitigation of risks ahead of their removal - to be properly monitored, and for clubs to be given the support they need so that these changes can happen as soon as possible. Player safety must always come first."
