Sports.title: Liverpool prepare blockbuster offer for PSG star Bradley Barcola - but there's a catch
Sports.content:
Liverpool prepare blockbuster offer for PSG star Bradley Barcola - but there's a catch

Bradley Barcola is Liverpool's top transfer target this summer and the Reds are now ready to move forward with trying to sign the Paris Saint-Germain winger

View 2 Images Bradley Barcola is Liverpool's top transfer target (Image: Getty Images)

Liverpool are ready to make their opening offer for Paris Saint-Germain winger Bradley Barcola, but their bid will be rejected by the French giants.

‌



Barcola has emerged as Liverpool's number one transfer target this summer, with new manager Andoni Iraola desperate to strengthen in wide areas. The France international has entered the final two years of his current contract with PSG, who have softened their stance on a deal.

‌



The reigning Champions League champions had initially been firm in their stance that the 23-year-old was not for sale at any price. But, having lined up potential replacements, a deal can now be done - if their asking price is met.

‌



Liverpool have found it slow going in the transfer window this summer, with a £35million deal for Osasuna winger Victor Munoz the only significant piece of business done, as the £55m arrival of Jeremy Jacquet was sealed in January.

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Liverpool weigh up hijacking £60m Arsenal transfer to appease desperate Andoni Iraola READ MORE :

But the Reds are now ready to step up negotiations with PSG for Barcola, according to L'Equipe. They will submit an official offer in the region of €115million (£98m) in the expectation that it will be rejected.

‌



PSG don't want to lose Barcola, who has contributed heavily to their success under Luis Enrique's management. Yet they are also unwilling to keep a player against his will, so have slapped a €150 million (£128.5m) price tag on their star player.

Their resolve has likely be strengthened by the £120m fee RB Leipzig got from Real Madrid for Yan Diomande - a player four years younger and with far less experience than Barcola.

Barcola has 39 goals in 152 appearances for the club since joining from Lyon three years ago. He has combined well with Ousmane Dembele and Desire Doue under Enrique's management, but is keen to join Liverpool.

‌



View 2 Images Andoni Iraola is desperate for a new winger (Image: Michael Miller/ISI Photos, ISI Photos via Getty Images)

Barcola has already agreed personal terms with Liverpool and it seems likely that a deal can be done. Liverpool sporting director Richard Hughes is leading discussions, with Luis Campos representing PSG and agent Moussa Sissoko speaking on behalf of Barcola.

L'Equipe says that Liverpool are not actively pursuing any alternative to Barcola, which is a measure of their determination to land the Frenchman. Iraola spoke publicly about the need for a winger, even after Munoz was signed.

‌



"There are obvious situations that we know where we need to sign players," he said last month. "A winger, for example – we definitely need to sign a winger.

"But there are other situations that we will have to analyse what the market gives you, what’s the cost, how we also see the players we have. We have some tricky positions where we have injured players that we trust but is still not the ideal situation. So, it will depend on a lot of things."

Sports.title: Arsenal could break unwanted transfer record as Mikel Arteta green lights two deals
Sports.content:
Arsenal could break unwanted transfer record as Mikel Arteta green lights two deals

Arsenal are still chasing a blockbuster signing in the summer transfer window and Mikel Arteta's side need to lay the groundwork first by making space in the squad

View 2 Images Mikel Arteta knows that sales are needed this summer (Image: Stuart MacFarlane/Arsenal FC via Getty Images)

Arsenal could finally eclipse their record sale with Gabriel Martinelli attracting interest from Turkey. The Gunners' focus recently has been on Bruno Guimaraes and Vinicius Junior, but exits are also in the pipeline.

‌



Guimaraes is poised to join Mikel Arteta's side for £75million after a compromise was reached with Newcastle. But the pursuit of Vinicius has ended in defeat, with the Brazilian forward set to sign a new contract with Real Madrid.

‌



Arsenal will now turn their attention to other targets as they chase a blockbuster deal, and while the identity of their alternative signing is not yet known, the groundwork is being laid. Leandro Trossard (Besiktas), Jakub Kiwior (Porto), Karl Hein (Werder Bremen) and Christian Norgaard (Everton) are currently the only players to leave and bring in transfer fees this summer.

‌



It is something that sporting director Andrea Berta knows he must address, especially if a world-class forward like Julian Alvarez and a centre-back to cover for the injured William Saliba is to arrive before the deadline passes on September 1.

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Liverpool's firm stance on Djed Spence transfer as Reds battle defensive injury crisis READ MORE :

Martinelli has entered the final year of his contract with Arsenal, posing the possibility of his exit, over seven years after he joined the club. The 25-year-old has 62 goals in 278 appearances for the club since his £6million move in 2019, but his time may have come.

‌



Arsenal are reportedly considering a sale to Galatasaray, who are interested in landing the Brazil international. And were a move to come to fruition it could see Martinelli become Arsenal's record sale, with the £35m earned for Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain's move to Liverpool in 2019 surprisingly still the high-water mark for the club.

Their inability to sell well has become an issue for Arsenal, who have often seen their rivals out-perform them. Trossard pulled in £17m from Besiktas, while Norgaard earned just £7m from Everton. If Arsenal are to achieve their goals in terms of incomings then Martinelli and Gabriel Jesus could become facilitators.

View 2 Images Gabriel Martinelli and Gabriel Jesus could both be sold (Image: Stuart MacFarlane/Arsenal FC via Getty Images)

‌



Jesus has become a fringe player at Arsenal, with Viktor Gyokeres and Kai Havertz ahead of him in the pecking order and is attracting interest from Napoli and AC Milan. The 29-year-old's contract expires in June 2027, meaning this window is Arsenal's last realistic chance to earn a decent fee.

Arsenal are understood to be seeking a fee in the region of the £17m they got for Trossard, but as time ticks by in August they could be forced to compromise.

Arteta knows that Arsenal must strengthen their squad this summer if they are to stand any chance of defending their Premier League title in 2026/27. "We are really active, trying to improve and evolve the team. That's clear," he said in a post-match press conference after facing Girona on the weekend.

Article continues below

"We expect to have movements in the next few weeks, obviously, because we want to get better like anybody else. And you can just see it. The transfer market and our opponents, what we are doing, we won't sit still. And we are very ambitious in what we want to do."

Sports.title: UEFA could boycott 5 tournaments in next 11 months after new Gianni Infantino statement
Sports.content:
UEFA could boycott 5 tournaments in next 11 months after new Gianni Infantino statement

Gianni Infantino is determined to cling onto power as FIFA president and his refusal to resign in the wake of the World Cup private investment scandal could force UEFA into action

View 2 Images Gianni Infantino is ready for the fight (Image: AP Photo/Martin Meissner)

UEFA could be forced to carry out their threat of boycotting FIFA tournaments in less than a month after Gianni Infantino refused to give in to the mounting pressure on him to resign.

‌



Rather than fall on his sword, Infantino has made moves to solidify his position as FIFA president. Following seven hours of crisis talks in Morocco on Wednesday, FIFA released a statement saying Infantino had their "full support" after his botched attempt to invite private investment into tournaments.

‌



FIFA have opted to close ranks and go on the offensive, saying they will "no longer tolerate any attacks on its integrity, good governance and due process and will take all necessary measures to protect and safeguard its name and reputation".

‌



The battle lines have been drawn, with UEFA leading the backlash against Infantino. The Football Association has followed in Wales' footsteps by formally withdrawing their support of the Swiss, but with the pressure yet to tell, UEFA and their allies may have to follow through with their threat.

Gianni Infantino state of play as 211 nations decide desperate FIFA president's fate READ MORE :

Argentina at odds with England as statement released on FIFA president Gianni Infantino READ MORE :

In a statement on Thursday, UEFA said FIFA's words following their meeting "changes nothing" and that their threat of a boycott stands. It means FIFA have been put on notice ahead of their next international tournament, the Under-20 Women's World Cup, which is scheduled to be hosted in Poland, beginning on September 5.

After that comes the Under-17 Women's World Cup in Morocco in October and the Under-17 World Cup in Qatar in November and December. Next summer comes a much bigger fish: the Women's World Cup in Brazil. If it came to it, boycotting that would send a strong message - and it is a sacrifice England star Lucy Bronze is willing to make.

‌



FIFA tournaments UEFA could boycott FIFA Under-20 Women's World Cup (Poland) - September 2026 FIFA Under-17 Women's World Cup (Morocco) - October 2026 FIFA Under-17 World Cup (Qatar) -November/December 2026 FIFA Women's Champions Cup (Miami) -January 2027 FIFA Women's World Cup (Brazil) - June/July 2027

“The message that we stand by … is ‘for the good of the game’. The players who play in those competitions, the European players, we stand by our beliefs and what the right thing is for our game,” Bronze said ahead of a Chelsea pre-season friendly in New Zealand.

“If that means boycotting competitions, then that has to happen. It’s for the future of the game and not just for me today and tomorrow, it’s for all the little girls or little boys who come after us to make sure that they’re in a good place, when the game is moving forward in decades to come, not just tomorrow.”

‌



With Infantino not willing to resign, UEFA may have to back a rival candidate in the upcoming FIFA presidential election. Infantino has been in charge for 10 years and was set to stand unopposed for a fourth term next year, but the events of the past week have changed everything.

View 2 Images UEFA president Aleksander Ceferin is leading the effort to oust Gianni Infantino (Image: Nicolò Campo/LightRocket via Getty Images)

A UEFA statement shared on Thursday afternoon read: "UEFA's associations were very clear about the conditions attached to the non-participation in FIFA competitions.

‌



"First, the proposals to sell off the major competitions had to be withdrawn, and secondly, assurances have to be made that such attempts to disfigure the game in this way will never be made again.

"These conditions have not been met. In addition, UEFA made it abundantly clear in its statement on Saturday that it has lost confidence in Gianni Infantino's presidency. That position holds.

"Yesterday's (Wednesday) announcement that some people employed by the FIFA President (and whose careers depend on his favour) agree with him changes nothing."

Sports.title: Araujo set for surprise Liverpool loan move
Sports.content:
Liverpool have agreed a surprise deal for Barcelona defender Ronald Araujo to join on loan for the season.

The deal is a straight loan for the 27-year-old, who signed a new contract until 2031 last year.

The Uruguay international joined Barcelona B in 2018 before being promoted to the first team in 2019.

The 27-year-old centre-back will add to Andoni Iraola's options at the heart of his defence following the departure of Ibrahima Konate to Real Madrid and fitness concerns over relatively inexperienced 21-year-old Jeremy Jacquet.

The summer signing from Rennes has made fewer than 100 senior career appearances and has not featured in pre-season yet after missing the second half of last season following shoulder surgery.

Sports.title: Debut Lankshear goal sees Boro past Wrexham as Wolves & Stevenage progress
Sports.content:
Will Lankshear's debut strike ensured Middlesbrough made a winning start to the season as they beat Wrexham 1-0 in the Carabao Cup first round.

Lankshear, a £10m summer signing from Tottenham, scored the only goal of the game in the 61st minute as he hooked home an excellent first-time volley.

Middlesbrough almost claimed a seventh-minute opener, but while Adilson Malanda prodded Sebastian Berhalter's cross goalwards from close range, Danny Ward kept the ball out with a superb point-blank save.

Danny Imray wasted a decent chance for Wrexham when he failed to make a proper connection from Callum Doyle's cross, and the visitors went close again six minutes before the break when Sam Smith fired a low shot into the legs of Sol Brynn after he was rolled into space by Nathan Broadhead.

Lankshear came close with an effort that was curled just over the bar at the start of the second half, but the 21-year-old did not have to wait too much longer for his first goal in a Boro shirt.

Leo Castledine headed Jeremy Sarmiento's cross into Lankshear's path, and the striker swivelled neatly before hooking a superb first-time volley into the far corner.

Boro almost doubled their lead with three minutes remaining, but Morgan Whittaker's low strike rebounded off the post.

Wolves coast past Port Vale as Jimenez makes return

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of Wolves' clash with Port Vale in the first round of the Carabao Cup.

Wolves progressed with a comfortable 3-0 win over Port Vale in which all three goals came in the first half. Adam Armstrong, Andre and Fer Lopez took the game away from the League Two side as Cesar Peixoto marked his first game in charge with a win.

Jon Brady's Port Vale had opportunities. Jordan Lawrence-Gabriel hooked an extraordinary chance away from the Wolves goal before the break, before Mo Faal's low penalty was saved by the legs of Dan Bentley to deny the travelling fans a consolation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Port Vale's Jordan Lawrence-Gabriel misses a chance from six yards out in his side's Carabao Cup clash with Wolves.

The Wolves supporters among the crowd of 21,360 at Molineux were more interested in serenading their returning hero. Raul Jimenez, the club's Premier League top scorer, re-signed this summer after three years at Fulham and came on as a late substitute.

The Mexican centre-forward did fire off one fierce shot on goal but he was unable to mark the occasion with a goal that would have been cruel on a competitive Port Vale side. But it is Wolves who take their place in the second round of the Carabao Cup.

Stevenage strike late to beat Wycombe

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the first round Carabao Cup match between Wycombe Wanderers and Stevenage.

New signing Josh Magennis headed the winner in the dying seconds to send Stevenage through to the second round of the Carabao Cup with a 2-1 victory at Wycombe.

It was a fitting start to the Boro's 50th anniversary season as substitute Magennis, a summer capture from Exeter, rose to score from Phoenix Patterson's left-wing corner in the fifth minute of second-half stoppage time.

The visitors had shaken off early pressure to take the lead against the run of play in the 27th minute.

Midfielder Dan Kemp took advantage of hesitancy in the Wycombe defence as he raced through to fire home a low shot.

That stung the home side into action and Ewan Henderson equalised in the 38th minute. Winger Silko Thomas crossed from the left and the Scot slipped through the visiting defence to score right-footed from just outside the six-yard box.

Stevenage scared their Sky Bet League One rivals again on the stroke of half-time when Kemp rattled the bar with a shot from the edge of the box.

Wycombe took control after the break but struggled to break through.

New boy Emre Tezgel, on for Cauley Woodrow, was thwarted by Boro skipper Carl Piergianni as he attempted to force home Thomas' cross from the left in the 77th minute before Magennis settled the issue.

The Carabao Cup is back for the 2026/27 season, with every first-round tie available to watch live on Sky Sports!

West Ham, Burnley and Leicester are among those in action on Saturday - and you can follow the goals as they go in from all 29 ties on Soccer Saturday.

Every match from the opening round will be shown live on Sky Sports, with clubs from the Championship, League One and League Two entering the competition.

Sports.title: New Zealand begin South Africa tour with flattering win over Stormers
Sports.content:
New Zealand's first full-scale tour of South Africa in 30 years began with an underwhelming 38-21 win over the Stormers.

The scoreline flattered a scratch All Blacks side which was favoured to win comfortably.

The makeshift Stormers - in pre-season mode - rallied twice to tie the score, which was knotted at 14-14 until 13 minutes to go.

When the Stormers lost their second scrum-half and had no more reserve backs, the patched-up backline was ruthlessly exposed by New Zealand, who scored three tries in the last eight minutes.

The good news for the All Blacks was they appeared to finish with no major injuries, seven players made their first appearance in the black jersey this year, and two more made their debuts off the bench; prop Siale Lauaki and inside back Josh Jacomb.

"They came at us with their set-piece and we need to be better in those areas. We expected a lot of aerial attacks and we probably did ‌not handle that as well as we could have."

Sports.title: UEFA aware of allegation it paid off Infantino's 'mistress' while he worked for them
Sports.content:
UEFA confirms it is aware of an allegation that it paid off an alleged mistress of Gianni Infantino while he was working for them; Infantino, now FIFA president, strongly denies the allegations

Gianni Infantino: UEFA aware of allegation it paid off an alleged mistress of FIFA president while he worked at European governing body

UEFA has confirmed it is aware of an allegation that European football's governing body paid off an alleged mistress of Gianni Infantino.

The Telegraph is reporting that while Infantino was general secretary at UEFA, a woman who was allegedly in a relationship with the now FIFA president received a six-figure sum.

According to The Telegraph, UEFA paid for the individual's MBA (Master of Business Administration degree) after she left.

In a statement to The Telegraph, a FIFA spokesperson said: "FIFA president Gianni Infantino strongly denies these allegations, and they are categorically untrue. Any insinuation of inappropriate conduct or violation of statutes or regulations is defamatory.

"No employee at UEFA and FIFA has ever raised a complaint regarding Mr Infantino's behaviour because there never was an incident where he was involved. All company actions related to employees, including any departure and severance packages, have always been approved by the appropriate directors in accordance with all applicable regulations."

UEFA told Sky Sports News that an individual was paid, but this was in line with regulations at the time - which have since been tightened.

In a statement to Sky Sports News, UEFA said: "We are aware of the allegations and can confirm a departure payment was made to the individual in question, coupled with the payment of fees for an MBA course at a local business school.

"The payment was in line with the regulations that existed for departing staff at the time. Such regulations have been tightened since 2016 and the current staff regulations - which apply to all UEFA employees at whatever level - reflect those found in a modern, high-profile organisation."

Infantino worked at UEFA from 2000 until leaving in 2016, when he took up his current role at FIFA.

FIFA has been contacted for comment by Sky Sports News.

Sports.title: Flintoff steps down as England Lions head coach
Sports.content:
Andrew Flintoff has stepped down as head coach of the England Lions.

Flintoff began in the role in September 2024, meaning he leaves just under two years in.

In June it was announced Flintoff would become head coach of Sydney Thunder in Australia's Big Bash League.

On the decision, Flintoff said: "Unfortunately I've made the decision to step away from my role with the Lions. Not only have I enjoyed my time having the opportunity to work with the best young cricketers in the country, but have taken great pride in seeing them develop.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Relive the top highlights from Andrew Flintoff's seven-game stint with Brisbane Heat in 2014/15.

"I'd like to thank the coaches and staff for all their passion, tireless work and support they give every day. In particular, Ed Barney who I've loved working with and was so lucky to have as a performance director, and obviously Rob (Key) for trusting me with one of the most important roles in English cricket.

"I can't wait to get started with the Thunder later in the year and see where coaching takes me."

Ed Barney, ECB men's performance director, said: "Fred has helped to transform the Lions environment into a programme that has had a major impact on young players. By creating an environment that both supports and pushes excellence at all times he has helped bring forward a new generation of young players.

"Coaches have also flourished alongside him, whether early in their coaching journey or with decades of experience, and he has consistently maximised the expertise around the group. We wish him the best in the next stage of his coaching career and look forward to a time he returns to the English game."

Mike Yardy will step in as head coach for the four-day Professional County Club Select XI match against Pakistan Men, which begins at Beckenham on Wednesday August 12.

Sports.title: Infantino’s World Cup sell-off debacle has rocked football but Fifa’s crisis has deep and rotten roots
Sports.content:
There are decades in which nothing happens, and weeks in which decades happen, and those weeks tend to result in leaders being toppled. Not even a fortnight ago, Gianni Infantino was taking his victory lap on Instagram, attacking “those behind their pens and papers, behind their screens spreading hate and false rumours” who had dared to question elements of his World Cup, which had generated a record $15bn in revenues. But the next day came the revelation of his plan to sell the World Cup to outside investors and a backlash that has him scrabbling to save his presidency.

It has been a remarkable few days, but this is a story whose roots stretch way back, to the decision in Zurich in 2010 to award the 2022 World Cup not to the US but to Qatar, to a furious Bill Clinton hurling an ashtray across the room and demanding action, to an FBI inquiry into corruption, and to the flipping of the larger-than-life Concacaf general secretary Chuck Blazer, who had two apartments in Trump Tower, one for himself and one for his cats.

Blazer now appears as the cheery, bearded, acceptable face of Fifa corruption. He drove about on a mobility scooter with his parrot, Max, on his shoulder and once high-fived Vladimir Putin after the Russian president suggested he looked like Karl Marx. But it was Blazer’s evidence that led to the arrests at Zurich’s Baur au Lac hotel in 2015 and the resignation of Sepp Blatter six days later.

The overwhelming favourite to replace Blatter was the president of Uefa, Michel Platini. He, though, was unacceptable to the US, because it was his decision to switch his vote to Qatar, following – although he maintains not as a result of – a meeting at the Élysée Palace with the then French president Nicolas Sarkozy and the crown prince and prime minister of Qatar.

Conveniently, evidence was found of a payment he had received from Fifa in 2011 leading to his suspension. The Berne federal prosecutor, Michael Lauber, broke protocol to name Platini as something “between a witness and a suspect”. It was enough: Platini stepped aside and Infantino stepped in as Uefa’s candidate. Lauber subsequently became attorney general of Switzerland only to resign after secretly meeting Infantino while investigating Fifa. Platini was subsequently cleared and is suing both Fifa and Infantino.

View image in fullscreen Chuck Blazer’s evidence led to the resignation of Sepp Blatter (left) in 2015. Photograph: Fabrice Coffrini/AFP/Getty Images

At the time, Infantino was the secretary general of Uefa, notable largely for his comical earnestness while conducting Champions League draws. He was elected Fifa president in February 2016, defeating the Bahraini Sheikh Salman bin Ibrahim Al Khalifa, the president of the Asian Football Confederation, an avid hunter of wild boar who denied allegations of complicity in the torture of pro-democracy campaigners. Key had been a late change of mind by the Caribbean bloc: Sunil Gulati, the president of the US Soccer Federation, took credit for his persuasiveness.

With an ally elected, the US, Mexico and Canada won the right to host the 2026 World Cup. “You wanted to have it there and I wanted to have it there, and we really did it before we came to office,” Donald Trump, performing his classic trick of supervillain exposition, told Infantino at a dinner in Davos in 2020. The order of events is worth reiterating: Infantino was elected in February 2016, Trump was inaugurated in January 2017, the World Cup hosting decision was taken in May 2018.

The US has been a constant in Infantino’s presidency. He took power at a time when the US attorney general, Loretta Lynch, was promising to swill corruption out of Fifa but in terms of decisive action that has amounted to little more than a handful of cases involving dodgy South American broadcast rights deals. In May 2019 Fifa appointed as legal representatives the US law firm Paul Weiss. A few weeks earlier Paul Weiss had named a new senior partner: the former US attorney general Lynch. The following year, she praised Fifa’s newfound “transparency and ethical behaviour”.

Few would agree with her. Infantino arrived promising reform, yet within a year he was removing two leaders of Fifa’s ethics commission. The same weekend that Trump sacked James Comey as head of the FBI, in part for investigating Russian interference in US politics, Infantino fired Miguel Maduro, the chair of the governance and review committee, for blocking the re-election as a Fifa vice-president of the head of the Russian Football Union Vitaly Mutko on the grounds that as Russia’s sports minister he breached guidelines on political involvement.

View image in fullscreen Loretta Lynch promised to swill out corruption from Fifa during her time as US attorney general but there was minimal decisive action. Photograph: Saul Loeb/AFP/Getty Images

Infantino repeatedly bypassed the Fifa council, ducked the scrutiny of press conferences and came increasingly to rule by fiat. The plan to sell off a chunk of the World Cup is just the most egregious example. Why would he keep a plan of such revolutionary significance from his senior staff? Why would he give his members 53 days to consider such a plan, offering them a cash bonus to acquiesce? Why would he undermine his own tournament with hydration breaks and a half-time show in the final? Why override disciplinary protocols so the right players will be on the field, seemingly to highlight the tournament’s commercial appeal to potential investors?

The people who were in on the deal were connected to the Trump family, specifically Joshua Kushner, the brother of the president’s son-in-law. Again, questions immediately arise. Why would you sell off 21% of all future revenues for only 28% of what this World Cup made? Infantino’s relationship with Trump – awarding him the inaugural Fifa Peace Prize, appearing with him at world events, giving him a Club World Cup trophy, renting an office for Fifa in Trump Tower that is seemingly barely used – had already brought criticism.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Uefa’s robust and united response, the threat to boycott Fifa tournaments, was evidently not anticipated. The plan is dead, at least for now. Infantino, damaged, clings on, having rallied at least some senior Fifa staff at an emergency meeting in Rabat this week. The chief operating officer, Kevin Lamour, one of the two members of the five-man inner council who voted against the plan when informed about it the day before the World Cup final, was, notably, not there. Plans to expand the World Cup to 64 teams, rallying Infantino’s base, have been accelerated.

View image in fullscreen Gianni Infantino’s relationship with Donald Trump has attracted plenty of criticism. Photograph: Image Photo Agency/Getty Images

Letters of support that had looked as if they would ensure Infantino a further term unopposed are being withdrawn. On Friday, perhaps impressed by the promise of the 2030 World Cup final being in Casablanca, the Confederation of African Football pledged its support, joining Mexico, Argentina, Qatar, the UAE, Lebanon, Kuwait, Bhutan and Sri Lanka in backing Infantino.

Perhaps there will be an election, as scheduled, next March. Perhaps Infantino can muster a majority among Fifa’s 211 members. But Uefa has vowed to “paralyse” Fifa until he is gone. The first tournament that might be boycotted is the Under- 20 Women’s World Cup, which begins in Poland on 5 September. Poland has made significant investment in infrastructure and is keen for the tournament to go ahead as scheduled but its football federation would be unlikely to step outside the Uefa bloc.

The politicking goes on although already the discussion seems more about who might challenge or defeat Infantino than about how to change Fifa, where clientelism has reigned since João Havelange won the 1974 presidential election. The institution itself is rotten; it may be that it is irredeemable.

It’s very hard to know how genuine Infantino’s attempt to reform Fifa was, but it quickly foundered. And so Fifa’s attempt to move on from the crisis caused by the executive who rented an apartment for his cats in Trump Tower has wound up back in Trump Tower, with a president who rents an office there.
