Sports.title: Boardroom struggle deepens gloom as West Ham prepare for life on the outside
Sports.content:
There have been 10 summers of West Ham’s London Stadium tenancy and a number of winters of discontent. As the Hammers kick off the new season on Saturday, a Carabao Cup first-round fixture with Portsmouth is a stark reminder of reduced circumstances, further confirmation of last season’s relegation from the Premier League. The summer has been as bleak as any of those winters, with a number of factors colliding to deepen the gloom of relegation.

Certain clubs, including West Ham back in 2011-12 when promotion was achieved at first time of asking under Sam Allardyce, have used the Championship to take a beat, to refresh and replenish. Can this be the case at West Ham 2026? The Hammers are short-odds favourites for promotion but behind the scenes it has been a summer of turbulence, particularly in the boardroom, where a power struggle is being fought.

Portsmouth will bring 9,000 supporters on Saturday but will David Sullivan be present? This week it was revealed the operators of London Stadium had recommended the former joint-chair (but still co-owner) stay away, because of the “potential for demonstrations and anti-social behaviour by some spectators”.

It is expected that Sullivan will turn up, despite a fans’ advisory board statement that his attendance would cause “offence and upset”. It has been suggested that he wants to enjoy the coming season as a fan and is happy to bide his time before any consideration of selling his 38.8% stake. Considering his personal circumstances, his attendance would be a brazenly unpopular act. On 25 May, when relegation was confirmed despite a home win over Leeds, Sullivan was forced to leave the stadium early for his own safety.

View image in fullscreen Daniel Kretinsky wants to increase his shares in West Ham to just under 50.1%. Photograph: David W Černý/Reuters

Sullivan continues to deny allegations of sexually exploitative and predatory behaviour towards women over several decades made by the BBC’s Panorama documentary in early June, though he stepped down from his role on the eve of the broadcast “to avoid disruption to the club while he addresses the matter privately”.

Even before those allegations became public, Sullivan was a lightning rod, lambasted for his stewardship of a club in vertiginous decline since winning the Europa Conference League in May 2023. The £100m fee received for Declan Rice that summer was frittered away. Fellow Prague hero Jarrod Bowen, the club captain, has pledged to stay on, tasked with leading the club back up.

Until his defenestration Sullivan had acted as the club’s de facto director of football, often to the frustration of those in the football department. His chief ally, Karren Brady, stepped down in April as storm clouds gathered, severing a working relationship that dated as far back as 1990.

Among the club’s support, 50,000 season tickets have been sold for the attempt at re-entry to the Premier League. The overriding desire among fans is for Sullivan to completely depart the scene. His announced departure had installed a modicum of optimism.

Potential new sheriffs are circling but the picture is complicated, any future direction opaque as a result. As Sullivan stepped down the expectation was that Daniel Kretinsky, the Czech billionaire owner of Royal Mail who has owned 27% of West Ham since 2021, would make his move. Instead, this week, he cut that share down to just under 25%, though this was part of a strategy.

Last weekend, the familiar face of Amanda Staveley entered the picture. In July 2024 she departed Newcastle, after her leading role in bringing in the Saudi Arabian Public Investment Fund, but now Staveley wants to return to football. Last September, she was linked with a takeover at Tottenham, and it is suggested she will use a similar source of funding to engineer her move for West Ham. Among Newcastle fans, with their club faltering this summer, Staveley’s energy is lamented. With her connections, some Hammers fan hope she could have a similar galvanising effect.

View image in fullscreen David Sullivan’s closet ally, Karren Brady, left the club in April. Photograph: PA Images/Alamy

The key is the 25% that belonged to the late David Gold, Sullivan’s former joint-chair. As Staveley loomed, Kretinsky appeared ready to take up his first refusal on purchasing that 25% from Vanessa Gold, David’s daughter and current co-chair. Adding that to his 27% would take him beyond 50.1%, leaving him liable for a formal takeover offer. But shifting 2% to a Czech ally, the entrepreneur Jakub Havrlant, now means he would be short of that obligation should he cut across Staveley’s ambitions by buying Gold’s stake. Sullivan’s shares also hold the balance of power and Staveley’s next move is keenly awaited.

While that plays out, what of football? The arrival of free agent, the former Brighton and Ajax defender, Joël Veltman, was the first addition of a summer where the sales of Mateus Fernandes to Tottenham and Crysencio Summerville to Al-Hilal fetched a collective £140m, commensurate to a year of Premier League TV money. Youth product Freddie Potts’ departure to Club Brugge for £10m disappointed some fans. Needs must if further players are to arrive. There is interest in Ireland’s World Cup playoff hero Troy Parrott, the striker at AZ Alkmaar, though attracting players to the Championship has its difficulties.

View image in fullscreen West Ham have cashed in on key players, such as Mateus Fernandes to Tottenham, to cushion their descent into the Championship. Photograph: Phil Walter/Getty Images

In the dugout remains Nuno Espírito Santo, who stayed when his departure had been expected. Nuno’s zen-like calm is required at a club where panic regularly sets in. The vacuum created by Sullivan’s situation, relegation and lack of transfer business heightens anxieties. A new season has arrived, with uninviting league fixtures against Burnley, Charlton, Watford and Wolves by 1 September. Karim Virani, previously a club employee who departed in 2020, more recently at Glasgow Rangers, has returned as interim chief executive. Attempts are being made to stitch West Ham into a semblance of unity.

This summer, the London Stadium played host to concerts from Take That and Metallica, and staged the Diamond League athletics meet in July, where Josh Kerr broke the world mile record. Thursday saw a bid confirmed to stage the 2029 World Athletics Championships, following an impasse between the club and the stadium owners. Further reminders that West Ham’s home will never be fully their own, 10 years after departing the Boleyn Ground.

Such were the terms Sullivan, Gold Sr and Brady agreed for a stadium that fans continue to resent, where Sullivan is unlikely to be made to feel welcome.

Sports.title: Jay-Z’s Roc Nation Sports making waves in European football transfer market
Sports.content:
In the end there was a clear winner. And Jay-Z’s latest victory came only 24 hours after the first record featuring him actually rapping for four years had been released by his wife, Beyoncé, on an extended remix pack of Morning Dew (Donk).

These days, the man who remains one of the most influential artists in hip-hop has his fingers in many pies, from the streaming service Tidal and his own streetwear brand, to champagne and cognac. But it is Roc Nation Sports – an offshoot of his entertainment company of the same name founded in 2008 – making headlines in the summer transfer window.

Established five years later in partnership with Creative Artists Agency, it began mainly representing players from the NBA, NFL and MLB, including Kevin Durant. Bayern Munich’s Jérôme Boateng was the first football client, in 2015, before Roc Nation Sports International (RNSI) was established four years later with a focus on stars at big European clubs.

Based in London, it now has more than 100 players on its books, including Vinícius Júnior – the Brazil forward who signed a lucrative new contract with Real Madrid this week believed to be worth around €25m. That came after Arsenal had been linked with a blockbuster move for the 26-year-old.

In July 2023 RNSI took over the successful Brazilian agents TFM – who already represented Vinícius, Gabriel Martinelli, and Endrick – and renamed it Roc Nation Sports Brazil.

In negotiations that have lasted two years, it had hoped to persuade Real to increase their star asset’s salary to €30m a year to match Kylian Mbappé, and allowed his contract to enter its final 12 months in an effort to drum up interest elsewhere. While Arsenal – now exploring other attacking options including Everton’s Iliman Ndiaye – are believed to have been willing to pay a big fee for Vinícius, it is understood that they thought signing him on a free transfer next season was more likely.

Nonetheless, Real upped their offer and Vinícius stayed. It is a decision that looks likely to cost them the chance to sign Rodri from Manchester City after Barcelona stole a march on their great rivals.

View image in fullscreen A phonecall from Vinícius Júnior reportedly led to Yan Diomande signing with Roc Nation Sports. Photograph: Kirsty Wigglesworth/AP

On the same day as the new six-year contract for Vinícius was announced, Yan Diomande flew to the Spanish capital to complete his record £115m transfer from RB Leipzig. The 19-year-old – who has made only 46 appearances at senior level for the German club and for Leganés in the Spanish second division but is already the most expensive African player in history – was pictured with his agents, Nathan Campbell and Kareem Gbaja on a private jet. RNSI has been reported to have been paid up to £17m in commission and fees.

A long-running saga that began when Liverpool had a £70m bid rejected by Leipzig in June ended with Diomande signing a seven-year deal at the Bernabéu on Thursday. It has provided a telling insight into the mechanisms of a modern transfer, with every week bringing a fresh twist. Having been told they must pay in excess of £100m to sign Diomande, Paris Saint-Germain withdrew from the race at the end of July after releasing a statement that said the European champions “will not engage in the inflationary and manipulative games of certain player agents”.

RNSI has also had to fend off two legal challenges, including one from the former Bournemouth winger Max Gradel who claims that his agency, Maxidel Management, had an existing agreement with Diomande. Gradel has filed a complaint with Fifa, although world football’s governing body did not block the player’s move to Real. Dez Bamba – who is president of Diomande’s first club, AFI Sud Comoé in Côte d’Ivoire – has said that the winger was persuaded to join RNSI after receiving a call from Vinícius. RNSI has not commented on the case.

Meanwhile, the Rainbow World Group instigated proceedings at the high court in London and the British Virgin Islands against Diomande in mid-June “to enforce binding image rights and intellectual property agreements tied to his early career development”. It is claimed Rainbow invested significant resources in the winger, including taking him for trials at Chelsea, Bournemouth, Crystal Palace and Newcastle before he was signed by Leganés. RNSI has not commented on the case.

Given Diomande’s meteoric rise, perhaps it is no surprise that clubs are flocking to invest in African academies.

Jeff Luhnow – the former general manager of the Astros and St Louis Cardinals who won three World Series baseball titles and owns Leganés as part of his Blue Crow network of clubs – told the Guardian last year Diomande was expected to be the first of many after they set up recruitment and development programmes in several African countries, including Ghana and Zambia, in the past several years. “We’ve got more players like that in our pipeline,” said Luhnow.

RNSI announced in November that it has signed eight young African stars, including the Ghana Under-17 midfielder Joseph Narbi and Francis Gomez, a Gambian winger currently at AC Horsens in Denmark. “We believe Africa is a hotbed of untapped footballing potential, and our expansion here is a natural progression of our global vision,” said Campbell.

In the dog-eat-dog world of football agents Jay Z’s new kids on the block are certainly making their presence felt.

Sports.title: Lucy Bronze backs Uefa’s stance on boycotting Fifa for ‘good of the game’
Sports.content:
Lucy Bronze has backed Uefa’s stance on boycotting all Fifa competitions for the “good of the game” and to safeguard football for future generations.

On Thursday Europe’s governing body doubled down on its threat – including next summer’s Women’s World Cup – amid the furore surrounding the Fifa president Gianni Infantino and his shelved plan for a privately funded Fifa Forward Enterprise scheme.

“The message that we stand by … is ‘for the good of the game’. The players who play in those competitions, the European players, we stand by our beliefs and what the right thing is for our game,” the 34-year-old Chelsea and England right-back said.

Bronze was speaking before Saturday’s pre-season friendly against Auckland FC at Eden Park. She was responding to a question by the New Zealand Herald whether it would be disappointing not to play in Fifa competitions.

She added: “If that means boycotting competitions, then that has to happen. It’s for the future of the game and not just for me today and tomorrow, it’s for all the little girls or little boys who come after us to make sure that they’re in a good place, when the game is moving forward in decades to come, not just tomorrow.”

Next summer’s tournament in Brazil could be the England defender’s fourth senior World Cup. The Lionesses have reached at least the semi-finals of her previous three. Her first global competition coincidentally came in New Zealand, when she helped England reach the semi-finals of the 2008 Under-17 Women’s World Cup.

Uefa’s threat of a boycott could have an impact on September’s Under-20 Women’s World Cup in Poland which is set to get under way in under a month’s time, with England due to line up in Group B alongside Brazil, Canada and Tanzania.

Meanwhile, Channel 4 has confirmed it will air the knockout stages of the Women’s African Cup of Nations live, with the quarter-finals and semi-finals to be streamed on its YouTube channel. The final to be shown live on E4. It will mark the first time that a UK broadcaster has shown the tournament live.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Elsewhere, the Football Association has appointed Sian Massey-Ellis as its new senior manager for women referees. Massey-Ellis became only the second woman to join the Premier League officials list in 2010 and has officiated at 150 top-flight matches, as well as five Women’s FA Cup finals. She was first female to officiate in a men’s FA Cup final.

Sports.title: Norway’s Klaveness tells Fifa president Infantino to resign: ‘There is no trust now’
Sports.content:
The Norwegian FA will ask Gianni Infantino to resign with immediate effect after his doomed attempt to sell stakes in the World Cup to private investors.

Norway is the first federation to call directly for the Fifa president to step down after a series of controversies that came to a head with the crisis engulfing his Fifa Forward Enterprise scheme.

The decision was made at a meeting of the Norwegian Football Federation board (NFF) on Thursday night. Norway has consistently taken a lead in efforts to scrutinise Fifa’s governance and recent events have taken any faith in its leadership beyond the point of no return.

“We decided that there is no trust in Infantino now,” the NFF president, Lise Klaveness, told the Guardian. “We have been worried consistently and there has been one more step in a worrying direction every year, every part of the year. The trust is now gone for us, there is no way back for Infantino.

“We’re left in a very polarised cooperation globally and, I would say, chaos. So we will ask him to resign immediately so that the global football community can look ahead and cooperate going into the future.”

The NFF is expected to formally write a letter requesting Infantino’s resignation in the coming week. Norway was among a handful of countries not to back his re-election as president next March, although several European federations have withdrawn their endorsement in the past week.

“We understand that we’re one country, but it’s our position,” Klaveness said. “It’s just one step further for us. We did not vote for him in 2023 but we hoped we would support him, he was elected and the reason why we were so clear in our statements was to really give the signal that we wanted him to implement the good reforms he was part of. But he didn’t, and now we will ask him to resign.”

The NFF agreed to demand a full review into the package of reforms passed upon Infantino’s ascent to the presidency in 2016, which were intended to extricate Fifa from the corruption crisis that had previously dogged the governing body. Klaveness said the investigation should ask “what was implemented, what was not, what should have been implemented and what we should also implement to make this a functioning organisation”.

Norway will also formalise a fresh complaint to Fifa’s ethics committee on three fronts, taking in the FFE scandal, the award of Fifa’s peace prize to Donald Trump and the Folarin Balogun affair at the World Cup. It will attempt to bring a number of major European federations on board for its submission in an effort to further increase the pressure on Infantino.

“We want the ethics committee to show their work transparently because this is a very big part of the issue,” Klaveness said. “There are all kinds of control mechanisms in place but they are not really holding the council and president accountable.”

View image in fullscreen Gianni Infantino leaves after attending the Women’s Africa Cup of Nations match between Malawi and Zambia in Rabat. Photograph: AP

In June, the NFF wrote to the ethics committee supporting a complaint by the advocacy group FairSquare, which centred on alleged breaches of political neutrality by Infantino. It will now make a new submission that asks for the three situations to be considered individually. “We will join them in one letter but they are very different cases and we want the ethical committee to treat them separately,” Klaveness said.

The NFF is understood to have particular concerns that the timing of Infantino’s FFE offer, which promised federations significant financial gains if accepted, may constitute an abuse of position at this proximity to a presidential election. It has also been observed that the FFE scheme, had it been passed, would have locked in commitments extending well beyond Infantino’s term.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to The Recap The best of our sports journalism from the past seven days and a heads-up on the weekend’s action Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

As with its call for Infantino to step down, Norway is the first federation to adopt a public stance regarding the peace prize or the Balogun case. Fifa’s decision to suspend the USA striker’s red card during the World Cup, meaning he was free to face Belgium in the last 16, came after Trump had called Infantino to discuss the ban.

Uefa’s federations have stood together in backing a potential boycott of Fifa competitions, a stance Uefa reasserted on Thursday despite Infantino’s shelving of FFE. Klaveness said the move is not merely symbolic and is intended to bring swift results.

“There’s no point in Uefa standing in a war position for half a year,” she said. “That would not be good at all. Now it’s crucial that we do it because global football cooperation is at stake. It’s very good to see we have strong leadership in Uefa that knows now is crunch time for this case. We cannot sell out this core of football.”

The first competition in line for a boycott would be the Under-20 Women’s World Cup, which is due to start in Poland on 5 September, but Klaveness expects the continued turmoil to have been resolved by then.

“I hope and think it will not come to that,” she said. “A lot of water will go under the bridge before that. But this is why we ask Infantino to resign. It’s so unstable now that it’s a matter of time. He cannot recover this and we cannot put the sport on the spot. The biggest priority is to be together with Uefa and have this strong position.”

Klaveness and the NFF have held a consistent line in calling for scrutiny of Fifa’s operations since she assumed her position in March 2022. She has been vocal on human rights issues and governance standards within Fifa, criticising failings surrounding the Qatar World Cup and questioning the process that awarded Saudi Arabia the 2034 edition of the tournament.

Sports.title: Manchester City reject Barcelona’s opening £38.5m bid for Rodri as talks continue
Sports.content:
Manchester City have rejected an offer of £38.5m (€45m) from Barcelona for Rodri and want at least £60m before allowing Spain’s World Cup-winning captain to depart.

Barcelona have emerged as Rodri’s preferred destination after talks with Real Madrid broke down this week. It is understood that the 30-year-old, who is now in the final year of his contract at City, has agreed personal terms with the Spanish champions after indicating that he would like to return to his homeland following the departure of Pep Guardiola.

Rodri moved to the Etihad in 2019 from Atlético Madrid and has turned down the offer of a lucrative extension. Yet City are believed to be adamant that he will not be allowed to leave for less than their asking price. Barcelona are continuing negotiations in the hope of reaching a compromise.

Rodri, who won the World Cup Golden Ball as the tournament’s best player last month, spoke to Barça’s manager, Hansi Flick, and sporting director, Deco, about a potential move on Wednesday.

The Spanish champions will be without Frenkie de Jong for several months after the Netherlands midfielder sustained a knee injury and have targeted Rodri as a replacement. He has had minor surgery on his back and will miss most of City’s pre-season programme.

City have signed Elliot Anderson from Nottingham Forest for £116m and remain in negotiations with Lille over a deal for Ayyoub Bouaddi. The Morocco midfielder could cost up to £80m but they could be tempted to bring in a more experienced replacement for Rodri should he depart, with Chelsea’s Enzo Fernández among those thought to be under consideration. The 25-year-old is also wanted by Real, whose manager, José Mourinho is said to not to have the news of being gazumped by their great rivals well. Reports in Spain have claimed that the 63-year-old is unhappy after making the signing of a central midfielder his priority on returning for a second stint at the Santiago Bernabéu.

Real have already brought in the winger Yan Diomande for £115m and Marc Cucurella, Bernardo Silva, Ibrahima Konaté, Denzel Dumfries and Carlos Espí, so they may have to balance the books by selling either Aurélien Tchouaméni and Eduardo Camavinga if they want to pursue Argentinian Fernández.

Crystal Palace have confirmed the signing of Takehiro Tomiyasu after a successful trial period. The former Arsenal defender has been training with Palace during pre-season and has done enough to earn an initial 12-month deal with the option of extending that by another two years. Tomiyasu becomes new manager Pierre Sage’s second signing of the summer after the arrival of Óscar Mingueza on a free transfer. Palace are expected to complete a deal for the USA youth international Zavier Gozo from Real Salt Lake in MLS.

Sports.title: Tottenham and Atlético in talks over Romero with Van de Ven set to sign new deal
Sports.content:
Tottenham are in talks with Atlético Madrid over the sale of Cristian Romero after categorically rejecting Arsenal’s approach for the Argentina defender and are expected to agree a new five-year deal with Micky van de Ven.

Romero has made no secret of his desire to leave Spurs despite signing a new four-year contract at the start of last season and had looked set to join Inter for a fee of around £35m. But Atlético are long-term suitors of the 28-year-old and are thought to be his preferred destination, with Diego Simeone’s side understood to be prepared to match Inter’s bid.

Reports in Spain on Friday suggested that personal terms have already been agreed with Romero, although his move may have to wait for Atlético to free up space in their squad before they can complete the transfer. Nahuel Molina, Romero’s Argentina teammate, is expected to join Roma while Aston Villa are hoping to sign Matteo Ruggeri.

Arsenal had also made their interest known as they search for a replacement for William Saliba, with the Frenchman out for an extended period due to a back issue. However, Tottenham – who have signed defenders Jan Paul van Hecke and Marcos Senesi this summer – insisted that they did not want to sell to another Premier League club, least of all their north London rivals. Arsenal are also interested in Villa’s Ezri Konsa.

It is understood that Van de Ven had been considering his future in north London at the start of the summer after Tottenham narrowly avoided relegation last season. But the impact of the new manager, Roberto De Zerbi, has persuaded the Netherlands international to commit his future to the club after talks with his representatives.

Tottenham have already spent more than £200m on six new players this summer and are still in the market for a new attacker. Last week, De Zerbi said that they had “completed 60% of our project in the transfer market”.

Sports.title: Liverpool in surprise loan deal to sign Barcelona centre-back as Ibrahima Konate replacement
Sports.content:
Liverpool in surprise loan deal to sign Barcelona centre-back as Ibrahima Konate replacement

Liverpool have agreed a deal to sign Ronald Araujo on loan from Barcelona, talkSPORT understands.

The surprise transfer comes amid the Reds' lack of depth at centre-back, with Ibrahima Konate leaving earlier this summer.



3 Araujo is set to join Liverpool on loan in a surprise transfer Credit: Getty

Konate departed the club for Real Madrid, signing on a free transfer after his contract at Anfield expired.

It means Virgil van Dijk, new signing Jeremy Jacquet, Joe Gomez and Giovanni Leoni are the only senior centre-backs in the squad.

So, Andoni Iraola has been keen to bring in an experienced head with the new Premier League season just two weeks away.



A verbal agreement is in place between Barcelona and Liverpool, and Araujo is now set to spend the season in England.

It's understood that the deal is a loan without a buy option.

Araujo on the move

Araujo played 38 games in all competitions last season for Barca, helping lead them as captain to the La Liga title.



In total for the Spanish giants, he's played 213 games across a seven-year span in the first team following his arrival in 2018.

During his spell, he has won three league titles, two Copa Del Reys and three Spanish Super Cups.



The 27-year-old has spent the majority of his career in Spain, only playing for Uruguayan teams Boston River and Rentistas before.

Araujo has also picked up 27 Uruguay caps during his six-year international career, being part of their squad at the World Cup this summer.

3 Araujo departs Barcelona after winning eight trophies and playing over 200 games Credit: Getty

Fourth summer signing

Liverpool are now on the brink of securing their fourth signing of the summer transfer window since Iraola's appointment.



They have already confirmed Jacquet's £60m pre-agreed move.

Meanwhile, Spanish winger Victor Munoz has also joined the club for £35m and teenager Ifeanyi Ndukwe has signed too.

Araujo is set to join them in arriving at Anfield, while the Reds have continuously been linked with Bradley Barcola.

Barcola wants to join the club from Paris Saint-Germain this summer, with Liverpool expected to pursue him.

Tottenham and England's Djed Spence has been linked too, but talkSPORT understands Liverpool are not currently in for him.



3 Araujo will be Liverpool's fourth signing of the summer transfer window Credit: Getty

Mental health break

Liverpool-bound Araujo was granted a leave of absence by Barcelona last season to take a break for his mental health.

He began his break at the start of December last year before returning 'stronger' midway through January.

Posting on social media at the time of his return, with Barca lifting the Spanish Supercopa, the defender said: "I learned that stopping at the right time is self-love."



"Taking care of your mind and heart is not giving up, it is trusting that God works even in silence. Stopping renewed me and allowed me to come back stronger.

"The process was not easy, but coming back like this is a privilege.

"Thank you to the club, my teammates and the fans for their treatment, affection and respect. It was beautiful to return lifting this trophy. We continue together."

Sports.title: Newcastle eye former Tottenham midfielder as shock target amid Bruno Guimaraes sale
Sports.content:
Newcastle are interested in signing ex-Tottenham midfielder Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg, talkSPORT understands.

Hojbjerg is viewed as a budget option that will add experience to the squad as Bruno Guimaraes nears a switch to Arsenal.

3 Hojbjerg could potentially be a replacement for Guimaraes at Newcastle Credit: Getty

Captain Guimaraes is set to depart the Magpies and join the Gunners after a £75million deal was finally agreed.

He will follow Sandro Tonali and Anthony Gordon out the door, while manager Eddie Howe also resigned from his post.

Matthias Jaissle has replaced Howe in the dugout, with this summer becoming one of major change for Newcastle.

And to make up for the loss of some of their key stars and boss, they're going to need some renewed leadership.

Eyeing experience

Hojbjerg could be their chosen man, with the former Spurs player said to be available for around £10m to 15m.

The 31-year-old midfielder played 43 games for Marseille last season, scoring five goals and assisting another five.

But it's his Premier League experience that Newcastle will be attracted to most.

Hojbjerg has played 254 top-flight games in his career - last playing in England for Tottenham in the 2023/24 campaign.

He played 145 times for Spurs in the Premier League during his four-year stay, while also featuring 109 times for Southampton between 2016-2020.

In total, the Denmark international has completed eight seasons in the league, so he won't be unfamiliar should he return.

3 Newcastle want experience and Hojbjerg has played over 250 Premier League games Credit: AFP

Guimaraes latest

Guimaraes has not been confirmed to have left for Arsenal yet, but it's understood that the Brazilian is set to be announced imminently.

Mikel Arteta identified him as a priority target this summer, and after a long saga, the deal has now been agreed.

The 28-year-old left Newcastle's training camp earlier this week to undergo a medical ahead of the move.

He will become Arsenal's fourth summer signing, following Christos Tzolis and Illan Meslier through the door.

Piero Hincapie also made his loan from last season permanent.

As for Newcastle, they're going to have more cash to splash once Guimaraes eventually leaves the club.

3 Guimaraes is set to join Arsenal after a £75m deal was agreed this week Credit: Getty

Hojbjerg is a target to use up to £15m on, while they have already spent nearly £150m on signings in the window.

Bazoumana Toure joined from Hoffenheim for £43m, with Aladji Bamba signing for £34m and Lucas Hornicek for £25.7m.

Sean Steur and Ewen Jaouen also joined for a combined £41m.

Sports.title: Arsenal player confirms ACL rupture in heartbreaking statement as Declan Rice reacts
Sports.content:
Arsenal youngster Louie Copley has confirmed that he has suffered an ACL rupture during pre-season duty.

Copley was making his second senior outing for the Gunners on Wednesday as he featured in a 3-1 defeat to Spanish side Real Betis.

2 Copley suffered an ACL rupture playing for Arsenal against Real Betis Credit: Getty

But just nine minutes into his substitute appearance, the 19-year-old suffered a horrible injury, receiving lengthy treatment.

He eventually hobbled off the pitch, with manager Mikel Arteta revealing he was concerned about Copley post-match.

Arteta said: "We’re quite worried for the kid because the mechanism doesn’t look very positive, the symptoms that he already has.

"So we’re going to have to wait and see for tomorrow’s scan. And yeah, touch wood that he’s not that bad."

'Words can’t describe how I’m feeling'

Unfortunately for Arteta and the Gunners though, Copley has revealed some devastating news in a heartbreaking statement.

On Friday, he posted on Instagram: "Words can’t describe how I’m feeling right now, to making my pre-season debut for the team I’ve grown up supporting to finding out I’ve ruptured my ACL.

"The road ahead won’t be easy but I’ll give everything to come back stronger and better."

Plenty of the Arsenal squad have reacted to Copley's emotional post, replying with their support for the teenage starlet.

Declan Rice replied with a love heart emoji, with Ben White, Max Dowman and Tommy Setford all doing the same.

Jurrien Timber also commented with a praying emoji.

2 Arteta's worst fears were realised as Copley confirmed a serious injury Credit: Getty

Devastating blow

Copley will have hoped to make a big step in his professional career this campaign, having been part of Arsenal's pre-season.

He came off the bench against Girona for his maiden first-team appearance earlier in pre-season, playing 20 minutes.

And then he also featured against Betis, but after being brought on at half-time, his injury saw him taken off soon after.

Copley had appeared on the bench in the Champions League for Arsenal' last season for a clash against 's 3-0 league phase victory over Club Brugge.

The academy product then spent the second half of the campaign on loan at Crawley Town, featuring nine times in League Two.

Sadly, he's now expected to be sidelined for a large part of the upcoming season in what is a huge blow.

Sports.title: Man City set to re-sign World Cup winner immediately after selling James Trafford
Sports.content:
Manchester City are set to sign goalkeeper Geronimo Rulli from Marseille following James Trafford's exit, talkSPORT understands.

Trafford became Leeds United's highest-paid player after completing a club-record £40million move to Elland Road on Thursday.

3 Man City are set to bring in World Cup-winning goalkeeper Rulli Credit: Getty

He had struggled for minutes at City and was unable to displace Gianluigi Donnarumma in goal under Pep Guardiola.

So, the England international opted to move on and sign for their Premier League rivals.

And with Donnarumma expected to continue as Enzo Maresca's No.1, City were left needing to bring in a replacement.

But just a day later, they've struck a deal with Marseille to bring in a new No.2 goalkeeper for a fee in the region of £2.5m.

Rulli is expected to sign a two-year contract at the club with the option for an additional year, talkSPORT understands.

He is set to fly for a medical ahead of the move to Manchester.

Immediate replacement

Man City have swooped in to get a deal done for Rulli instantly after losing their back-up in Trafford to Leeds.

And now, the 34-year-old is set to be Donnarumma's understudy, arriving at City for what is actually his second stint.

He was signed by the club in 2016, but never played a game, leaving to return to his old side Real Sociedad almost straight away.

Rulli has spent the last two seasons with Marseille in France, starting 29 Ligue 1 games last campaign, keeping eight clean sheets.

3 Rulli (left), who was back-up to Emi Martinez at the World Cup this summer, will now be Donnarumma's No.2 Credit: Getty

The year prior, he started 34 games and kept five clean sheets.

Before joining Marseille in 2024, he spent a year in the Netherlands with Ajax, whom he joined from Spanish side Villarreal.

The goalkeeper had been in LaLiga for six years before that, having three different spells at Sociedad in his career.

Rulli started his career in Argentina with Estudiantes - and he's picked up eight caps playing for his country since 2016.

World Cup winner

Despite only playing eight games for Argentina over the last decade, he has become a World Cup winner with his nation.

The veteran was part of the successful squad in 2022 as Lionel Messi finally got his hands on the Jules Rimet trophy in Qatar.

3 Rulli replaces Trafford after he joined Leeds for £40m Credit: Getty

Rulli didn't play a game at the tournament, but still managed to taste the success that so many players dream of.

He was also in the 26-man set-up for Argentina again this summer, but they were beaten in the World Cup final by Spain.

Sports.title: Cristian Romero is one of the worst ever Premier League captain’s – he’s got serious anger issues
Sports.content:
Cristian Romero is one of the worst ever Premier League captain’s – he’s got serious anger issues

Cristian Romero has been labelled as one of the worst captains in Premier League history amid his impending Tottenham exit.

Those are the views of ex-Liverpool striker Dean Saunders and former Aston Villa forward Gabby Agbonlahor, who have slammed the Spurs star for his behaviour last season.



4 Romero was appointed as Spurs' captain last summer following Son Heung-min's departure Credit: Getty

Romero and Spurs finished in 17th place for the second straight top-flight campaign last term, which was his first as captain.

He played 23 games and received two red cards, also getting embroiled in a controversy at the end of the season.

The feisty centre-back flew to Argentina despite Tottenham having a must-win relegation clash on the final day.



Then, over the summer, he was involved in some World Cup chaos that saw his nation majorly criticised for their actions.

All of those factors led to Saunders calling him one of the worst skippers to have ever played in the Premier League.



He said on talkSPORT Breakfast: "Romero is up there with one of the worst captains in the history of the Premier League.

"Spurs have finished 17th and 17th, two years running. He was the captain so he can't be that good can he?



"And he's an absolute liability on the pitch. He's a walking red card and his behaviour in the World Cup after the whistle went sums him up."

Agbonlahor slams 'shocking' Romero

Agbonlahor agreed with Saunders' take on Romero when reacting to his comments on Drive on Friday afternoon.

"I think it's fair," the former England forward said, also criticising the Spurs defender. "As a captain, you have to be reliable.

4 Agbonlahor agreed with Saunders' claim that Romero is a 'liability' on the pitch Credit: Getty



"A captain is a role that's a privilege, you should be going around in the game and training ground setting standards.

"He's not the kind of captain you want...if you're struggling in a game you're not looking at him to lift you. He'd probably go and get sent off."

Agbonlahor added: "I think he's a liability...when he's at it, especially for Argentina, he's a top defender, but something about his ego says to be he thinks he's better than Spurs.

"I think he thinks Spurs are beneath him, the way he tried to stay in Argentina for the last game of the season, he probably got forced by his agent to get back.



"He's a liability, he's got anger issues, he should see someone about that because some of the tackles and red cards he got over his career have been shocking.

"I think in the Premier League now, you need to be able to trust all 22, 23 players not to give a silly red card away."

4 Romero has never been sent off for Argentina but has six reds for Spurs Credit: Getty

Agbonlahor continued to rip into Romero, questioning the 28-year-old's short fuse and differing attitude with club and country.



"Football has changed," he said. "It's different to 20 years ago when if someone's annoying you, you can leave one on them.

"You can't do it anymore, how many times has he done it? He's got frustrated by someone and left a bit on them and got sent off.

"You shouldn't do it anyway, but when you're captain and in your late 20s...

"He's good at tackling when it suits him - 40 caps for Argentina and zero red cards, but for Spurs six red cards, that says it all."



And now, Romero is set to leave Tottenham after five years...

4 The Spurs skipper is set to join Atletico after agreeing personal terms Credit: Getty

On the way out

Tottenham captain Romero has agreed personal terms to join Atletico Madrid, talkSPORT understands.

He held talks with Inter Milan this summer and was even linked to a shock move to north London rivals Arsenal.

But now, he looks set to be heading to Spain - and that's a move that Agbonlahor thinks suits him to a tee.



Diego Simeone's Atletico have become renowned for their aggressive approach on the pitch over the years....

"If there's a team that suit Romero, it's Atletico Madrid," he said.

"If there was a bet I could put on that he'd get the most red cards, it'd be on him."

Sports.title: Aston Villa could wait until end of window to make move for Premier League striker
Sports.content:
Aston Villa could wait until end of window to make move for Premier League striker

Aston Villa could delay trying to sign Nicolas Jackson until the end of the transfer window due to UEFA rules, talkSPORT understands.

The Villans have been heavily linked with a move for Jackson, who is free to leave Chelsea and is valued at around £65million.



4 Nicolas Jackson is currently away on Chelsea's pre-season tour of Australia and Asia Credit: Getty

Having spent the 2025/26 campaign away from Stamford Bridge on loan at Bayern Munich, the Senegal international now looks set for a clean break from the Blues.

Villa aren't the only club being tipped to make a play for Jackson, with Spurs also linked with the striker.

But with Unai Emery's side keen to strengthen after some high-profile departures - namely Morgan Rogers and Youri Tielemans - they could be interested in doing business with Chelsea again.



Knowing major sales would be required this summer to avoid falling foul of UEFA's financial restrictions, Villa sanctioned the departure of Rogers to the Blues for a British record £117million.

That wasn't the end of the two clubs' deals either, as Alejandro Garnacho then headed to Villa Park on loan.



talkSPORT previously reported that the Argentina international had been offered to Villa alongside Jackson in the wake of their deal to sign Rogers.

And while a move for the Chelsea striker remains a possibility, talkSPORT's Ben Jacobs has now revealed there are some obstacles that could delay any deal until later this summer.



Financial constraints

According to UEFA's transfer rules, multiple deals completed between the same clubs within a 45-day period is classified as a swap.

With Rogers heading to Stamford Bridge at the end of July, Villa and Chelsea still find themselves within this window.

This means that, if Villa were to sign Jackson now, they would have to reduce the profit made from the Rogers sale to the difference between that figure and how much was paid for Jackson.

4 Morgan Rogers joined Chelsea as their club-record signing Credit: Getty



4 Alejandro Garnacho linked up with the Villans on an initial loan deal shortly later Credit: Getty

Villa were able to avoid a similar situation with Garnacho by signing the winger on an initial loan deal with a conditional obligation to buy.

Speaking on talkSPORT's Transfer Insiders, reporter Ben Jacobs explained how the Midlands outfit could now bide their time over Jackson, in order to comply with UEFA rules.

Jacobs explained: “Villa do like Nicolas Jackson.

“We heard some reports that Tottenham were in - that's not my understanding. Spurs sources are denying that they're going to bid for Nicolas Jackson.



“And then if Villa are going to move, maybe the reason why there's no movement is; if both clubs are to reflect Morgan Rogers and should Jackson go to Villa, Nicolas Jackson [would go] positively on their books, because when you do these sales, you can take that transfer fee and you can put it on your annual books, and then if you've got an outlay, you can amortise it, which makes it a bit more palatable.

“But under the new UEFA rules, you can't do these mirrored or separate deals within a 45 day window."

4 Jackson has 30 goals in 81 games in a Chelsea shirt Credit: Getty

Jacobs explained: “If you roughly go back to when Morgan Rogers [moved to Chelsea], depending on when it was actually signed, and Chelsea might not have known that Villa were going to bid or potentially proceed with Jackson.



“But if you go back to that deal roughly, if it is to fall outside of a 45- day window, then it would likely suit both Villa and Chelsea to do that deal right at the end of the window, because we're definitely still within that 45-day period now."

Jacobs claimed UEFA restrictions have likely delayed any move by Villa for Jackson, while he also pointed to the striker's situation at Chelsea.

With new boss Xabi Alonso keen to take a look at the 25-year-old before sanctioning a sale, he has joined up with the Blues squad for their pre-season tour of Australia and Asia.

However, he still faces an uncertain future following the arrival of veteran striker Danny Welbeck from Brighton.



Jacobs continued: “Maybe that's why we haven't had any update on Nicholas Jackson's future, coupled with the fact that Xabi Alonso has just needed to see particularly both [Liam] Delap and Jackson in preseason before maybe inputting which one of them, or potentially both, he wants to depart.”

Sports.title: Trailblazing Premier League official Sian Massey-Ellis retires and instantly lands new job
Sports.content:
Premier League assistant referee Sian Massey-Ellis has announced her immediate retirement from officiating.

The trailblazing sideline official will now begin work as the Football Association's (FA) Senior Manager of Women Referees.

3 Massey-Ellis never wilted in the face of criticism from players Credit: Getty

Massey-Ellis' new role centres on supporting and developing the ever-growing pool of female officials in addition to inspiring the next generation.

Massey-Ellis: 'Greatest honour to serve the game'

“From standing beneath the Premier League sign before my very first match to officiating at FIFA World Cups, UEFA European Championships, Champions League finals and across domestic fixtures and competitions in England, football has taken me on a journey beyond anything I could ever have imagined," Massey-Ellis said in a statement.

"Every opportunity has been a privilege and one I have never taken for granted.

“Throughout my career, football has challenged me, tested my resilience and pushed me to become a better professional and person.

"While there have been unforgettable highs and difficult moments, what I will treasure most are the people and experiences that have defined my journey.

"I am incredibly grateful to Pro Ref, The FA, FIFA and UEFA for the opportunities they gave me, as well as every coach, mentor, colleague and match official I have had the privilege of working alongside.

"Above all, I owe an enormous debt of thanks to my family, whose unwavering support, sacrifices and belief made every achievement possible.

“Although I am stepping away from the touchline, I am not stepping away from football.

"If my journey has helped change perceptions, open doors or inspire even one young person to believe they belong in the game, then I will consider that one of my greatest achievements.

"I'm excited by the opportunity to help support, develop and inspire the next generation of match officials, giving something back to a sport that has done so much for me.

3 The 40-year-old begins her new role in September Credit: Getty

“As I prepare for one final walk onto the pitch, I leave with nothing but gratitude. It has been the greatest honour to serve the game I love and represent English officiating.

"To the young girl who simply loved refereeing and dreamed of reaching the very top - we did it.

"Thank you, football."

Pro Ref Chief Refereeing Officer Howard Webb added Massey-Ellis 'has been nothing short of a powerhouse' over the course of her officiating career.

"She has done us proud time and time again - domestically and on the international stage, breaking multiple barriers and setting the standard for those coming through in her footsteps," Webb added.

History-making

Massey-Ellis hangs up the flag having become just the second female to be an assistant referee in Premier League history, with Wendy Toms the first to do so.

3 Massey-Ellis has paved the way for the next generation of female officials Credit: Getty

She went on to be the first female involved in the men's FA Cup final and the Community Shield.

Massey-Ellis was also a trailblazer internationally, becoming the first female selected to officiate a men's European match when she was an assistant referee for a Europa League fixture in 2019.

She also represented England at four UEFA Women's Euro tournaments as well as the 2019 and 2023 FIFA Women's World Cups.

The 40-year-old's vast achievements on the sideline earned her an MBE in 2017 for her services to football.

Sports.title: World Cup winner showcases incredible physique aged 56 and gives fans achievable workout tip
Sports.content:
France legend Bixente Lizarazu has done it all in his career and now he's handing out top workout tips to his fans on social media.

The ex-Bayern Munich star, now 56, won it all as a player.

2 Lizarazu lifts the World Cup in 1998 Credit: Getty Images - Getty

He scooped the Champions League, European Championship, World Cup and six Bundesliga titles, plus the Intercontinental Cup and individual awards from UEFA and FIFA.

And the left-back did it in the era of Roberto Carlos too.

Since retiring in 2006, Lizarazu hasn't taken his foot off the gas, rather he's put his foot to the floor.

Had his Weet-a-Bix

By 2009 he was a European Champion, this time in the sport of Brazilian jiu jitsu.

He won it in the Blue Belt Senior 1 Light Division.

His physical ability has always been of repute with Zinedine Zidane once claiming only Lizarazu could have stopped him getting sent off in the 2006 World Cup final.

Not only did the 97-cap France legend take to BJJ, he has also been surfing, skiing, diving and cycling in his retirement.

And now he's showcased his outrageous physique once more, this time warning his fans to look after their bodies.

He posted a workout video on Instagram where he only used his bodyweight or small weights.

With it, Lizarazu insisted that with age it's important to stop your body losing muscle, but that doesn't mean you have to lift heavy.

He said in the caption: "Weight training is important after 40, essential after 50… after that, I don't know, we'll see!

"My goal isn't to gain muscle, but to avoid losing it.

"Are you familiar with sarcopenia?

"It's the progressive loss of muscle mass and strength, mainly due to aging. We all go through it, sooner or later…

"So it's good to have a complete, personalized weight training protocol.

"I have several.

2 Lizarazu is one of the best left-backs in football history Credit: getty images

"You'll notice that I only use small equipment (dumbbells, kettlebells, TRX, bodyweight)."

A host of former players hailed him in the comments with ex-Liverpool and France star Djibril Cisse saying simply: "Incredible."

Ex-Lyon and Nice star Anthony Mounier added: "Transfer window time!! If any club is looking for a left-back, I know one who's still available."

And former France goalkeeper Gregory Coupet said: "Beautiful animal."

Sports.title: Powerlifting racism row: Spotter declares 'I am racist' after sabotaging star's record attempt - admitting in astonishing social media post: 'I did it intentionally'
Sports.content:
Powerlifting racism row: Spotter declares 'I am racist' after sabotaging star's record attempt - admitting in astonishing social media post: 'I did it intentionally'

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

A powerlifting assistant is under police investigation in Lithuania after claiming he deliberately sabotaged a Black athlete's squat attempt because he is 'racist'.

Belgian athlete Sonita Muluh's attempt to squat 334.5kg at the World Classic Open Powerlifting Championships in Lithuania in June was disqualified after spotting assistant Ernestas Kusinas placed his knee under the barbell during the lift.

After the event, Kusinas sparked outrage by claiming in an Instagram post that he had deliberately sabotaged Muluh's lift because he is 'racist', a remark he later insisted was intended to mock those accusing him of racism.

The Lithuanian Powerlifting Federation referred the case to police, who have launched an investigation into both the Instagram post and the events at the championships, a spokesperson told Reuters.

The Instagram remark read: 'Sorry for you morons, I'm racist and I did it on purpose because I hate you pieces of s***'.

If found guilty, Kusinas could face a maximum sentence of two years in prison.

Powerlifting assistant Ernestas Kusinas (above) is under police investigation in Lithuania after claiming he deliberately sabotaged a Black athlete's squat attempt because he is 'racist'

The spotter placed his knee on the barbell during Sonita Muluh's attempt to squat 334.5kg

Kusinas later told Reuters the Instagram post was written in anger and was intended to mock social media users who had accused him of racism, rather than reflect his true views.

The spotter claimed he had unintentionally interfered with Muluh's attempt as a result of being tired from his duties at the event.

Kusinas, who has since been banned for life from all powerlifting events by the Lithuanian federation and switched his social media accounts to private, claimed he had 'thrown him the bone he wanted' in response to an unidentified Instagram user who had accused him of racism.

Muluh, 29, became world champion in 2024 and has won medals at multiple Powerlifting Championships throughout her impressive career.

The Cameroon-born powerlifter's partner Kristof De ​Coninck urged that she could have won the event in Lithuania without Kusinas' interference, insisting poor assistance risked 'very serious injuries'.

'Initially, we thought it was a mistake,' De Coninck said.

'But then, it became clear (because of the social media comment) that the person had done it ⁠deliberately, motivated ​by racial bias.'

Speaking to BBC Sport about the controversy, Muluh said: 'It's shocking to wake up five weeks later and it's all over the internet that he did it on purpose because of the colour of my skin.

'I feel unsafe and uneasy that this person is standing beside me with massive weight, with what can go wrong, with the amount of weight on your back.

'I was lucky when I realised [it hit his knee] and I could stabilise it. Not everyone could. It was the heaviest ever squat for a female.

'(Kusinas) did not reach out afterwards to apologise, but he is not obliged to. I thought it was a human mistake, that cost me a lot on the day.

In an Instagram post after the event, he claimed he did it intentionally because he is 'racist'

Muluh, pictured in 2025, admitted she feels 'unsafe and uneasy' after his Instagram comment

'But there was no hatred [from me]. I didn't lash out; didn't curse at him. There was a video of it posted afterwards and I said: "I hope he does not get hate." I believed it was an honest mistake.

'And then I find out five weeks later that he said this.'

Meanwhile, the Lithuanian Powerlifting Federation has said in a statement: 'We would like to address the situation that unfolded on social media.

'We reviewed available information relating to Ernestas Kusinas and were deeply shocked by the views and activities addressed publicly which contradict the principles we stand for.

'The federation takes full responsibility for addressing this matter.'

Sports.title: Liverpool agree surprise loan move for Barcelona captain Ronald Araujo as Andoni Iraola looks to bolster injury-hit defence
Sports.content:
Liverpool have agreed a surprise deal for Barcelona defender Ronald Araujo to join on loan for the season.

Primarily a central defender, Araujo would also provide cover at right back for Jeremie Frimpong and Conor Bradley, whose knee injury is set to continue sidelining him for the opening months of the 2026-27 season.

The deal is a straight loan for the 27-year-old, who signed a new contract until 2031 last year.

The centre back will add to Andoni Iraola's options at the heart of his defence following the departure of Ibrahima Konate to Real Madrid and fitness concerns over relatively inexperienced 21-year-old Jeremy Jacquet.

The summer signing from Rennes has made fewer than 100 senior career appearances and has not featured in pre-season yet after missing the second half of last season following shoulder surgery.

Joe Gomez suffered a muscle injury in Liverpool's opening pre-season game, while teenage centre back Giovanni Leoni is still recovering from an ACL injury, leaving captain Virgil van Dijk as Liverpool's only fully fit senior centre back.

Liverpool have agreed a surprise deal to sign Barcelona captain Ronald Araujo on loan

The Uruguayan led Barcelona to the LaLiga title last term, but is set for a move to Anfield

The Uruguay international joined Barcelona B in 2018 before being promoted to the first team in 2019.

He has made more than 200 appearances for Barcelona but finds himself down the pecking order in Spain, with the likes of Pau Cubarsi and Gerard Martin ahead of him.

Araujo has therefore taken up the opportunity to move to the Premier League, with more than two weeks still to go until Liverpool's first game of the competitive season.

The 6ft 3in central defender was at the World Cup with Uruguay and was sent off when Barcelona lost 3-0 at Stamford Bridge against Chelsea in the Champions League in November.

He didn't play a minute for his country in North America, though, as he was injured in training and didn't recover in time to feature before Marcelo Bielsa's side were knocked out in the group stage.

The Reds will face Monaco on Sunday in pre-season and then Cesc Fabregas's Como a week later, before starting their campaign against Newcastle on August 23.

Araujo will become the third major arrival at Anfield after the signings of Jacquet and winger Victor Munoz.

Sports.title: Rodri tells Real Madrid he wishes to join Barcelona while Aston Villa strike agreement with Atletico Madrid star in move that could help push Cristian Romero closer to Spain move: WINDOW WATCH
Sports.content:
Rodri tells Real Madrid he wishes to join Barcelona while Aston Villa strike agreement with Atletico Madrid star in move that could help push Cristian Romero closer to Spain move: WINDOW WATCH

It's that time of the year again – the transfer window is now open until September 1 and it's sure to be a busy period with clubs looking to make big signings ahead of next season.

Here are today's latest developments from Simon Jones and the Daily Mail Sport team...

Aston Villa agree move for Ruggeri

Atletico Madrid left-back Matteo Ruggeri has agreed to join Aston Villa.

The 24-year-old Italian will cost £16m plus add-ons.

His transfer will help pave the way for Atletico to bid for Tottenham captain Cristian Romero.

Atletico Madrid's 24-year-old left-back Matteo Ruggeri has agreed to join Aston Villa

West Ham back in for Solomon

West Ham have revived talks with Tottenham over a deal for winger Manor Solomon.

Talks initially broke down over bonuses due if West Ham were promoted which the Championship side thought were unreasonable but the clubs are working towards a £10m agreement.

Hojbjerg is Newcastle's surprise midfield target

Newcastle United are interested in former Tottenham midfielder Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg.

The experienced Danish international has been identified as someone who could help smooth the transition from losing Bruno Guimaraes and Sandro Tonali from their midfield.

Though far from the headline signing Newcastle fans would have been hoping for, the 31-year-old knows the Premier League well and could provide the steadying hand for their two young additions Sean Steur, 18, and Aladji Bamba, 20.

Newcastle United are interested in former Tottenham midfielder Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg

Hojbjerg has 97 caps for Denmark and has been performing consistently well for Marseille. Newcastle had previously tried to sign him in 2022 from Tottenham for £30m.

He joined Marseille permanently last year, after an initial loan, for £17m and worked under Spurs boss Roberto de Zerbi. He has gone on to make 75 appearances and score eight goals for the French side in all competitions.

Newcastle sport director Ross Wilson has been working through an extensive list of names but at least knows that Hojbjerg could hit the ground running and provide Matthias Jaissle with another experienced head in the dressing room.

Newcastle have previously enquired about Lucas Bergvall at Tottenham, Felix Nmecha at Dortmund and Angelo Stiller of Stuttgart as they try to find the right blend for their midfield.

Guimaraes, 28, has been sold for £75m this week and will be confirmed as an Arsenal player over the weekend.

Wilson said: 'We didn't want to sell him. It was a world record fee for a player his age.

'What we had to weigh up was, very respectfully from Bruno with his behaviour towards us, very emotionally as well, effectively told us he wanted to leave and move on.

'That doesn’t mean he can go but it certainly plays a part in what our thinking is when we hit a certain range of number. But there’s no part in saying it was part of our strategy and was in our thinking this summer — it wasn’t.

'But we have got to be flexible and react to things that happen. It might have been in our plan to sign one player but we didn’t get him so we move on to another. We can only be honest about that.'

WITH CRAIG HOPE

United keeping tabs on Hall

Manchester United made a fresh enquiry for Newcastle left back Lewis Hall at the end of last month but were told he is not for sale.

As reported, Hall has been on United's radar this summer as it is clear they need to strengthen that position with Luke Shaw, now 31, in the final year of his contract while youngster Harry Amass has been told he may be best leaving for first team football.

Newcastle want to strengthen in that position themselves and also want a right-back with Tino Livramento likely to move on.

They are among the clubs who have checked on 19-year-old Jorge Salinas at Racing Santander along with Aston Villa. But Newcastle see Salinas as one for the future rather than ready to go now.

Palace sign ex-Arsenal man

Crystal Palace have signed former Arsenal defender Takehiro Tomiyasu on a free transfer.

Daily Mail Sport understands the 27-year-old has signed a one-year contract, with the option to extend it by a further two years.

Tomiyasu, who made 65 appearances for Arsenal from 2021-25, spent last season at Ajax but missed most of the campaign through injury.

The Japanese international will provide depth at centre-back and wing-back for Pierre Sage’s side.

BOBBY MANZI

Eagles swoop for Gozo

Crystal Palace have agreed an £11million deal to sign Real Salt Lake winger Zavier Gozo.

The 19-year-old has been given permission to have a medical.

Real Salt Lake winger Zavier Gozo looks set to join Crystal Palace

Tigers pounce on Norwegian midfielder

Hull have signed midfielder Jens Hjerto-Dahl from Tromso for a fee around £8million.

The 20-year-old has penned a five-year contract until the summer of 2031, becoming the Tigers’ sixth summer signing.

Lukic likes look of Ipswich

Fulham midfielder Sasa Lukic has completed his Ipswich medical ahead of a £9m move. He is expected to sign a four-year deal.

Atletico remain in pole position for Romero

Atletico Madrid remain in talks with Tottenham for Cristian Romero.

Numbers have been discussed between the two clubs, though Atletico have yet to make a formal offer.

Daily Mail Sport reported in July that Atletico had rekindled their long term interest in the Argentina centre back, who also has Inter Milan keen to sign him.

Atletico Madrid remain in talks with Tottenham over Cristian Romero but are yet to table a formal offer

However, the Italians are struggling to meet his personal terms despite offering £34m to Spurs.

Arsenal had enquired to Romero's representatives but that is unlikely with Diego Simeone and Atletico in pole.

Rodri sets sights on Barca

Rodri has informed Real Madrid that he wishes to join Barcelona.

The Spanish champions are now in official contact with Manchester City to try and agree a fee though their initial proposal is understood to be closer to £40million, well below their £68million valuation.

His representatives say out of respect to Madrid who were 'class in their approach', they were informed that the 30-year-old's preference is to link up with Hansi Flick's squad.

Rodri has informed Real Madrid that he wishes to join Barcelona

Wrexham target Ipswich keeper

Wrexham have asked about Ipswich Town's Alex Palmer as an alternative solution to find a new goalkeeper for the Championship season.

The 29-year-old is valued around £3.5million.

Wrexham have also been talking to Sunderland about Anthony Patterson though he is priced around £8m.

Leicester City's Harry Souttar remains a target too though Sheffield United are also in the mix for the Australia centre back.

Wrexham have asked about Ipswich's Alex Palmer as a potential goalkeeping option

Coventry remain in talks over Hamer return

The Blades, meanwhile, are continuing talks with Coventry City over the sale of midfielder Gus Hamer.

The Brazilian is keen to return to Coventry and the chance to play in the Premier League. He has also spoken to manager Frank Lampard.
