World.title: Adaptation of Seita Vuorela's novel 'Karikko' begins filming on Saaremaa
World.content:
The film is based on the acclaimed novel "Karikko" ("The Reef") by Finnish author Seita Vuorela, which won the Nordic Council Children and Young People's Literature Prize in 2013. The screenplay was written by Jytte-Merle Böhrnsen.

Kari is a mysterious adventure film about a sister and brother, Kathi and Mika, who travel with their mother to a former seaside camp for their summer holiday. They soon discover a wild gang of teenagers on the beach who call themselves the Wrecks, as well as a mysterious abandoned hotel. The deeper the children delve into the secrets of the place, the more the boundaries between past and present, memory and oblivion, and the worlds of the living and the dead begin to blur.

The film is directed by Australian-born director Phillip Donnellon, who gained international recognition with his short film "Bird in the Wire," which was selected for the competition program of the Cannes Film Festival in 2001. Kari is his first feature-length fiction film.

Donnellon said he was initially advised against filming on Saaremaa because it was considered too remote as a filming location.

"I come from an even more remote island in Australia myself, so I managed to convince the producers to come and take a look. When we started exploring possible filming locations, I was overjoyed – I immediately realized that Saaremaa hides real treasures. The story unfolds at a very special coastal camp that has to feel both like an adventurous nature park and a place closely connected to the sea. Mändjala Campsite, Panga Cliff and the surrounding beaches were a perfect fit for our film," Donnellon said.

German actress Nora Tschirner plays the mother of Kathi and Mika. The young lead roles are played by Leo Humphreys, Esme Hobson and Lovena Börschmann Ziegler. The Estonian young actors appearing in the film are Derek Leheste, Torm Laos, Karl Jakob Moora, Alen Aiden Mathieson, Hugo Gorski, Mia Mahala Mäe and Aimei Zuo.

Filming in Estonia will continue until September 9.

World.title: Gallery: Tartu welcomes Moby on 'Play' 25th anniversary tour
World.content:
Tartu Song Festival Grounds hosted Moby on Thursday, as the U.S. musician and producer brought his 25th anniversary "Play" tour to Estonia.

Moby's latest tour celebrates the 1999 album that marked his breakthrough, earning critical acclaim and reaching millions of listeners worldwide.

"Play" was later included on Rolling Stone's 500 Greatest Albums of All Time list.

Moby began his career in punk rock before moving into electronic dance music and rave culture.

He has since released 22 studio albums, selling more than 20 million copies worldwide, with hits including "Honey," "Porcelain," "Flower," "Natural Blues," "Bodyrock" and "Why Does My Heart Feel So Bad?"

Throughout his career, he has earned multiple Grammy, Billboard Music Awards, Brit Awards, MTV and NME nominations and wins.

His music has also appeared in films including "The Beach" with Leonardo DiCaprio, the "Bourne" series with Matt Damon and the James Bond film "Tomorrow Never Dies."

Beyond his own recordings, Moby has produced and remixed music for artists including David Bowie, Ozzy Osbourne, The Beastie Boys, Daft Punk and Public Enemy.

World.title: Paide and Flora both lose in UEFA Conference League qualifying first legs
World.content:
Estonia's representatives at the UEFA Conference League suffered defeats home and away on Thursday, as Paide Linnameeskond went down to Rapid Vienna (Austria) and Tallinna FC Flora lost 2-0 away to Inter Club d'Escaldes (Andorra).

The UEFA Conference League is the third tier of European club competition, and Thursday's games were the first leg of round three of qualifying, with a berth in the playoffs awaiting the aggregate winners.

Paide 1, Rapid Vienna 4

Paide Linnameeskond suffered a 4–1 home defeat against Rapid Vienna before 5,500 fans at the A. Le Coq Arena in Tallinn. The hosts kept the score at 1–1 before things began to unravel in the last 10 minutes.

This means they will go to Vienna for the second leg next week with a mountain to climb if they are to meet either Benfica or Hearts in the playoff round.

The 32-time Austrian champions Rapid started the match sharply and were awarded a penalty as early as the third minute, which Hungarian right-back Bendeguz Bolla duly slotted in.

The visitors kept up the pressure, keeping 75 percent of the possession in the first half, though such shots as they had were little threat to Paide's Gambian 'keeper Ebrima Jarju's goal, and some chances even began to emerge for the home side as well.

This manifested with a Paide equalizer in the 41st minute when a low corner made its way into Rapid's penalty area; a touch from striker Abdourahman Badamosi hit the crossbar before it fell to forward Daniel Luts, who fired it into the net from a few meters out.

However, Rapid got back in control of the tempo in the second half. In the 71st minute, Paide committed a poor misplaced pass near their own penalty area, though Jarju saved the resulting close-range effort. Two minutes later, it was Rapid's goalkeeper's turn to keep out a fierce shot at his near post from striker Modou Pa Sohna.

In the final 10 minutes, however, the visitors settled things once and for all with three unanswered goals. In the first of these, Jarju came off his line in time to cut out a through ball, but the ball unfortunately ricocheted to striker Moulaye Haidara, who calmly slotted it home. Just two minutes later, Bolla delivered a low cross from the right into the goalmouth, where winger Petter Dahl turned it into the net, and in the fourth minute of stoppage time, Haidara capped a fine attack to put the finishing touch on the match.

Benfica meanwhile put six past Hearts, while the latter responded with just the one goal, in their first leg of the same qualifying stage.

Tallinna FC FLora players. Source: Ken Mürk/ERR

Flora lose 2–0 away to Andorran champs

Meanwhile reigning Estonian champions FC Flora went down 2–0 away to Andorran league champions Inter Club d'Escaldes in the first leg of their third-round qualifier, for the same competition.

Despite being based in tiny Andorra, the hosts have picked up some notable victories in the Conference League competition in recent years. Three summers ago, they defeated Scottish Premiership club Hibernian at home in the second qualifying round of the Conference League. Then last season, they beat Romanian giants FCSB, and drew with Slovenian powerhouse Olimpija Ljubljana.

AVUI JUGA UN DELS NOSTRES!



UEFA Conference League

➡️ Tercera eliminatòria (anada)

19h

️ Nou Estadi de la FAF

Encamp pic.twitter.com/xapXCvX29D — Federació Andorrana de Futbol (@Fedandfut) August 6, 2026

Inter are reigning Andorran league champions, though they have only one Andorran player in their squad, who came on for the final 10 minutes on Thursday. The overwhelming majority of the squad are Spanish nationals, many of them products of the academies of major clubs. For example, Inter midfielder Juan Camara has appeared for Barcelona in a Champions League match, while Inter Club d'Escaldes 'keeper Javi Diaz has played for La Liga side Sevilla.

The first half of Thursday's match belonged entirely to the hosts: Forward Faysal Chouaib put Inter ahead as early as the fifth minute, with the Andorran champions retaining 75 percent of possession during the first half, registering 13 shots during that time to Flora's two, one of which was on target.

The visitors came out for the second half in much better shape, however, holding more possession and even creating some chances in front of the hosts' goal. One good opportunity fell to national team striker Rauno Sappinen, but he was not ready for the ball inside Inter's penalty area. However, it was Inter who doubled their lead, in the 62nd minute, thanks to a goal from winger Domi Berlanga. The hosts held on to that margin to the final whistle, taking that advantage into the second leg in Estonia next Thursday, August 13.

World.title: Estonian raspberries thrive as new methods help farms weather changes
World.content:
Estonian raspberry growers are reporting a strong season this year as farms turn to new growing methods to protect crops from increasingly unpredictable weather.

Recent years of volatile spring and summer weather have pushed growers to experiment with new ways of cultivating raspberries. This summer, those adaptations combined with favorable weather conditions have helped berry farms achieve a strong harvest.

At Tontoli Berry Farm in Põlva County, raspberries are now grown in outdoor pots instead of directly in the ground.

Owner Kardo Tamm said the plants are also set out later in spring, with early-season raspberry plants initially kept in greenhouse-like tunnels to shield them from spring frosts.

The later planting schedule has helped protect their plants from cold.

"This year's raspberry harvest has been good," Tamm said. "We haven't had heavy rains that damage the berries during harvesting, and the cold this spring didn't do too much damage."

At Joosepi Farm in Ahja, the first tunnel-grown raspberries ripened around Midsummer, while outdoor potted raspberry plants are now reaching peak production.

Owner Kaire Roositalu said their harvest is expected to continue through late August.

"We have a lot of raspberries," she said, calling this year's harvest good. She noted that the outdoor crop is only just getting started.

World.title: Careless waste handling attracts rodents to the city
World.content:
The Põhja‑Tallinn district government is collecting tips about rat and mouse activity through mid‑August to direct pest control efforts to the most affected areas. Experts say careless waste handling encourages rodent spread.

Kadri Karnau, communications specialist at the Tallinn Environment and Public Works Department, said the city does not gather centralized statistics on rodent numbers because they cannot be reliably assessed. Still, residents' observations are welcome because they help identify larger colonies.

Rodent control in the capital is divided by areas of responsibility, meaning homeowners' associations play an important role. "When a colony is discovered, the first step is to speak with the private property owner or the homeowners' association, which is responsible for rodent control. The city and district government can only carry out control on areas they manage," Karnau said.

The Environment and Public Works Department uses rat poison placed in special plastic boxes. Karnau said districts do not conduct large‑scale preventive poisoning because it would pose a danger to pets, birds and people. Control is always targeted and based on specific nesting sites and movement paths.

Ettevõtmise eesmärk on leida üles kõige probleemsemad ja pahategelikud rotid. Autor/allikas: slyfox photography/Unsplash

Joosep Sarapuu, a zoologist at the Estonian Museum of Natural History, said local control will not eliminate rodents from the city. "It is not possible in practice to achieve 100‑percent eradication of rats. When one colony disappears, the area becomes freely accessible to newcomers again," he said.

Rat control is complicated by their biological behavior. They exhibit neophobia, meaning fear of new objects. When a plastic box with poison or a trap appears, rodents need time before they dare to approach it.

A common belief that colonies send their weakest members to test poison is not entirely accurate, Sarapuu said. "Dominant individuals do not check new things because they have established routes and a stable food supply. Lower‑ranking members are forced to look for new feeding sites and movement paths. That is why they are the first to encounter poison and traps," he said.

Joosep Sarapuu. Source: ERR

How can people keep rodents away from their homes? Sarapuu said summer is a good time to check a home's rodent‑proofing because pests try to enter houses when the weather gets cold. "You should find small gaps and openings where rats and mice can get inside and seal them carefully. Second, you must check food waste to make sure it is not easily accessible. In that case, rodents are likely to be fewer or not present at all," he said.

Karnau also said a tidy neighborhood is the best way to keep rodents away. "Trash rooms and waste containers must be kept in good condition and closed to prevent food waste from spreading into the surroundings. It is also wise to avoid feeding birds and squirrels and to keep the areas under bird feeders clean because fallen food attracts rodents," she said.

World.title: Expert: Talk of a direct Russian attack is extremely foolish
World.content:
Claims by anonymous American intelligence sources that a possible limited Russian attack against NATO may happen in the coming years are exaggerated speculation, said security expert Rainer Saks, former secretary general of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (2015-2020) and the Foreign Intellegence Service (2011-2015).

ERR: A U.S. intelligence assessment has been published by The Wall Street Journal, stating that Russian leader Vladimir Putin, whose invasion of Ukraine has stalled, could test NATO in the coming years by attacking one of the alliance's member states. The report mentions both cyberattacks and a limited ground incursion. What should we make of all this?

Rainer Saks: First of all, this is another classic case where anonymous sources have said something, fragments have been written down, but official comments are either unavailable or refused. It is a very broad and diffuse text.

As for these general assessments that Russia "could do something," there is no significant indication behind them that Russia is actually planning to do so. It is a hypothetical assessment that Russia could do this, that or the other. As long as Russia is not planning such actions, publishing assessments like this in the current context actually works very much in Russia's favor. Even the suggested time frame, from this autumn until 2029, is completely absurd.

Russia is certainly not making plans like that.

It is difficult to judge whether this was leaked by the U.S. government or is the initiative of an individual intelligence official. We will not speculate about that, but this is speculation rather than a report based on a concrete intelligence assessment.

The proposed actions — from cyberattacks to a limited military incursion — essentially cover the entire range of scenarios that could theoretically be considered. Therefore, I would not take this at present as a serious warning requiring the rapid implementation of countermeasures.

For example, Russia has been carrying out cyberattacks against NATO member states continuously since at least 2005–2006.

At the same time, NATO countries' responses have so far not been appropriate, because before the invasion of Ukraine, several European countries sought to engage Russia and develop energy cooperation instead. Examples of the kind of situation described in the intelligence report can also be found 15 to 20 years ago, so there is nothing new in it.

At the moment, publishing such a report works more to Russia's advantage, because Russia itself has not directly threatened NATO countries with any military action. Instead, a context is now being created that allows it to manipulate information even more than it has done so far.

In that sense, I think the text published by The Wall Street Journal is extremely foolish.

The article also points to indications that Russia is already testing NATO's response, for example, drones and missiles have fallen on the territory of Romania and Poland. This is presented as one indication that perhaps something is underway.

At the same time, those very countries have themselves said that they do not regard this as deliberate Russian action, but rather as accidental or technical incidents. I cannot say whether the official comments differ drastically from what is actually happening.

This is, of course, a problem because while active warfare is taking place in Ukraine, the possibility of, for example, Ukrainian drones ending up in allied territory or being shot down there is indeed an elevated risk.

There are only two main scenarios under which Russia would begin testing NATO's unity.

The first is that NATO has completely fallen apart internally. Although NATO's unity has suffered in several respects recently, there is no full political unity and there are sharp disagreements between different member states, it cannot be said that there is no unity at all. I would not yet go so far as to claim that NATO's collective defense has therefore been called into question.

The domestic political problems of member states and NATO's internal weakening are, in fact, the most likely scenario that could lead to a military confrontation between Russia and a NATO member state. At the moment, however, that process is clearly not advancing rapidly.

The second theoretical possibility is that if Russia truly decides to attack NATO militarily, it would first have to reorganize its forces. For such an attack — or even a test — to be genuinely supported, Russia would most likely have to carry out a mobilization. To some extent, that is theoretically possible after the State Duma elections, because the forces fighting against Ukraine have been unable to achieve success, and according to the Russian General Staff's calculations, there are too few troops.

In a situation where a full-scale war is still being fought in Ukraine, launching a new war against an even stronger opponent would, in my view, require Russia to declare martial law and carry out full-scale mobilization. That is something without which I do not believe Russia would proceed with very aggressive plans.

The article repeatedly refers to the fact that the Americans are running low on missile stockpiles because of operations in the Middle East and donations to Ukraine. Could it instead be that this article and the intelligence assessment are aimed at a domestic U.S. audience, to remind people of the need to replenish weapons stockpiles quickly?

That may indeed be the case. However, there is one important nuance here: the issue is not that the United States lacks certain types of missiles in its stockpiles, primarily air defense missiles and Tomahawk-type long-range strike weapons, of which too many have been expended against Iran. It is natural for stockpiles to decline during active military operations, but production is reportedly not keeping pace with what is needed. That is an embarrassing situation — what is the point of launching military operations if you cannot simultaneously replenish your stocks?

What is being overlooked, however, is that Russia has exactly the same problem, only even more severe. It also lacks sufficient air defense capabilities, as demonstrated by the success of Ukraine's long-range strikes. For example, this morning yet another large Wildberries warehouse, deep in the Urals some 1,800 kilometers from Ukraine, was set on fire.

Russia is in exactly the same position of weakness. Its entire missile capability is focused on Ukraine, and it is unable to carry out large-scale missile strikes on a daily basis. The war has lasted four years and has significantly exhausted Russia.

Of course, we can talk about hybrid attacks, but the conditions for Russia to launch a military incursion into NATO territory or start a military conflict with NATO are in no way favorable for Russia at present.

Why do you think intelligence assessments claiming that Russia is about to start testing NATO keep being published, when in reality they do not correspond to the facts?

I cannot answer that question. It is probably influenced by many different factors, ranging from incompetence and foolishness to domestic political objectives.

There is, of course, genuine reason to be concerned about the overall situation. There is nothing good about it. A major war is underway, and the governments of Europe and the United States have been unable to bring it to an end. That is indeed a very serious problem. Supporting Ukraine has also not been as successful as it should have been — a great deal has been done, but not enough.

A separate question is why European leaders have been unable to pull themselves together. Four years after the start of the full-scale war, they are still unable to produce enough of the military equipment that is needed. That is a very bad sign. In that sense, it is understandable that many people are seriously concerned about the situation and are trying to warn of possible negative developments.

World.title: Apple officially enters Iraq under new digital services framework
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Apple has legally joined Iraq’s regulated digital market, having met the country’s standards for digital platforms and services, according to the Communications and Media Commission (CMC).

According to the regulator, Apple has been categorized as a trusted digital service provider in Iraq, which includes the App Store, Apple Music, Apple Podcasts, Apple Arcade, and Apple Ads.

The certification means Apple’s digital services may now function under an official Iraqi regulatory framework, having passed the CMC’s technical and legal standards.

Iraqi officials said the decision is anticipated to boost the country’s digital economy and enhance the investment climate for multinational technology firms.

The development also corresponds with a significant step toward Apple’s physical presence in the Iraqi market. Asiacell has reached a direct arrangement with Apple to include iPhones in its retail network across Iraq.

As part of the cooperation, Asiacell will provide real Apple products with valid warranties throughout its network, while retail personnel will undergo Apple-approved training.

The regulatory permission and Asiacell deal represent a substantial change in Apple’s position in Iraq, pushing both digital services and official device distribution further into a market of over 46 million people.

The move is another indication of Iraq’s quickly emerging technology and consumer market, as Baghdad attempts to lure global corporations, legalize digital services, and promote increased investment in the country’s information technology industry.

World.title: Al-Ghodwa deploys Linde warehouse equipment in Baghdad
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Linde Material Handling of Germany has completed a new warehouse technology project in Baghdad with its official Iraqi partner, Al-Ghodwa Group, as modern logistics systems gain traction in Iraq.

The project was completed in early August, and it comprised the installation and commissioning of two Linde Very Narrow Aisle (VNA) trucks built for high-density warehouse operations.

As part of the turnkey project, Al-Ghodwa installed the guiding system, calibrated and tested the equipment, and taught the local operators.

The technology enables firms to store more items in their current warehouse space by running equipment securely in tighter lanes, which increases productivity and reduces space needs.

The project combines Linde’s German warehouse technology with local installation, maintenance, and after-sales services in Iraq.

Linde Material Handling is a subsidiary of Germany’s KION Group, one of the world’s biggest producers of industrial vehicles and a leading supplier of warehouse automation systems.

The Baghdad installation comes as Iraq’s logistics and distribution industry grows, amid investment in manufacturing, retail, transportation, and private-sector growth.

World.title: Saudi renews invitation to Iraq PM as Baghdad, Riyadh seek to repair ties
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Saudi Arabia has extended an invitation to Iraqi Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi to visit Riyadh as the two countries try to regain momentum in ties after a dangerous escalation involving Iran-backed militias operating from Iraqi soil.

Al-Zaidi met with Saudi intelligence head Khalid bin Ali Al-Humaidan in Baghdad on Friday, with the Saudi official conveying a message from the kingdom’s leadership extending the offer and discussing greater security cooperation, according to the Iraqi government.

The meeting is notable since Al-Zaidi canceled a scheduled visit to Saudi Arabia last month in response to US-Saudi airstrikes on Iran-aligned armed groups in Iraq.

These operations followed a series of drone assaults on Saudi Arabia.

Riyadh claimed that Iran-backed militias fired drones from Iraqi territory, attempting to damage oil installations in the Eastern Province and targets near Riyadh, and publicly urged Baghdad to prevent its land from being used as a launchpad for assaults against the country.

Saudi Arabia then launched operations with US troops against Iran-backed militia strongholds in Iraq, increasing pressure on Baghdad to bring armed organizations operating outside of effective official control under its authority.

During Friday’s meeting, Al-Zaidi underlined Iraq’s refusal to allow its land to be used for attacks on Saudi Arabia or any other country, emphasizing Baghdad’s commitment to sovereignty, good neighbor relations, and regional security.

According to the Iraqi statement, the two sides agreed to maintain information sharing and security cooperation, with Baghdad aiming to avoid future assaults that may prompt another military reaction on Iraqi soil.

The outreach coincides with Saudi Arabia’s efforts to deepen regional security relationships.

On Friday, Riyadh, Ankara, and Islamabad signed the Mecca Joint Defense Agreement, which states that any military assault on one of the three nations is considered an attack on all.

Saudi authorities are also apprehensive about additional strikes by Iran-aligned forces.

For Al-Zaidi, the repeated Saudi invitation provides a chance to mend ties with one of Iraq’s most significant Arab neighbors while also displaying Baghdad’s determination to prevent Iran-backed forces from dictating its regional connections.

The implications extend beyond security. Iraq has been pursuing more Saudi and Gulf investment as part of a larger push to diversify its economy, attract foreign money, and enhance trade and infrastructural ties with its Arab neighbors.

As a result, Friday’s meeting constitutes a crucial step in moving Baghdad-Riyadh relations past last month’s dispute. However, continued progress is likely to be strongly dependent on Iraq’s capacity to show that attacks on its neighbors would not be launched from its territory in the future.

World.title: Spain imposes border checks on Italy as migrant showdown grows
World.content:
Madrid – Spain announced on Friday it would introduce temporary border checks on travellers from Italy in response to Rome imposing similar measures after a mass migrant rush into Ceuta.

The checks, which come “amid the persistent irregular migration pressure” facing Italy, will start at midnight on Saturday and last until September 7, Spain’s interior ministry said in a statement.

Hours earlier, Spain threatened Italy with countermeasures if it did not swiftly lift its own border checks, drawing a rebuff from Rome.

The rare spat between the European Union and NATO allies came after tens of thousands of people crossed from Morocco to Spain’s North African territory on July 30-31 in an unprecedented, deadly rush.

The scenes infuriated EU members that back a hard line on irregular immigration, including Italy which imposed a one-month suspension of its visa free-travel Schengen deal with Spain.

The Spanish government slammed the measure Friday as “unfair, contrary to the EU’s interests and discriminatory for the Spanish population”.

Foreign Minister Jose Manuel Albares described it as “a torpedo fired at the hull of European unity.”

“We urge the government of Italy to rectify, put an end to the checks and treat Spaniards like other European citizens,” the government said.

He threatened “proportional measures” in response by Sunday if Italy failed to comply.

– ‘Creating rifts’ –

Within hours, the government of Italy’s far-right Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni said it “had no intention of revising the decision” before August 15, when it said Spanish authorities “expected a new wave of migration” to hit Ceuta.

“Italy does not accept ultimatums or impositions from abroad regarding national security and border control,” Meloni’s office said in a statement.

“Only when there is certainty that there are no security or terrorism risks to Italy, that no new wave is occurring, and that no irregular migrants are heading toward European territory, will the decision be reconsidered,” it read.

Spain’s interior ministry announced the reciprocal measures within hours.

Spanish police have been monitoring online rumours and social media about possible fresh arrivals in Ceuta in mid-August, according to local media. But authorities have not expressly said they expect a repeat of last week’s rush.

Border authorities would in the meantime “do their utmost to ensure maximum ease of movement for Spanish and European citizens” who are not affected by border checks, the Italian statement added.

Italy, which does not share a land border with Spain, introduced border controls at maritime and air entry points for third-country nationals arriving from the Iberian country.

The move announced on July 31 was an “extraordinary measure” intended to “safeguard national security and prevent possible repercussions for our nation”, Meloni said at the time.

She was among EU leaders who called for Spain to be suspended from the visa-free Schengen travel zone after the Ceuta incident, despite such a move being legally impossible.

Italy’s coalition government has sought to stop the tens of thousands of people who land in small boats on the country’s shores each year.

The Spanish government warned against “creating rifts and sterile conflicts driven by internal electoral motives” and said “we trust that pro-European sentiment, common sense and good faith prevail”.

Of the 72,000 people who entered Ceuta, 70,000 have returned to Morocco, according to official Spanish figures.

Spanish authorities said 80 people died in the crossings.

Moroccan rights groups however estimate the figure to be higher. The Moroccan Association for Human Rights (AMDH) and the European Coordination for Human Rights in Morocco on Friday said at least 141 deaths were recorded and that the toll was likely to rise.

Morocco’s interior ministry has said 11 people died on its side of the border, all but one by drowning.

Those who remain in Ceuta — including hundreds of unaccompanied children — face dire living conditions with little access to food, water, and shelter.

World.title: Saudi Arabia, Turkey, Pakistan sign defence pact amid regional war
World.content:
Riyadh – Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan signed a joint defence agreement on Friday amid violence in the region from Houthi attacks and the US-Iran war.

Riyadh is looking to strengthen its security ties against the backdrop of war between the United States and Iran, which has drawn in surrounding nations and disrupted shipping through the Strait of Hormuz and the Red Sea.

The war has emboldened Iran and its Houthi allies in Yemen, both of which have attacked Saudi Arabia, while analysts say Washington is now seen as an increasingly unreliable partner.

In a joint statement published by the official Saudi press agency and Pakistan’s foreign ministry, the three countries announced the signing of the “Mecca Joint Defence Agreement”.

They declared a “shared commitment to further strengthening their collective security and to promoting peace, security and stability in the region and beyond”.

Pakistan’s foreign ministry said the pact meant an attack on any member would be regarded as an attack on all, adding it was “intended to strengthen collective deterrence”.

Ankara nonetheless said later that the agreement was “not aimed at any particular country”, according to a post on X by the presidency’s communications director.

It added that “the agreement is not in contradiction with the commitments of Turkey’s existing international alliances, including those at the heart of NATO,” according to a post on X by the government’s anti-disinformation service.

Riyadh said “the agreement does not represent an effort to establish a military axis or a sectarian bloc”.

“Nor is it linked to any nuclear ambitions or arms race, rather it is focused on building sustainable capabilities,” Deputy Minister for Public Diplomacy Rayed Krimly said on X.

The “does not constitute a threat to the security of any country in the region”, he added.

– ‘Layers of security’ –

Since the onset of the regional war, Saudi Arabia has grown closer to Turkey, Egypt and Pakistan, which have been pushing for mediation and a resolution to the conflict.

Umar Karim, an expert on Saudi foreign policy at the University of Birmingham, England, said the alignment “is clearly oriented towards Iran and meant to address Iran’s new strategic approach which is geared towards dominance of the broader Gulf region”.

The fact that Turkey and Pakistan border Iran means they could “exercise a different kind of leverage” on Tehran, he added.

A source close to the Saudi military and government told AFP before the signing that although the agreement had been under discussion for a long time, “the latest developments in the region expedite it”.

Andreas Krieg of King’s College London said the deal showed a clear desire to diversify alliances beyond the United States.

“Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan are not trying to replace the United States,” he said.

“They are building the capacity to protect their interests when Washington cannot or will not do so.”

Riyadh, in particular, he added, “wants several layers of security rather than one American umbrella”, after the shock of the Iran war.

The deal will support Saudi Arabia’s ambitions to become an organiser of regional security and diversify its defence umbrella, said Krieg. Turkey and Pakistan gain political clout and access to potential Saudi investments, he added.

Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan met Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman in Mecca on Friday, the Turkish presidency said on X, sharing an image of the meeting.

Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and army chief Asim Munir also travelled to the Gulf kingdom for the signing.

– Renewed Houthi attacks –

Saudi Arabia and Pakistan had already announced a mutual defence pact in 2025, a move that drew attention because Pakistan is the Muslim world’s only nuclear-armed state.

The deal also comes as a truce between Riyadh and the Houthi rebels in neighbouring Yemen has broken down. The Houthis have launched attacks on Saudi soil and declared a maritime blockade against Saudi Arabia, which they have attempted to enforce by attacking Saudi tankers.

The Houthis, backed by Iran, have added pressure to Gulf energy exporters — already under strain from Tehran’s blockade of the Strait of Hormuz — by threatening Red Sea shipping.

Saudi Arabia has led a military coalition backing Yemen’s internationally recognised government against the Houthis since 2015.

A truce was agreed four years ago which largely held until hostilities broke out again in recent weeks.

On Thursday, the Houthis killed at least 58 Yemeni government troops in missile and drone attacks, a military source said, in one of the conflict’s deadliest days in years.

World.title: US dollar exchange rate continues to rise in Iraq
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The exchange rate for the US dollar compared to the Iraqi dinar rose on Thursday in the Iraqi capital, Baghdad, and the capital of the Kurdistan region of Iraq, Erbil.

The US dollar exchange rate slightly rose in Baghdad’s al-Kifah and al-Harithiya stock exchanges, reaching 1,523.5 Iraqi dinars compared to 1,520.5 Iraqi dinars on Thursday morning.

The exchange rate in currency exchange shops in Baghdad ranged between 1,530 Iraqi dinars and 1,520 Iraqi dinars, Shafaq News reported.

In Erbil, the US dollar exchange rate also rose, fluctuating between 1,525.5 and 1,525 Iraqi dinars.

The Central Bank of Iraq (CBI) said in February 2023 that it has begun using the new US dollar exchange rate of 1,300 dinars to every US dollar.

The previous official exchange rate was 1,450 dinars to one US dollar, which was being exchanged in the parallel market at a rate of 1,550 dinars.

While the official exchange rate was 1,450 dinars per dollar in January 2023, the US currency was being exchanged at 1,610 dinars during the same month in the parallel market in Iraq. This variation indicated a difference of over 10 percent in the exchange rates.

World.title: Iraq to increase production from Kirkuk oil fields
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Oil Minister Basim Khudair announced on Thursday plans to increase oil production from the Kirkuk oilfields.

The decision intends to capitalize on a recent agreement with Turkey for exporting oil to the port of Ceyhan.

This move also aims to circumvent the closure of the Strait of Hormuz and increase Iraq’s oil exports via ports on the Mediterranean.

The instruction utilizes the recently expanded Kirkuk-Ceyhan pipeline deal, with the goal of increasing exports from 180,000 barrels per day to approximately 750,000 barrels per day.

Khudair stated that increasing production lays the groundwork for boosting export volumes through Turkey to 1.5 million barrels per day.

Turkish Petroleum Corporation (TPAO) has officially partnered with British Petroleum (BP) to bolster cooperation in oil and natural gas projects in Kirkuk oilfields.

In 2025, BP reached a deal with Iraq’s North Oil Company (NOC) to develop oil fields in the northern Iraqi province of Kirkuk, with investments projected to reach $25 billion.

The step is part of the Iraqi government’s attempts to optimize energy sector investments, increase oil output, and minimize gas flaring.

The enhanced output directly addresses the Iraqi government’s growing deficit as a result of continued maritime restrictions in the Strait of Hormuz.

By producing more petroleum from Kirkuk, Baghdad reduces internal shipping expenses from southern fields while increasing supplies to global markets via outlets on the Mediterranean.

World.title: Iraqi Prime Minister orders higher military readiness as security tensions rise
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister and Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces Ali Al-Zaidi has directed all security and military formations to raise their operational readiness and combat preparedness, according to the Security Media Cell.

The directive aims to maintain a high state of preparedness across Iraq’s security forces through intensified training exercises and operational movements designed to strengthen national security and protect public interests.

In a statement, the Security Media Cell said the Commander-in-Chief instructed security and military forces to increase their level of readiness while conducting training exercises and field movements.

The measures are intended to ensure that all security formations remain fully prepared to carry out their assigned duties and respond to potential security developments.

According to the statement, the directive is part of ongoing efforts to maintain continuous operational readiness across Iraq’s armed forces.

The Security Media Cell said the enhanced readiness program is designed to reinforce Iraq’s security framework and improve the capabilities of military and security units.

Officials stated that maintaining high readiness contributes to:

Strengthening national security.

Preserving public stability.

Protecting Iraqi citizens.

Safeguarding public institutions and national interests.

The government has increasingly emphasized preparedness amid evolving regional security challenges.

The announcement comes during a period of elevated security concerns in Iraq following recent regional developments and heightened tensions involving armed groups.

The official statement, however, does not specify any particular threat or military operation linked to the readiness order.

Some media reports and political analysts have suggested the move may be connected to broader security developments or precautionary planning ahead of upcoming government deadlines. These assessments are analytical interpretations and were not included in the official Security Media Cell statement.

The latest directive reflects Baghdad’s continued focus on ensuring the operational effectiveness of Iraq’s security institutions.

By ordering additional training activities and maintaining high alert levels, the government aims to preserve stability while ensuring security forces remain prepared to respond to any developments affecting the country’s security environment.

World.title: No conflict of interest in RDI Fund, says government
World.content:
Since its establishment under an Act of Parliament in 1996, TDB has relied upon independent expert committees rather than individual officials for evaluating technology proposals

NEW DELHI: The government on Friday said the Research, Development and Innovation (RDI) Fund is being implemented through a robust institutional framework with "stringent conflict-of-interest safeguards" in place, highlighting that it is designed "not to exclude domain expertise but to regulate it through clearly defined conflict-of-interest provisions".Rebutting a media report that 15 of the 22 entities that got public funds to boost India's deep-tech ambitions have investment links to seven members of the selection committee, raising questions of conflict of interest and propriety, Technology Development Board (TDB) secretary Rajesh Kumar Pathak said the mere existence of a professional or investment association with an innovation ecosystem entity does not constitute a violation of conflict-of-interest norms."What the framework requires is full disclosure of such interests and complete recusal from the evaluation and decision-making process relating to the proposal concerned... All members had, accordingly, recused themselves, and each decision was taken not by simple majority but by super-majority (two-thirds) of eligible members," said Pathak."Members who declare a conflict of interest neither participate in discussions nor vote on the concerned proposal."Pathak also underlined that TDB has "consistently followed similar conflict-of-interest safeguards for nearly three decades" while supporting indigenous technology development.Since its establishment under an Act of Parliament in 1996, TDB has relied upon independent expert committees rather than individual officials for evaluating technology proposals.The same institutional principles continue to govern project selection under the RDI Fund, reinforcing continuity, credibility and public confidence in the decision-making process, he added.Prof Umesh V Waghmare, secretary in the department of science and technology and TDB chairperson, said the government has followed the conflict-of-interest guidelines and framework diligently and strongly believes that there have been no violations. TDB is one of the agencies selected to grant money under the Centre's Rs 1 lakh crore RDI Fund. It has, so far, approved assistance for 22 projects involving Rs 2,192 crore of financing.

World.title: Eyeing framework to regulate OTT content: I&B min
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The information and broadcasting (I&B) ministry has told a parliamentary committee that it is mulling a comprehensive statutory framework to regulate the airing of programmes on OTT platforms, "which are offensive to moral standards of society", without infringing upon the rights and freedom of individuals.

The department-related standing committee on the ministry of home affairs, in its recommendations in the 259th report tabled in Parliament on Friday, said the proposed comprehensive statutory framework for regulating OTT content must incorporate robust technology-enabled age verification mechanisms, effective parental controls and suitable penalties for non-compliance.

While observing that the existing framework continued to rely largely on self-regulation by OTT platforms, the committee - in its recommendations on the action taken on its 254th report - reiterated that the government examine the feasibility of establishing an independent post-release review panel - comprising experts from fields like child development, education, law, social sciences and civil society - to review flagged OTT content and lay down appropriate corrective measures.

The panel had, in its 254th report, said, "OTT platforms have emerged as a primary source of entertainment in India, with a reach that surpasses traditional cinema, including a substantial audience of minors." The committee pointed out that unlike films, which require mandatory pre-certification under the Cinematograph Act, OTT content operates under a self-classification system with post-release grievance redressal as per the IT (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Rules, 2021.





The panel said that although the aforesaid rules require age ratings, parental controls and a grievance mechanism, the lack of pre-release checks and weak age verification still leaves minors exposed to harmful content. Accordingly, it recommended that the government consider establishing a recognised panel of experts who will monitor new OTT releases.

World.title: Share data on river waters, India tells China
World.content:
NEW DELHI: In another round of diplomatic engagement on the border issue, India and China had âfrank discussionsâ and reviewed the situation along the line of actual control (LAC), with the former underlining that maintaining peace and tranquillity in the border areas is essential for the development of bilateral relations.

The Indian side also reiterated the need for early convening of the next meeting of the Expert Level Mechanism on trans-border rivers, which was established in 2006, and emphasised the importance of sharing technical details on upstream projects.

Following the recent announcement of a mega dam project by China, India has been raising the need for transparency and consultation with downstream countries on such upstream activities.

According to the Indian govt, as a lower riparian state with established user rights to the waters of trans-border rivers, India routinely conveys its views and concerns to the Chinese authorities, and has urged them to ensure that the interests of downstream states are not harmed by activities in upstream areas. India has repeatedly stressed resumption of the provision of hydrological data and other cooperation pertaining to trans-border rivers.





The 36th meeting of the Working Mechanism for Consultation & Coordination on India-China Border Affairs (WMCC) on Thursday saw both sides agreeing to continue using existing diplomatic and military channels, including the WMCC, local commander-level meetings and other agreed mechanisms, to resolve outstanding issues and avoid misunderstanding and miscalculation along the LAC.

World.title: Delhi high court stays food regulator's ban on certain Dabur products
World.content:
NEW DELHI:

on Friday stayed an

directive prohibiting Dabur India from selling food products such as honey, cow ghee and edible oils with "100%" claims.

Justice Amit Mahajan noted that Dabur was selling the products for decades and had shown a prima facie case for relief at this stage, as the FSSAI issued the order without granting a hearing to the company.

The HC issued notice to FSSAI on Dabur's petition challenging the prohibition and asked it to file its reply before the next date, while listing the matter for hearing on Aug 24.

Dabur argued that the FSSAI order was in violation of principles of natural justice. It also submitted that the expression "100%" is used by many players.

World.title: ‘Little hope of tracing 2 missing sailors’, Centre informs Supreme Court
World.content:
Solicitor general (SG) Tushar Mehta told the bench that despite intense search and rescue operations, the missing Indian seafarers â Deepak Kumar Gupta and Ram Chandra Dubey â could not be located

NEW DELHI: The government informed the Supreme Court on Friday that there is very little hope of locating two Indian seafarers who are missing since the drone attack on Palau-flagged merchant ship M V AGN Ragnar on July 25 while it was departing Ukrainian waters.Filing a combined action-taken report by MEA and the Directorate General of Maritime Administration, solicitor general (SG) Tushar Mehta told the bench that despite intense search and rescue operations, the missing Indian seafarers â Deepak Kumar Gupta and Ram Chandra Dubey â could not be located.The Supreme Court told Mehta to facilitate the familiesâ availing maritime insurance payments.

World.title: Air India salary hikes salaries of pilots by up to 15%
World.content:
Air India is restoring international flights that were slashed post the West Asia crisis and will return to Jan-Feb levels next month

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Air India on Friday hiked pilot salaries by 8% to 15%, with commanders getting the biggest hikes and increases tapering by rank. Going ahead, first officers or co-pilots will get command upgrades in AI Express, which has single-aisle aircraft, then move to AI, which has wide-body aircraft with higher pay, to build progression within the group. Air India has tried to make Air India Express more attractive through better pay and to address shortages on the B737 fleet.Air India pilots have for years been facing a 40-hour guaranteed pay â meaning they get minimum pay for these hours irrespective of actual flying, while flying more means more pay â while IndiGo has fixed pay for 70 hours. Under the revised framework, Air India will continue to provide guaranteed pay for 40 flying hours but has enhanced flying allowance rates. Rates beyond 40 hours have been increased, aligning compensation with industry benchmarks while rewarding productivity.Air India is restoring international flights that were slashed post the West Asia crisis and will return to Jan-Feb levels next month. Pakistan airspace closure means longer routes, higher flying time and greater pilot requirements.A senior commander flying 55 hours a month will get Rs 8.3 lakh, up from Rs 7.5 lakh, while a first officer will get Rs 3.3 lakh, up from just over Rs 3 lakh.Privilege leave has been reduced from 30 to 24 days, though weekly offs will not be counted as leave.Since Tata Group took over Air India and Air India Express in Jan 2022, it has grown from around 100 to 300 aircraft. Under the new framework, Air India Express will serve as the âprimary pathwayâ for command upgrades. They can then progress to Air India for wide-body flying. A fleet allowance is being offered to pilots supporting the B737 fleet in Air India Express.

World.title: NCAER: Bihar booze ban hasn't worked; lift it, fund development work
World.content:
NEW DELHI: A new paper by NCAER has proposed lifting prohibition in Bihar to generate resources for financing development and capital expenditure. It argued prohibition has not reduced crime against women and legal drinking has shifted to the consumption of illegal alcohol and drugs.

The paper by a team of economists led by Ratna Sahay said an end to prohibition can help the state increase its tax revenue by 14-15% while reducing expenditure on enforcement. It also argued for more central transfers to states to help meet flood-control activities.

"Overall, available evidence doesn't indicate a broad-based reduction in crimes against women following prohibition. At the same time, the prohibition regime has been accompanied by concerns regarding expansion of illicit liquor trade, increased enforcement challenges and corruption, and the growing use of alternative intoxicants, including illicit drugs," the paper said, while noting a significant rise in illegal liquor trade.

Presented at India Policy Forum on Friday.

After returning to office on the promise of prohibition, Nitish Kumar had imposed a ban on consumption and sale of liquor in one of the most stringent regimes in the country.

While the paper credits Kumar's tenure as CM for restoring law and order and getting Bihar back on the development path, it said the state still lags several other states in revenue mobilisation and depends on transfers from the Centre.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines





The paper identified six priority areas for the state: gaps in education, gaps in health, gaps in governance and law and order, recurring floods and disasters, the missing private sector, and gender discrimination and violence. To achieve its goals, it suggested higher capex, lower subsidies, raising resources and getting more resources from the Centre.

It noted that Bihar's debt burden at 39% of state GDP is higher than both high- and low-income groups, with the exception of Punjab (47%) and Bengal, which is similar. "Raising state revenues is insufficient to finance the reforms, given the state's limited taxing capacity. Additional transfers from the Centre are needed, depending on the reform," the paper said.

World.title: Supreme Court shunts out two coal scam judges on unusual Delhi high court request

On Friday, Delhi HC issued the consequential transfer and posting orders for judges Sunena Sharma and Dheeraj Mor

NEW DELHI: Barely six months after appointing a sessions judge to exclusively hear coal scam cases in Delhi, Supreme Court has replaced her, acting on an unusual request from the Delhi high court, which said she and another special CBI judge were âbetter suited for certain other responsibilitiesâ.A bench of Chief Justice Suryakant and Justices Joymala Bagchi and V Mohana, in an order, recorded that Delhi high court had sought the transfer of special judges Sunena Sharma and Dheeraj Mor so they could be assigned other responsibilities.Sharma had assumed charge in January after SC approved Delhi HCâs request to relieve then incumbent Sanjay Bansal, who had presided over the special coal scam court for nearly four-and-a-half years. Mor was appointed special judge in April 2025. The latest request came with Sharma barely six months into her tenure and Mor having completed just over a year in the post.SC noted that it had received a letter from the registrar general of Delhi HC stating that Sharma and Mor were âbetter suited for certain other responsibilitiesâ. The HC also described both judicial officers as âof outstanding meritâ and said it wished to utilise their services elsewhere.Accepting the request, the top court permitted Delhi high court to transfer Sharma and Mor from the posts of special judges hearing CBI coal scam cases. It also approved the appointment of Virender Kumar Kharta, earlier special judge of the NDPS court at Saket, and Ajay Garg, previously an additional sessions judge at a fast-track court in Tis Hazari, as their replacements. Kharta will succeed Sharma, while Garg will take over from Mor.On Friday, Delhi HC issued the consequential transfer and posting orders. Interestingly, neither Sharma nor Mor has been assigned a fresh judicial posting. According to the notification, both have been attached to the office of the principal district and sessions judge (CBI).The high court directed both officers to notify all matters in which judgments or orders had been reserved before relinquishing charge and pronounce them on the scheduled date or, at the latest, within two to three weeks despite the transfer. The dates fixed for pronouncement must also be reflected in the cause lists of both the previous and new courts, as well as on the courtâs website.Last year, 29 CBI corruption cases were pending before two special coal scam courts, while more than 27 had already been disposed of.

World.title: Gender integration in India’s uniformed services: The Coast Guard catches up
World.content:
The Union Government’s decision to introduce permanent career opportunities and retirement benefits for women officers in the Indian Coast Guard (ICG) marks another significant milestone in India’s journey towards gender parity in the uniformed services. The reforms, approved by Defence Minister Rajnath Singh, not only address a long-standing demand of women Coast Guard officers but also bring the maritime force closer to the standards already established in the Indian Army, Indian Navy and Indian Air Force (IAF).

The policy change comes nearly two years after the Supreme Court questioned the Ministry of Defence and the Coast Guard over the continued denial of Permanent Commission to women officers despite similar reforms having been implemented in the three armed services following landmark judicial interventions.

While the Army, Navy, and Air Force have each travelled different paths towards integrating women into mainstream military roles, the Coast Guard has until now lagged behind in providing long-term career progression. The latest reforms seek to bridge that gap.

What has changed in the Coast Guard?

The new policy introduces two major reforms for women officers serving under the Short Service Appointment (SSA) scheme.

First, women officers will now be eligible for Permanent Absorption in the General Duty (GD) cadre, allowing them to pursue a full career in the service rather than leaving after completing their short-service tenure. Earlier, women could serve only for a limited period under the SSA scheme, while many male officers had the option of permanent appointments.

Second, all branches of the ICG have now been opened to women officers, enabling them to perform all duties on a par with their male counterparts. Women officers will now also be entitled to pension and retirement benefits on a par with their male counterparts.

These changes are expected to improve the retention of trained personnel, provide greater financial security and encourage more women to consider the Coast Guard as a long-term career.

The Indian Coast Guard has inducted women officers for more than three decades, but their career progression remained restricted compared with that of the armed forces.

Women officers have served in operational support, logistics, law, education, administration and selected maritime operational roles.

However, the absence of Permanent Commission created uncertainty regarding promotions, leadership opportunities and retirement security.

The reforms also align with the government’s broader effort to expand women’s participation across India’s defence establishment and recognise merit over gender in determining career opportunities.

Among the three armed services, the Indian Army has witnessed the most significant legal transformation on gender equality.

For decades, women officers were inducted only through the Short Service Commission (SSC) and largely confined to support arms such as Signals, Engineers, Army Air Defence, Army Service Corps, Intelligence Corps, Judge Advocate General and Ordnance.

The turning point came in 2020 when the Supreme Court directed the Government to grant Permanent Commission to eligible women SSC officers, ruling that gender-based discrimination in career progression was unconstitutional.

Today, women officers are eligible for Permanent Commission in 12 Arms and Services, besides the Army Medical Corps, Army Dental Corps and Military Nursing Service. They are also being promoted to the rank of Colonel (Select Grade), appointed to command units and granted career waivers where required to ensure parity with male officers.

Another landmark reform followed in 2021 when women were allowed entry into the National Defence Academy (NDA), enabling them to undergo the same pre-commission training as male cadets.

However, regular induction into combat arms such as Infantry, Armoured Corps and Mechanised Infantry remains unavailable, making the Army’s transition towards complete gender integration a gradual process.

The Indian Navy has steadily broadened operational opportunities for women over the past decade.

Initially restricted to education, logistics and law branches, women officers are now eligible for Permanent Commission in several streams, including logistics, education, naval architecture, observer and air traffic control.

Perhaps the most visible change has been the induction of women on board frontline warships, something considered impractical until a few years ago because of accommodation constraints. Today, women officers routinely serve at sea, while the Navy continues modifying ships and shore establishments to support larger numbers of women personnel.

The Navy has also opened all branches and specialisations except submarines to women officers and Agniveers, becoming the first service to induct women under the Agnipath scheme across nearly all operational streams.

Women now serve as naval pilots, Naval Air Operations officers and operators of Remotely Piloted Aircraft (RPA). From January 2024, women cadets also became eligible for induction through the prestigious 10+2 B.Tech. entry scheme at the Indian Naval Academy.

The Indian Air Force remains the most gender-integrated among India’s military services.

Women first entered the IAF as officers during the 1990s under the Short Service Commission. In 2015, the Government approved the induction of women fighter pilots on an experimental basis. The success of that initiative led to its formalisation as a permanent scheme in 2022.

Today, women fly frontline fighter aircraft such as the Su-30MKI and Rafale alongside transport aircraft and helicopters. They serve across engineering, logistics, administration, meteorology, air defence and technical branches, with career progression broadly comparable to that of men.

The IAF has also institutionalised the induction of women through the NDA, earmarking vacancies in flying, technical and non-technical branches. Since December 2023, women have also joined the force as Agniveer Vayu personnel, further expanding gender representation at the airmen level.

Among all three services, the Air Force offers the widest operational integration and is widely regarded as the benchmark for gender inclusion.

India’s armed forces have undergone a remarkable transformation over the past decade in women’s participation. Enhanced recruitment through the NDA, Permanent Commission, command appointments, operational deployments and expanded career opportunities have increased the number of women officers across the services to around 11,000.

Yet, gender integration remains a work in progress. Infrastructure, accommodation, training practices, career planning and operational policies continue to evolve as more women enter military service.

The Army still retains restrictions in combat arms. The Navy is steadily expanding sea-going appointments, while the Air Force has already achieved extensive operational integration.

For the Coast Guard, the latest reforms represent a decisive shift. By granting Permanent Absorption and retirement benefits to women officers, the force has taken an important step towards ensuring equal career progression and long-term service opportunities.

World.title: Remove posts with derogatory content ‘targeting constitutional heads’: Delhi Police write to X
World.content:
The Delhi Police on Wednesday (July 29, 2026) wrote to X in connection with a complaint alleging that “derogatory, malicious and defamatory content targeting constitutional heads” is being circulated on the social media platform.

The Police have asked the platform to delete or remove the alleged post or video from the platform immediately and provide the complete registrant details including full name, address, contact details and email ID of the said X account ID holder.

This is as per routine communication to the platforms for takedown of posts, said Vinit Kumar, DCP, IFSO (Special Cell). “Nothing related to the protests,” he added, referring to the Cockroach Janta Party-led (CJP) protests in the national capital.

He further said that no FIR related to such posts have been registered in the last month.

This comes as the Delhi Police is in the process of sending takedown notices to Instagram, in an attempt to remove several reels and posts that emerged during the youth protests at Jantar Mantar and elsewhere, officials said.

Without specifying the time frame or the nature of the content, the officer admitted that a large number of such posts had recently been flagged and taken down.

Law enforcement agencies typically send takedown notices under Section 79(3)(b) of the Information Technology Act that notify platforms of specified content that is illegal, however without a legally binding takedown requirement.

World.title: Trainee IPS officer arrested in sexual harassment case
World.content:
The Hyderabad City Police’s Women’s Safety Wing arrested trainee IPS officer Uday Krishna Reddy late on Tuesday (July 28, 2026) in connection with a sexual harassment case filed based on a complaint by a fellow probationary officer at the Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel National Police Academy (SVPNPA).

The case was initially registered at the Attapur police station before being transferred to the Women’s Safety Wing’s She Teams for investigation.

An officer involved in the investigation said that the accused had initially evaded the arrest and investigation by switching off his mobile phones and resisted the arrest during apprehension. Following his arrest, he was shifted to Osmania General Hospital for a medical examination and is expected to be produced before a court in Rajendranagar.

The arrest comes days after reports that Uday Krishna Reddy had allegedly attempted to end life and was admitted to a private hospital in S.R. Nagar, where he underwent treatment.

The case stems from a complaint filed by a 30-year-old married trainee IPS officer from Karnataka, who alleged that Uday Krishna Reddy repeatedly sexually harassed and assaulted her.

Based on the complaint, the Attapur Police registered a case under various provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita and the Information Technology Act. Further investigation is under way.

Meanwhile, an internal inquiry committee at the National Police Academy reportedly examined CCTV footage and other evidence before concluding that the allegations had merit. The academy subsequently placed Uday Krishna Reddy under suspension pending further proceedings.

World.title: Govt had told HC to reject petition on Waqf Board reconstitution, says CM Satheesan; P.Rajeeve contests claim
World.content:
Rejecting allegations that the United Democratic Front (UDF) had told the High Court that it will appoint non-Muslims in the Waqf Board as per the Union government’s Unified Waqf Management, Empowerment, Efficiency and Development (UMEED) Act, or the Waqf (Amendment) Act, 2025, Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan said that the government had asked the court to reject the petition.

The Chief Minister’s comments on Wednesday came in the wake of the Communist Party of India (Marxist) [CPI(M)] State Secretariat on Tuesday flagging growing resentment against the Indian Union Muslim League (IUML) from within the minority community for “endorsing” the Waqf (Amendment) Act, 2025. Addressing a press conference after the Cabinet meeting on Wednesday, he said that the Waqf Board appointed by the previous Left Democratic Front had also told the Supreme Court that the HC refused to reject the petition despite the State government’s demand.

“What is the need for a controversy when the government has made its stand clear? The previous Waqf Board’s term ended in December 2024. However, it was not reconstituted until February 2026, after the Union government brought in the amendments. If the new Board was formed as soon as the term ended, it would have remained so even if the new amendments had come into force,” he said.

However, Communist Party of India (Marxist) leader and former Law Minister P. Rajeeve accused the CM of misleading the public, even as the State government’s stand in the HC and the SC are available in the public domain. Addressing a press conference, he reiterated that the government said in the HC on July 14, 2026 through the special government pleader that it “is prepared to reconstitute the Board strictly in compliance with the mandate of the section 14 of the UMEED Act”, which means the inclusion of two non-Muslims.

“When the government has agreed to carry out the plea completely, what use is its claim that it asked the court to reject the petition? Kerala and Tamil Nadu had kept the two positions vacant until the SC hears the case related to the amendments. The BJP government in Madhya Pradesh has filled the position with RSS-linked people. Tamil Nadu has not changed its position, although there has been a change in government. But the UDF government in Kerala has taken a stand which deceives the Muslim community,” said Mr. Rajeeve.

He also rejected the CM’s allegation that the LDF government had wilfully delayed the reconstitution of the Waqf Board by citing similar precedents in the past, including in 2013 when the UDF was in power. Though the term of the Waqf Board ended in October 2013, it was reconstituted only a year later, with an administrator running the Board during the intervening period.

World.title: Human head found on cricket ground in Bengaluru
World.content:
B

A security guard discovered a human head on a cricket ground near Varthur early on July 29 morning, and alerted the police control room in Bengaluru.

While Varthur police were investigating, officers from the Baiyappanahalli Railway Police, who had registered an unnatural death (UDR) case after finding a headless body on a railway track about 300 metres away, arrived at the ground in search of the missing head.

Preliminary investigation suggests that the victim was struck by a train on July 28 night, and his head was severed by the impact. Police suspect that a pack of stray dogs might have carried the severed head from the railway track to the nearby cricket ground.

The deceased has been identified as Vishwanath (25), a native of Chittoor in Andhra Pradesh, who was working in a private firm in Bengaluru.

The Baiyappanahalli Railway Police have informed the victim’s family, and are trying to establish the exact circumstances leading to the incident.

World.title: Tamil Nadu CM Vijay hands over appointment orders to 126 TNPSC recruits
World.content:
Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay on Wednesday (July 29, 2026) handed over appointment orders to 78 newly recruited Group I officers and 48 newly recruited personnel of the Tamil Nadu Pollution Control Board (TNPCB) selected by the Tamil Nadu Public Service Commission (TNPSC), at the Secretariat in Chennai.

The Group I recruits include 28 Deputy Collectors, seven Deputy Superintendents of Police, 19 Assistant Commissioners (Commercial Taxes), 15 Assistant Directors (Rural Development), three District Employment Officers, and six Assistant Commissioners (Labour).

The TNPCB recruits include 40 Assistant Engineers, six Environmental Scientists, and two Grade II Librarians. Minister for Human Resources Management D. Sarathkumar, Minister for Environment and Climate Change V.K. Rajeev, and Chief Secretary M. Saikumar were among those present.

World.title: Allahabad HC dismisses petition of Mohammad Ali Jauhar Trust against demolition notice
World.content:
The Allahabad High Court on Wednesday (July 29, 2026) dismissed a petition filed by Mohammad Ali Jauhar Trust at Rampur on the notices for demolition of its university buildings, noting that an interim stay has been ordered.

When the matter was taken up before the court, it was informed on behalf of the petitioner that in an appeal filed before the Commissioner, Moradabad, the appellate authority had passed an interim order staying the demolition of university buildings.

Taking note of the interim order, the bench comprising Justices Mahesh Chandra Tripathi and Kunal Ravi Singh dismissed the petition, saying it need not intervene at this stage.

The Moradabad Divisional Commissioner's court had on Monday (July 27, 2026) granted interim relief to the university, founded by Samajwadi Party leader Azam Khan, staying the proposed demolition of 38 buildings on its campus until the final hearing in the case.

On July 15, the Rampur Development Authority (RDA) directed the university administration to demolish 38 of its 40 buildings within 15 days, alleging that they had been constructed without approved building maps. Students and others have been holding a sit-in protest against the order.

The demolition order was issued under Section 27(1) of the Uttar Pradesh Urban Planning and Development Act, 1973. The deadline expires on July 30.

Students of the university have "temporarily" halted their protest against the district authority's order following an interim stay.

The divisional commissioner will now hear the case on August 3.

World.title: Mumbai crime branch arrests 12 international gang members in ₹500 crore cyber fraud case
World.content:
The Mumbai police on Thursday (August 6, 2026) arrested 12 men in connection with a cybercrime operation that allegedly processed transactions of ₹500 crore in the past 6-8 months from Goa, with links to an international syndicate operating from Dubai.

The Mumbai police crime branch said that it has found that the bank accounts were allegedly being opened in Mumbai, and the related banking material was physically being sent to Goa by bus, allegedly using these accounts to process deposits, withdrawals and various account-to-account transfers. The accused were operating out of a rented two-storey villa in Goa, ‘Case De Nikole Villa’, near Calangute beach, the police said.

According to Raj Tilak Roshan, DCP Detection, the men, between the ages of 20 and 25, were mostly recruited from Ahmedabad or Rajkot in Gujarat. They were given 10 to 15 days of training before being placed in the villa.

Police said they allegedly used websites like ‘100 Panel’ and ‘Rudra’ to process funds linked to online gaming and cyber fraud (example: Digital Arrest Scams, etc.). “The transactions were made through user accounts on their laptops and mobile phones for cash withdrawals and deposits, routing the money into bank accounts under their control,” Mr. Roshan said.

Police also found that they allegedly maintained a ledger of all their transactions. They were also receiving a monthly salary of ₹30,000 and an additional 3% commission, the police said.

15 laptops, 128 ATM cards, 89 mobile phones, 76 SIM cards, 22 chequebooks, 77 passbooks, 6 routers, 3 keyboards, and 2 mice were recovered.

Between ₹15 crore and ₹100 crore has allegedly either been frozen or is continuing to be frozen, the police added. Some of the bank accounts that were seized had 83 complaints of cyber fraud from various parts of the country on the Cyber Control Room helpline no. 1930.

Earlier, the case was registered and was being investigated by Pydhonie Police Station. They were investigating the accused arrested in the crime regarding upper-level links.

The police will continue to investigate the sources of the accounts, where the laptops are from, etc.

The accused have been produced before a local Court and have been remanded to police custody till August 11, 2026.

World.title: Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, Turkiye sign tripartite defence agreement in Makkah
World.content:
Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye on Friday signed a joint defence pact in Makkah that empowers member states to treat an attack against one of them as an attack against all of them.

The Makkah Joint Defence Agreement, which seeks to strengthen the collective security of the three states, was signed by Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, Saudi Crown Prince and PM Mohammad bin Salman, and Türkiye’s President Recep Tayyip Erdogan at the “Makkah Al-Mukarramah Summit for Joint Defence” held at Al-Safa Palace.

The three countries announced the signing of the agreement in a joint statement published by the Foreign Office (FO) and Saudi Arabia’s official SPA press agency.

The statement said the pact reflected the three countries’ “shared commitment to further strengthening their collective security and to promoting peace, security, and stability in the region and beyond, in pursuit of a secure and prosperous future”.

“The agreement is intended to strengthen collective deterrence against any act of aggression, and stipulates that any armed attack against any one of the three states shall be regarded as an attack against them all.”

It also “provides for the enhancement of all aspects of defence cooperation” among the three countries, the statement added.

The agreement is “guided by the longstanding historical ties among the three states, based on the enduring bonds of brotherhood and Islamic solidarity that unite them, and building upon their shared strategic interests and longstanding defence cooperation”.

During the Makkah Al-Mukarramah Summit for Joint Defence, the “distinguished relations” between the three countries were reviewed, “along with a number of issues of mutual interest”, the statement noted.

Chief of Defence Forces (CDF) and Chief of the Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir, Deputy PM and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar, and Defence Minister Khawaja Asif were also present at the signing ceremony.

The defence and foreign ministers of Saudi Arabia and Turkiye were in attendance as well, pictures showed.

Sealing the agreement in Makkah, the holiest site in Islam, adds symbolic heft to a pact that builds on longstanding bilateral military ties among the three countries.

The agreement ties together Pakistan, the only nuclear-armed Muslim country; Saudi Arabia, the home to Islam’s holiest sites and one of the world’s top oil exporters; and Turkiye, Nato’s second-largest military.

‘Shield of peace’

Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif described the signing of the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement as a “historic pact”, saying the three countries were united by faith, friendship and a shared commitment to peace and security.

In a post on X, the prime minister said he was honoured to sign the agreement alongside the Saudi crown prince and the Turkish president.

He said the pact would serve as a “shield of peace” for generations and expressed hope that it would bring prosperity to the three countries and the wider Muslim world. Shehbaz also appreciated Field Marshal Asim Munir’s efforts and dedication towards the agreement.

‘Historic day for Pakistan’

Information Minister Attaullah Tarar, while talking to a private TV channel, described the signing of the joint defence agreement between the three states as a “historic day” for Pakistan, saying the pact reflected growing recognition of the country’s defence capabilities and strengthened ties among the three nations.

Speaking about the agreement, Tarar said the defence cooperation framework would take relations between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye to a new level.
